We set out from Omaha NE approx. 6am to arrive in Kona HI on Feb. 5th at approx 2.30pm. We had connecting flights in Denver and LAX. We sat on the runway in Omaha for 1.5 hrs with maintenance issues and paperwork past our connecting flight departure time out of Denver. At Denver they shuffled us back and forth between customer service and the boarding gate finally they ended up booking us on a flight to Oahu then Hawaiian Airlines to Kona. When we arrived in Oahu they had no record of us saying United did not have us booked to Kona. After waiting for everyone to board they were able to get us on. We arrived in Kona approx. 6.5 hrs after we expected to missing a 1/2 a day of our vacation time any activities we had booked and no luggage! Our luggage arrived about 11pm at night. Our return flight was not any better. We arrived at the airport early and was told they had a flight leaving shortly and room on it. With our Kona bound experience we thought it may be a good idea to have more time. Before we boarded they had hydraulic problems and the flight was delayed. We were told our tickets were gone for our originally booked flight. So we waited and for once we made it in time for our connecting flight to Denver until we boarded the plane and the starter went out on the plane they brought it back in fixed it but not before we missed our connecting flight from Denver to Omaha. By now we were wondering if this was normal for United? At Denver again we were shuffled around until they finally found a flight into Omaha for us. Our flight experience with United was well below satisfactory levels. The maintenance issues should be a concern for United. I wonder what their Preventative Maintenance plan looks like if they have one at all and or if they should reconsider their Union as paperwork should not take that long. Not sure we will ever Fly United again. On the positive side we made it there and back!

This round-trip flight was my first experience with flying Spirit Airlines. The initial price was significantly less than comparable round-trip flights. However the consumer should be aware that it is virtually impossible to travel Spirit Air without additional costs unless you can travel with just a backpack or other small carry-on item that will fit under the seat in front of you. Any additional baggage whether stowed or carry-on is charged. There is no complimentary food or beverage service and there is a fee to select your seat. After selecting my seat and paying for two bags (charged for each bag each way) my cost savings over other airlines was insignificant. In addition the in-flight service from the flight attendants was mediocre at best and the seat space was very cramped. The worst part about the experience however was the delays on both the outbound and return flights. My outbound flight was delayed nearly 3 hours and my return flight delayed 45 minutes. In neither case was the delay related to the weather air traffic control or anything related to the airport. In the first case the explanation given for the delay had to do with the aircraft being delayed for previous flights thus arriving late for my flight. On the return flight takeoff was delayed due to one of the flight attendants scheduled for my flight arriving late to the airport on another Spirit flight. The one gentleman in my row of seats on the return flight said how his outbound Spirit flight was also delayed. The other person in our row said when she booked her flight through a travel web site that she received a warning prior to confirming her purchase stating that 60% of Spirit flights are delayed. I can respect an airline for being "no frills" with the goal of keeping their costs low. However there is a difference between "no frills" and poor business practice. The delays appear to be the result of nothing other than airline inefficiency and the apparent consistency of delayed flights is inexcusable. To me that is not "no frills" but evidence of a business being poorly run. An airline can also be "no frills" but still provide friendly polite in-flight service. I'm not even talking here about the fact that they charge for all in-flight food and beverages but rather the general lack of friendliness and courteousness from the flight staff. I'm grateful to have been able to have a direct flight to my destination via Spirit and to have arrived to and from my destination safely. Beyond that my experience with the airline was mostly negative and I would not recommend Spirit Air unless it is your only option. If you do choose to fly Spirit beware of the specific costs travel light and plan for delays.

Unforgettable experience flying with Emirates from Singapore to Rome via Dubai. I was booked on flight EK433, with scheduled departure on Friday at 9.35am but was notified last minute via text message at 4.23am that I had been put on EK353 departing at 10.10am instead. To make things worse, that flight was delayed for another 1 hour 10 minutes. I didn’t know if I was traveling with Emirates or a budget airline that cancels flights on a whim. By the time I arrived in Dubai, my original 2 hour connection time had become less than 40 minutes. Ground staff in Dubai did not offer any form of assistance in making my connecting flight. I made it to the departure gate 5 minutes before closing time only to be told I had been offloaded from the plane. At no stage was I notified that I would be bumped from my connecting flight because of shorter than “minimum connection time” thanks to Emirates’ brilliant incompetence in punctuality. After some argument with the ground staff at the gate, I managed to get onto the flight with the supervisor granting me an act of grace, when it’s Emirates which had sinned. But his grace did not extend to my checked in baggage however, which will only arrive with the next flight. Arrangement to make delivery of my delayed baggage was made immediately after clearing immigration on arrival in Rome FCO airport Friday at 6.40pm, when I was assured my luggage would arrive following day. I even received an email saying my bag will arrive in Rome at about 12.40pm on Saturday. Little did I know I would be slapped in my face with Emirates’ commitment to punctuality again. When I haven’t received my bag at 5pm, I rang the baggage office, and was advised it had just cleared customs and would be delivered in the evening. 6 hours later I was still waiting, and followed up with another less than pleasant phone call. Upon which, the only solution they could offer is the contact number of the local baggage delivery agent. No, of course their gilded fingers can’t possibly dial the number to follow up on a customer’s delayed baggage. I finally received my bag on Sunday at 12.15am. Hooray for a change of clothes finally. No one from Emirates throughout this ordeal acknowledged their fault nor offered compensation for me to get a change of clothes and toiletries. Hello Tomorrow? More like Hello Never.

Don’t pay for the “change flight” option without reading the fine print very carefully. The flexibility is only valid for 4 months, is limited to a single change, and any additional changes incur extra fees. This information is not clearly disclosed elsewhere during purchase. On top of that, the fare difference charged for changes is almost as high as the cost of buying a new ticket, which defeats the purpose of paying for flexibility in the first place. Overall, the carrier feels disingenuous when it comes to hidden costs and lack of transparency. The experience left me feeling cheated, and it comes across as unprofessional and sleazy.

I was traveling Mumbai to Delhi and Delhi to Mumbai, but the AC's of Indigo was not at all working, we and other passengers were repeatedly saying that the AC's of the flight not working to the female attendant staff of Indigo, but there was no one interested to look into it and even courtesy to update. Very poor condition traveling with such low class airlines where Ac is not working (Travelled on 17th Jan from Mumbai at 8AM and Travelled on 24th from Delhi at 8pm which was delayed)

I booked 4 tickets directly through their website. Two days later, I realized the booking was Economy Saver instead of Economy Standard, so I requested a refund in order to rebook. LOT cancelled the booking and refunded only the taxes, about 15%. When I contacted customer service, I was told the ticket was non-refundable. If that was the case, the booking should not have been cancelled without my confirmation, or at least I should have been clearly informed of the consequences before cancellation.

On this trip I reviewed the on time performance my second flight, only to find that it had been delayed 29 days out of 30. My two flights accumulated 93 mins delay total and I barely made my connection. I have never experienced such a poor airline.

Not the best experience, flight crew were friendly but flight was delayed on every transit. Seats were changed without notifying anyone. Aircraft was changed without notification. Overall bad planning. Flight from Malaysia to Tokyo was delayed. Value for money if time is not a major problem. Luggage allowance was also very generous compared to other airlines.

Friday evening flight to Cairo was first delayed by 3 hours due to technical fault, with extremely poor communication. All passengers deboarded. Then they finally announced cancellation and put us in a hotel, and said we can maybe fly Saturday, if not Sunday evening. They refused to put us on another route or with another airline. They also refused to refund my ticket when I phoned them (which they must do, as the service has not been given at all). I am an experienced traveler, including within Africa. This is the worst experience of my life while flying. I have had to make the necessary changes to my trip all by myself and purchased a new ticket via Etihad.

I was charged AUD 300 for my cabin bag after being told it did not meet the airline’s cabin dimensions and had to be treated as checked-in baggage.  What was most disturbing was being told at Sydney Airport that if I did not pay, I could not travel.  The in-flight experience was equally disappointing. My entertainment screen was not working, and my food was poor. I was moved to another seat due to these issues, but the replacement seat was uncomfortable. Many crew members struggled to communicate effectively with me in English. I emailed Vietnam Airlines’ support team regarding these issues and received no response for over a month. Only after I requested cancellation of my return ticket did I receive a reply, offering a USD 50 voucher as compensation.  It felt unreasonable to be forced to accept a voucher instead of fair compensation.

The Customer Service is poor. If you ever find yourself in need of a response or online assistance your best option is to change airline. My personal experience is that their website often does not process the information entered and remains idle leaving you with the only option of starting from scratch often with the same result over and over again. I got plenty of apologies for their system failures with promises "we are working on it" but fact is that in over 3 years I have seen no improvement or even a worsening of the relation with me "the Customer". Trying to contact them via e-mail, even thru the "preferred" Megavolotea channel, leads to nowhere: messages are acknowledged but I never got a final response addressing the reported issue or need of assistance so I have given up on it. Contact via phone is unsatisfactory at best with reduced work hours and limited weekend coverage just like if you are trying to contact a government agency. I thought that 24x7x365 is the norm in the airline business but obviously, it does not apply to Volotea. The Customer unfriendly approach is confirmed by the fact that when you call you have to pay per minute to talk to an agent and there is no option to be called back leading to frustration and turning fliers like me to look for alternative travel options.

The website is clunky and confusing. There is no meaningful cancellation policy even within the 24-hour window, they issue only a credit.  The ground staff were rude and dismissive to me. I would not fly with them again.

I'm usually not someone who writes reviews about airlines but on my Amsterdam to Vienna 31JAN flight number there were 2 very rude cabin staff on board. There was basically no help or explanation about the transfer we had to do because the flight was delayed. and on top of that the plane was dirty.

I had a few flights with them to and from the Philippines, both domestic and international. I found Cebu Pacific to be very professional and on time. They deliver their service with passion. The aircraft were clean. We experienced only minor delays, nothing serious. I also found their products to be solid overall. I was pleasantly surprised and would recommend them.  Even though they are a low-cost carrier, some of their tickets aren’t that cheap anymore, but they are still a good choice when visiting the Philippines and Southeast Asia.

Less than one hour into the flight, tonic ran out, followed shortly by gin. After less than two hours, wine, prosecco, snacks, and sandwiches were no longer available and around 40 passengers were booked in Business Class. As a result, the advertised onboard service was not delivered, and even Economy Class passengers had nothing left to purchase. What is even more disappointing is that almost three months later, Eurowings has not responded to my complaint. The cabin crew handled the situation in an exceptionally professional and friendly manner, and only thanks to them did the flight remain calm. They deserve genuine recognition and appreciation.

Had a great time in lounge at Gatwick, a much nicer experience than Heathrow. A good flight with an above average cabin crew, unfortunately let down by the old style club world seats. The awful climbing over someone's legs to use the bathroom.

They damaged the lock for my baggage and after communicating for over a month, they wanted me to go and repair it. I did go to a reputed repair shop who said they can't repair it. So I wrote to flydubai that it can't be repaired but they want me to get a proof that it can't be repaired, how does one get that. I asked them to advise a repair shop to whom I can take it and they have no reply on this. So if you have a checked in baggage, please write it off before you fly with them, as getting a compensation for a mistake of this airline is impossible.
Air travel on Indigo still sucks. System failure at Kenya airport for 6E 1854 on Feb 1st 2026 with no remedy and manual checkin - will lead to missing connection a BOM to DEL.

KLM cancelled my connecting flight (AMS → Dublin) and sent me a self-service rebooking link that showed no available flights for days. With no reroute, no hotel, and no assistance offered, I was forced to buy a €399 last-minute Ryanair flight just to get home. Weeks later, with no refund or response, KLM then cancelled my return flight, claiming I was a “no-show” for the outbound flight — a flight they themselves cancelled. Customer service later told me the only way to reinstate my return was to pay €500 extra! Proceed with caution if you value being treated fairly when things go wrong.

Tried to do an online check in the day before my flight but was getting a system error, not clear. Called their support which actually uses a paid 0801 line. Was told that they keep some seats for families etc and I should check in at the airport. Rushed earlier at the airport only to be told  that the flight is overbooked and I might not travel!. I was shocked as I travel a lot. Actually there were at least 8 empty seats in that flight, no apologies offered.  Was in a seat with no usb and not even a seat bag. Still my knees were touching the seat in front although i am only 1.75.  No wifi. Food just a biscuit and juice or water. Only positive was landing on time in Gatwick. Return flight their system was again not allowing me to purchase a seat, had to call their support to be able to pay for that. Gatwick quite awful with dirty toilets and a hassle to reach. Return plane a bit better, had seat bags this time. No usb, no wifi.  At least it was half empty in that flight. Would never travel with them again.

Very good airline with very clean aircraft and a friendly crew. However, their English was quite limited. They offered a small snack, which was nice. The ticket price wasn’t very cheap for such a short flight. Overall, there were no major delays, and I found the airline to be very professional. It was a refreshing and positive experience. I would definitely recommend them if you’re flying in Southeast Asia or through Vietnam again.

All in all a pleasant experience. The Polaris lounge at SFO is one of the best and provides a very comfortable preflight experience. All the ground staff contacts were pleasant and boarding was smooth. Due to a short flight time and an arrival curfew in Sydney, take off was delayed but the captain explained the situation well and it was all fine. The seat and amenities were great and I was able to get quite a bit of sleep on the 14.5 hour flight. The crew was marvelous and attentive. No complaints whatsoever.the only weak spot was the food, which has been my observation of United for quite a while. The selections are ok but the overall presentation leaves much to be desired. Compared to most business class airlines, where food is attractively presented, United just plops it on a plate. I fly Turkish quite a bit and their presentation makes excellent catering even more appealing. If United were to put some effort into their menus and tray layout, they would have a solid product.

All in all a pleasant experience. The Polaris lounge at SFO is one of the best and provides a very comfortable preflight experience. All the ground staff contacts were pleasant and boarding was smooth. Due to a short flight time and an arrival curfew in Sydney, take off was delayed but the captain explained the situation well and it was all fine. The seat and amenities were great and I was able to get quite a bit of sleep on the 14.5 hour flight. The crew was marvelous and attentive. No complaints whatsoever.the only weak spot was the food, which has been my observation of United for quite a while. The selections are ok but the overall presentation leaves much to be desired. Compared to most business class airlines, where food is attractively presented, United just plops it on a plate. I fly Turkish quite a bit and their presentation makes excellent catering even more appealing. If United were to put some effort into their menus and tray layout, they would have a solid product.

One flight was with A320neo which had a very tight legroom and the return on a A321ceo which had an average legroom. Both aircraft were clean and the crew was very friendly. There was no IFE but there was free WiFi and stream on your mobile. Food was fine consisting of cheese pie or turkey pie and beverages (I had preordered fruit plate).
Flight out and back delayed but not the kind of compensation delay. Other things were basic rouge - tight seats and no amenities were expected.

Boarding was non-standard and potentially chaotic with no lanes. We were eventually separated by cabin. Plane was new and in very good condition. I like the A330-900 because it is so quiet. Seat comfort was good. Legroom was on the lower end of premium economy, but fine even for a flight this long. I was lucky in that I was in a center aisle seat and the next two seats were empty, giving me some room to stretch out. IFE was very good, with a lot of choices. Food was not great, but I don't expect much of airplane food, so I was fine. The cabin crew was friendly, solicitous, and very visible. One reason for my high rating is that my last flight on this route was on United Polaris, which was a heck of a lot more money. Condor bested Polaris on seat comfort, food, IFE, and crew for less than half the price. I'd happily fly them again.

Both flights were with A330-300 were clean but on the outgoing flight my seat did not recline and on the return flight 3 of the 5 rear lavatories were broken. Alcoholic drinks were on buy, food was plenty and tasty. IFE had around 160 films but were old ones, all the Bollywood films were without subtitles.

The staff were friendly and professional, and everything was on time. The planes felt new and were clean. The snack offering was simple, nothing fancy, but at least something was provided. In Manila, they made sure passengers knew where to go for connecting flights, which was very helpful. Although the tickets weren’t cheap, I would recommend this airline.

A short flight so fairly bare-bones, but no complaints at all. I was concerned about seat comfort and pitch, but I was pleasantly surprised by the width and legroom - and I'm 6'2". I could have easily been comfortable on a longer flight. Plane was very clean, and boarding was efficient. Cabin crew served beverages. The experience was much better than I thought it would be.

I flew with Turkish Airlines and my seatturned out to be defective and not in proper working condition. This affected my comfort during the flight. After the flight, I contacted Customer Service to report the issue and request compensation. Unfortunately, I never received any response. The problem is not only the broken seat, but the complete lack of customer care and willingness to resolve the issue.

The in flight WiFi is expensive, randomly stops working, and is slow.  They have electronic window shades, which they turned to closed an hour or so into the flight, in the middle of the day.We flew over Iceland around noon. It would’ve been nice to be able to see it out the window.  Their online check in did not work for me, on either their app or website. I had to arrive early to sort out the mess. The flight attendants don’t let you go to the restroom during the 45 minutes before landing. In fairness, the food was pretty good.

On 30 January 2026, we were scheduled to fly on Flight J9248 from Madinah Airport. We arrived at the boarding gate 20 minutes before departure and boarding was denied by the ground staff. No assistance, no flexibility, and no announcements were made. This level of customer service is unacceptable, and I would not recommend this airline based on our experience.

On my recent business trip from Spain to Austria, they lost my suitcase during a connection in Madrid. The worst part is the lack of accountability and effort to fix their mistake. Thanks to my GPS tracker, I knew exactly where my bag was at all times. It arrived in Vienna on Tuesday morning, just 2 hours away from my hotel in Linz. Despite my repeated claims, Iberia and their partners didn't bother to deliver it on Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, or Friday. I spent my work trip without my professional gear and personal belongings. In the end, I had to pick it up myself at the Vienna Airport Lost & Found on my way back home on Saturday. Ruined my trip entirely.

I booked a round trip flight with United and when my return flight was cancelled due to the weather, United was unable to reassign me to another flight. Due to this, I had to book a separate flight to get home a day later despite being entitled to another flight since I had originally booked a round trip. I've been contacting United since and they refuse to reimburse me for the flight I paid out of pocket for $710. It's amazing that they can treat their customers this way and get away with it.

I booked a round trip flight with United and when my return flight was cancelled due to the weather, United was unable to reassign me to another flight. Due to this, I had to book a separate flight to get home a day later despite being entitled to another flight since I had originally booked a round trip. I've been contacting United since and they refuse to reimburse me for the flight I paid out of pocket for $710. It's amazing that they can treat their customers this way and get away with it.

As a result of missing our connecting flight in Kuwait with Kuwait Airways, we were compelled to stay overnight at a hotel in Kuwait. On the following day, contrary to our original booking, we were not transported onward with Kuwait Airways. Instead, without any consultation or our consent, we were rebooked onto a flight operated by Etihad Airways to Colombo. This flight was extremely chaotic and poorly managed. The overall level of service was unacceptable and had a significant negative impact on our travel experience. This matter is serious given that we have previously encountered substantial issues with Etihad Airways, which was the reason we had deliberately chosen not to travel with this airline again. Despite this, we were effectively compelled to fly with Etihad once more, resulting again in a negative experience.

After missing our connection in Amsterdam on Jan 3rd, 2026, due to a delay, we were abandoned at the transfer desk and no rebooking was offered. Staff told us: 'Organize your own transport home, KLM will cover the costs.' In an effort to minimize damages and get our child home, we organized a rental car and replacement flights ourselves. Now, KLM is refusing to reimburse the ~3,000 EUR in expenses. In their emails, KLM claims they offered us a ticket refund—which never happened. When we confronted them and tried to accept this refund, they simply blocked us with robotic templates stating: 'Our decision will not change.'  Avoid KLM if you value honesty and customer support.
Check in was smooth and easy and the flight left on time. I appreciated the free drinks, including wine and beer, and snacks. Staff were friendly and efficient.
I enjoyed the flight. Departure was on time. Only water was offered free, which is fine on a short flight. The staff were friendly, helpful and efficient.

Our experience with Aeromexico's customer service was beyond excellent! When my family had a glitch with our booking on the morning of our flight, their staff willingly assisted us with great patience and professionalism. Mr Carlos together with his manager and a lady staff solved our problem without even charging for an extra penalty. Hoping to fly with Aeromexico again & again!

Before we even left for our holiday, Air India rescheduled our flights 3  separate times. Because of the constant changes, we lost a full day of our holiday and a paid night at our villa, money gone, time gone, and zero accountability from the airline. While we were abroad, they then tried to move our return flight to a different day. We refused. So instead, they moved us to an earlier morning flight, again cutting into our holiday. Then they changed it back. Then unbelievably 1 hour before departure they hit us with a 5 hour 45 minute layover delay when it was originally supposed to be 1 hour 15 minutes. That is not a small delay.  Throughout all this chaos we were offered nothing. No food. No drinks. No proper communication. Staff were either nowhere to be seen or completely unhelpful.  Then on  the flight, an 11 plus hour long haul flight the toilets were filthy, unhygienic and embarrassing for an international airline. My food was terrible, barely edible, and we were only offered drinks twice for the flight. I genuinely wish I had read reviews first, I would have avoided this airline completely. Unprofessional, unclean, unreliable, and unapologetic. Would never fly with them again.

Trichy to Kuala Lumpur. Ground staff were excellent. Very detailed and punctual. They were really doing their job. I would like to mention check in counter staff Bakul for being very courteous, polite and humble. It made a difference especially that we had to miss our earlier flight on 1st February 2026 on a different airline and stay back 2 extra days as my daughter had bad food poisoning. We were already very disturbed and exhausted. But it was a smooth process and we reached home safely.

I originally flew down to Tampa's on MX135 Islip to Tampa. The staff on the plane were miserable. It was as if they were inconvenienced by anything anyone asked them. No hello as you enter plane and literal straight faced the entire flight. Then I fly back to Islip from Tampa on MX118 and it got worse. They're rushing everybody to secure the cabin. Meanwhile, they're paging for customers that aren't on the plane yet and it's five minutes before door closing Time on the boarding pass. So because of that, I take my daughter's pull-up off at the seat, which I understand. I should've went to the bathroom, but she was rushing everyone to put the seatbelt on, so I'm thinking it's going to be a 3-5 min process so let me just take my daughters pull up off, I didn't put a new on just removed the old. Staff say to me "next time do that in the bathroom." I told of course and just wanted to explain I did it that for the good of the plane, she dismissed me, then the other flight attendant came by and chimed in, I explained to her what happened and she says but isn't the seatbelt light on, I said that's why I stayed in seat and she like but do understand what I'm telling you. About 10 min later the first attendant came by and said "I need you to open the window shade" so I opened it and turned to my four-year-old daughter and said "it needs to be open when we takeoff and this woman is so easily offended she says "I wouldn't be telling you to open it if you didn't need to" I told her I wasn't even talking to her". They can keep their seats. I'll spend an extra 50 bucks to travel on a nicer airline.

The Wifi didn't work. Requested refund. Finnair referred me to a companion airline, British Airways, who handled another part of the flight. British Airways referred me back to Finnair, thereby completing the circle. Spent 30 days on this thus far.

Allowing customers 2 bags in the cabin, getting off a plane becomes unbearably slow and it is time for airlines to better organise this, just as boarding is organised. Low cost airlines with their strictly applied hand luggage allowance are much more pleasant in this regard, as it makes deplaning faster and easier. Seats comfortable. Iberia is a quiet airline, with pilots getting on with flying, and not issuing any updates. Sitting on the plane on the tarmac with a late departure some information is sometimes not unpleasant.
Was great overall, no delay, flight was on time arrived on time, clean plane with good legroom, nice staff as well. Flight itself was good, would fly again

Another successful flight on Saudia and it was excellent value at under $300 Jeddah to London. Not a full flight so boarding smooth at the ever so easy Jeddah airport. A friend allowed me access to the excellent Saudia lounge too. Onboard service polite and efficient. Crew pleasant. Small amenities kit, hot towel and pillow blanket and headphones all provided. Food serving look quite basic but was fine and pizza slices and drinks served before landing. My third time on this route and I have always been impressed when considering the price too. Incredible value. Baggage took around 20 mins on arrival and LHR was quite quiet at the time. Do give Saudia a go if you want to make savings. My IFE was broken but as I had 3 seats to myself I used the next one. Selection sufficient (although I never really use IFE except the map). Will use again.

Bought a Business Class Lite ticket with no lounge access. First flight in QSuites was fine. In Doha our plane to Vie was 4 hours late due to operational reasons. No compensation offered, nothing. Flight itself was ok with a very mediocre lunch.

No Refund has been processed on a flight that has been cancelled within time and refund applied, waiting for 3 months plus, no response, no response on a different customer service centre contact approach.

I traveled with Arajet to Costa Rica and Mexico, always with my pet, and the service was excellent. The last time, traveling to NLU Mexico City, my connecting flight was delayed because we couldn't fly over Venezuela. They gave me a 5-star hotel to wait for my new flight. Everything was excellent. Viaje con Arajet a Costa Rica y Mexico, siempre con mi mascota y el servicio fue excelente. La ultima vez viajando a NLU Mexico City se demoro el vuelo en la conexion debido a q no podiamos volar sobre venezuela. Me dieron un hotel 5* para esperar mi nuevo vuelo. Todo excelente

I had a disappointing experience with this airline. The staff's language proficiency was lacking, and I had to request them to speak slowly on multiple occasions. Despite canceling my flight within the 24-hour time frame, they failed to provide a full refund as per their policy. When I filed a claim, the agent provided an incorrect confirmation number, which delayed the process. I repeatedly explained the issue over the phone and via email, but they refused to refund the full amount. The airline's disorganization was evident, and I will not be flying with them again.
A 2 hour 15 mins delay, which was notified 20 minutes before departure. No explanation, no excuses, just par for the course it seems.

Jakarta to Amsterdam was an exceptional First Class experience from start to finish. I was picked up from my home and met curbside at the terminal by the First Class team, who assisted me through check-in, security, and immigration before escorting me to the First Class lounge. In the lounge, there was a full pre-boarding à la carte menu along with an extensive drink selection. I opted for a light snack, which was excellent. At boarding time, I was personally escorted to the aircraft door, where I was warmly welcomed by the First Class crew: Nuning, Naurenia, Siska, and Chef Prima. The onboard service was outstanding. I ordered breakfast approximately three hours prior to landing, and both the quality of the food and its presentation were exceptional. We arrived in Amsterdam on schedule, where I was met at the aircraft door and escorted to the lounge to await my connecting flight. A special thank you to Naurenia and Siska for their outstanding service throughout the journey, and to Chef Prima for the excellent cuisine. T

Iberia informed me that my flight would be delayed and that my connection in Madrid to Bordeaux would be nearly impossible. When I arrived at Bogota airport the afternoon flight to Madrid (IB 0152) was still there - also heavily delayed - so I asked the staff to put me on the waiting list for that flight in order to catch my connection in Madrid and to save time and costs for both me and the airline. The local manager was very unpolite and she said 'the staff in Madrid would help me to get to Bordeaux'. The flight BOG-MAD left with more than 2,5h delay but we arrived in Madrid 30' before the departure of my connection to Bordeaux. As I only carried hand luggage I tried to catch the flight by running through T4 - there was no assistance by Iberia staff. The plane was still at gate but  gate is closed.  At the customer service the agent apologized but he only could offer me a flight to Bordeaux the next morning. The evening flight with Volotea he wasn't allowed to book, so I booked it myself. The flight itself with the A350 was a good experience and the crew on board was friendly and helpful - they promised me to inform the Madrid staff of my short connection, but nobody was there to help me once we arrived in Madrid. My food on board was bad. The seat is great and also the entertainment system very good. The free WIFI in business is a joke as you can only see your whatsapp messages. A very disappointing experience.

KLM lost our baggage for 8 days and the advice was for us to buy clothes and toilet products. Now 40 days after, KLM still refusing to process the claim and refund the outstanding amount.  Never flying KLM again!

Flew ScootPlus for the first time, but the experience was marred as the pre-ordered meal was incorrect, leaving the cabin crew having to find out the print-out data error. They were helpful despite the error. When I emailed feedback to help them improve their processes, the response was a refusal of compensation, something I never even requested.

This was one of the best flights I had, travelling with a 6 months baby for the first time. The flight attendants made the journey much easier and relax for of us.  I would like express my gratitude to the following staff, thank you for the hand written post card and sharing their personal chips to us. The Gin and Tonic they made was delicious.

We had such a great experience with Japan Airlines. Flying Premium Economy really felt premium here as some airports (eg at Narita Terminal 2) we even got priority check-in and boarding & lounge access was included. Staff was fluent in English and very professional. The airplanes are clean, well maintained and feel modern. The fact that the seats in premium economy are in a hard shell so the seat in front of you won’t be lowered onto your space is a big advantage, the entertainment system works smoothly and doesn’t feel clunky like with other airlines. There was no WiFi on our international flights however but we didn't mind that. Highly recommend!

We could not buy check in luggage before hand, had to pay per kilo at the airport which was £186 for 25kilo. We paid for 1.5 hour transit but ended up being stuck at the airport for over 10 hours. We missed our connecting flight and had to stay at the hotel to get another for next day. Staff  told us we could get compensation for the delay but Kuwait customer service are blunt and often get ignored. We were never offered any help or support. 1st and last time flying Kuwait Airways and would never recommend to anyone.

Venice–Marseille flight with Volotea in economy class. Everything went perfectly. Boarding was smooth, the cabin was clean and the comfort was adequate for an economy class flight. The cabin crew were pleasant and efficient. The flight arrived on time and the overall experience was very satisfactory.

Check in at Terminal 4 was fast and courteous; I was allowed one checked bag. Security was efficient and courteous as well. The plane was full, but boarding went well. The interior of the cabin seemed a bit old and worn, but the plane was clean and the seat was comfortable. The staff was friendly and efficient, and served a very good vegan Indian meal that I had ordered beforehand. The flight was pleasant and uneventful. We arrived at Mumbai on schedule. A good experience overall.

I chose this flight from Sydney to YVR as it was a direct flight 14 hr. I booked a Premium Economy seat for 50,000 avion points plus $3376. If you travel this route be prepared for less than stellar service and poor quality food, but I am comparing AC to the standard of Air New Zealand flight YVR to Auckland. There are 24 people in PE sharing bathrooms with 336 other passengers seated in Economy, and on a long haul flight the bathrooms get pretty disgusting. Premium Economy were given ear plugs to view the TV screen that required subtitles as the sound was so poor. On AC I received stale buns and a sloppy chicken dinner plus hard scramble eggs and one sausage for breakfast along with wooden cutlery. Plus we were awoken during the flight to get a bun with a cream cheese / tuna filling and 2 cookies. The AC check-in counter in SYD was excellent, the flight without complications and landed in YVR early. Our priority baggage was first off, so no complaints there. Please understand I love Air Canada and my usual flights (YVR to YOW) are wonderful. For these 5 hour short flights I fly Economy and have had good movies, great meals and service. I was embarrassed as I had told the Aussies waiting to board how great AC was. However, being a PE guest on this AC34 long haul flight was not close to the standard I know can be delivered.

I was slightly concerned about taking a carrier with 2 planes, However it was one of the best business class flights. The Plane was immaculately clean, the staff were superb the meal was excellent. Good Champagne and good wine served with a smile. The plane left on time and arrived on time. The meal was Chicken Roulade or a Fish dish, I chose the Chicken and was not disappointed.

This BA flight on 31 Jan was largely uneventful. The food service has deteriorated further. The seats in economy as uncomfortable as ever. BA crew are generally quite efficient but there's something very snooty and superior about BA staff which you don't see on many other airlines. It's hard to explain but it's almost as though they're there to do you a huge favour when in reality you're keeping them in a job and in many cases could fly with another airline. I've always resisted it when people have claimed this before but sadly I do believe it's true.

I booked this flight using avios and a companion voucher so was exceptional value. The cash fare however would have seemed expensive. On a Sunday afternoon/early evening Heathrow T5 check in and security had little queue and I was through to the departure lounge very quickly. As my flight was going from B gates, I opted for the B Gate Galleries Lounge, which was calm and not too busy. Food offerings were fairly good, I had some soup and a chicken dish with mashed potatoes, followed by some pork pie snack. Drinks offerings as always were plentiful and easy to access. Boarding was fairly quick and I was immediately offered a welcome drink, I chose the champagne. My bedding, amenity kit, headphones and water bottle were waiting in my seat as usual. Seat and area were generally clean although crumbs can be seen in some of the crevices. I am a fan of the club suite, even though I wish the walls and door were higher more similar to the Qsuite of Qatar Airways. The seat is comfortable in take off, lounging and sleeping mode, and there is ample storage. After take off and a fair wait, drinks and a bag of snacks were served while we waited for our meal. The snacks really should be in a bowl rather than a bag. For the meal I enjoyed a tuna and avocado starter which was beautifully presented and very tasty. My main was a malai chicken curry with rice, daal and breads. Presentation was fine, annoyingly quite a bit of the rice was crunchy rather than cooked, but the taste of the dish was decent. For desert I opted for the cheese board, which was good but should come with a couple more crackers. I made use of the club kitchen for a couple more top ups of wine before bed - whilst some people would prefer to ring the call button the convenience of the club kitchen and being able to help yourself is easier and quicker in my opinion. IFE was fairly good although I had to search for movies that I knew were on there as they didn’t come up in any browsing option I could find, making it appear there was a much more limited selection than there actually was. The screen is big however the quality of the movies was actually quite low, more like old analogue tv rather than hd let alone 4k. Given the recent refits of these planes this is disappointing - not sure if it is hardware limitation of just the software / quality of the videos they’ve purchased. WiFi messaging is free for members of The Club.  I did not try the paid packages. I slept fairly well for 2-3hrs. The ‘mattress topper’ is fairly pointless but does at least create a clean area to sleep on not just the seat itself. The pillow is excellent and the blanket keeps you warm enough. Breakfast was a full English, fresh fruit and a coffee. All of which were actually very good. Overall the cabin crew were very good. As this was a night flight they were not very present through the night, but were professional and friendly during all of the service.

Extremely disappointing experience on Emirates EK416 (Dubai to Sydney, 06 Feb — 13h 50m flight). Despite booking my family under a single booking reference, Emirates split us across different rows, seating my wife and one child separately from me and my other child. Another passenger was placed in our original aisle seats, forcing our family apart on a nearly 14-hour long-haul flight. It looks like Emirates is deliberately separating families to push passengers into paying extra for seat reservations. This is unethical, customer-unfriendly, and unacceptable, especially when traveling with children. Family seating should be a basic right, not a paid privilege. This experience has seriously damaged my trust in Emirates.

Very disappointed by the airline staff service, I was going to fly to LA then from LA connect with China southern airlines to China. Upon arriving the staff wasn’t present at the kiosk and after an hour the attendant finally showed up only to tell me I needed a visa to fly which wasn’t true under China visa free transit policy, after she stated that she left without giving me any further information or assistance. I tried to go to the front counter and they weren’t any help either. Due to this I had to book another flight with spirit airlines to LA to make my connection in time and of course when I got to LA China southern airlines checked me in without any issues. All I can say is the American Airlines in Houston is garbage and recommend people avoid using them when flying internationally.

I recently traveled Hainan Airlines' international and was impressed by the exceptional service throughout the journey. The cabin crew provided attentive, thoughtful and warm service that exceeded expectations. I highly recommend it to anyone seeking premium air travel.

KWI-FRA enjoyable flight on A330-800 neo Arriving at KWI on time and Transiting at KWI Airport quick and smooth. KWI-FRA on new fresh and clean A330-800 neo. WIFI was charged extra. Departure on time, flight full but crew very professional. Inflight service was efficient and friendly. A Delicious Lunch was serve (again 2 choices arabic lamb or chicken western style) same average IFE. During the flight crew ran often with tray of water and juices. 1 hours before landing at FRA chicken sandwich and beverage was serve. All in all enjoyable flight. On my opinion KAC is an underated airline in the Middle East with only one disappointed point - purchasing ticket directly on KAC website which I did the price was around 20% more expensive than purchasing via internet agency.

Bangkok to Kuwait a Boeing 777 with 3-3-3 layout. Check In was quick and smooth. Ground staff nice and helpful. Before entering the Gate, there was a security check of carry on baggages. The staff informed me that due to Kuwaiti laws that alcoholic beverage is strictly prohibited on board of the Kuwaiti aircrafts therefore the airport staff have to check all the carry on baggage if passengers brought alcoholic beverage at duty free shops.  Great crew and really helpful. Shortly after take off soft drinks was served and lights was shut down for sleep. Around 5 hours later we got hot breakfast, (2 choices western and asia ) IFE was mostly arabic and bollywood films. All in all comfortable flight  if you do not mind the IFE and alcoholic beverage

Last year, on our way home from MNL to LAX, I checked-in my wife's handicap scooter in a box and Philippine Airlines slapped us with $250 fee for 'oversized baggage' knowing it's for disability person. From LAX to MNL, there was no charge using same box. The normal fee for one way is $125, but they charged us double that. They have no consideration at all. The airline doesn't care about the passengers especially handicap people. They took advantage of us for profit/revenue. Their service is very poor and they would not reimburse us even after the complaint was filed to government and transportation agencies. We'll never fly with Philippine Airlines again!

We experienced a very chaotic checkin in Cebu. People where crossing from left and right, and more then one hour waiting time in line, and we got our first 40 minutes delay. In Singapore we’re sitting in the plain and we had a delay of three hours and reboarding. On our way back we experienced the same. I will avoid Scoot if I can!

My wife and I have flown Qatar many times, but this experience was not one of our best. Hard product was good, although the 777 used on the DOH-MLE-DOH sector must be one of the oldest in their fleet and feels it. Soft product was not up to scratch on the LGW-DOH leg. This was a holiday flight and my wife and I like our wine. The brut champagne ran out before we were an hour into the flight, and the sauvignon blanc ran out before we were half way through the six hour flight.

Wanted to do a quick visit to Mexico City from San Jose, Costa Rica. The flight is 3 hours. I booked a return flight for 437.90 Canadian. We are used to paying for luggage now, but I was expecting around $50 for each way, so I really didn’t think about it much. Until I checked in the night before when I was shocked to see they charge 237$ CND (as per my credit card later) for one piece of checked luggage and  they strictly enforce the carry on rule which is one bag, my back pack. I had a light travel ukulele and a yoga matt as well which to them counted as two extra pieces which then totaled 233.09 CND. So I was charged 507 CND for my baggage one way. And I’ll have to do it on my way back again! So, what I thought would be a 437 $ flight, plus $100 for my baggage, for a 3 hr return flight, has turned into a total cost of $1452 CND. I feel scammed and will never fly with Volaris again and I haven’t even gotten on the plane yet!

Very difficult situation. Flight was delayed for over 5 hours. They gave us a coupon for 1 restaurant meal but refused to honor it for trivial reasons (said it was not used at a restaurant even though it was). They offered very small amount of flight miles but we cannot use them unless we purchase an extremely expensive ticket. We were completely exhausted and it ruined our vacation.

Very disappointing experience with KM Malta Airlines. It was not clearly communicated that the hand baggage must be checked in and cannot be taken on board. The fact that I was not charged on the outbound flight made this even more confusing. Being charged €30 at the gate on the return flight felt unfair and poorly communicated. This policy should be made much clearer to passengers to avoid unexpected fees.

I am writing this review after an extremely distressing experience on an 8 hr Virgin Atlantic evening flight returning home from a family holiday. What should have been a pleasant journey ended very badly. There were 19 of us traveling, including children and we were all exhausted. Instead of receiving the level of service Virgin Atlantic is known for, we were met with rude and abrupt behaviour from cabin crew. Unfounded accusations were made about drinking prior to boarding the airline, alcohol service was refused and the overall attitude was dismissive and unprofessional. There was no disruption nor complaints from other passengers. Because of the way we were treated, I asked that we were not disturbed once asleep and as a result did not eat dinner or breakfast. This was not due to our choice, but because of the poor handling of the situation by the cabin crew. The lack of communication, empathy, and professionalism completely ruined the end of what had been a wonderful holiday. After many previous flights with Virgin Atlantic, this experience has destroyed my confidence in the airline. I would not choose to fly with them again. After complaining to them they still will not take responsibility of what happened and replied with excuse after excuse.

Booked a vacation through Sunwing, no warning given it would be a Westjet plane. Let alone one of their new squeeze every last dime out of consumers with 28" pitch (leg room). Canadian aviation standard is 30". Westjet continues to make anti consumer decisions to pad shar holder pockets. Shame on them for abandoning their roots. My family of 4 will not be flying with them in the future.

I was having trouble logging into my Vueling account. After waiting for over three months, I decided to contact them via Twitter, where they were incredibly kind and helpful, and they assisted me within 24 hours. The chatbot is terrible, but their Twitter support is amazing. Estaba teniendo problemas al iniciar sesión en mi cuenta de Vueling despues de mas de 3 meses de espera decidí escribirles por Twitter, donde de forma super amable y cordial no tardaron ni 24h en ayudarme. El chatbot es una mierda, pero por twitter son increibles.

We had a layover in Bogota and the screens only said gate changed A13 to A14. At almost exactly 5 p.m. it switched to boarding. We were there at 5:05 p.m. and were told the gate is closed. The staff was not answering any questions, only making us walk around from counter to counter and offering a penalty higher than a flight back to Europe. To us it seems the flight was overbooked and the whole thing was a rip-off! Not one employee that should have helped us in our situation was useful, or tried to help or was empathic at all. We asked questions and were literally ignored!! We were sent from counter to counter just to wait and wait again, going from one supervisor to the next, just to be sent away again without even trying to help or to understand our situation.

After a medical emergency abroad, I was forced to return to Canada and could not use my British Airways return flight from Rome. I notified the airline, provided documentation, and requested a credit for the unused return portion of the ticket. What followed was more than four months of deflection and obstruction. British Airways demanded medical documents, many of which were already provided, only to claim later that they were “not in the correct department” or “not attached to this case.” I received multiple AI-generated responses that did not address my situation at all. At times, replies were factually incorrect or unrelated to my case. Despite acknowledging my medical emergency, British Airways insisted on impossible or medically absurd requirements — such as retroactive certificates stating that I was “unable to fly”. British Airways claimed Expedia was responsible, while Expedia explicitly instructed me to deal with British Airways as the operating carrier. I was trapped in a circular loop where no one accepted responsibility. Even after confirming that my return flight was unused, British Airways continued to delay, request duplicate paperwork, and ultimately refused resolution.

My flights were canceled, and in addition to disrupting my entire trip, I lost the money I paid for additional services (carry-on baggage on both legs), which I was unable to use. As a consequence of the cancellation, I was forced to purchase last-minute tickets with other airlines, at significantly higher prices. As a result, this trip ended up being the most expensive trip I have ever taken, entirely due to Flybondi’s lack of responsibility. On top of that, their customer service channels are misleading.  They advertise an 0810 phone number as a contact option, but when you call, you are told to dial *3000 instead, which charges ARS 300 per minute from any phone provider. Once connected to this paid line, an automated message tells you — only once — that claims for cancellations or rescheduled flights must be sent by email, and then the call is terminated. In other words, you are charged to be told that they do not handle claims by phone. The post-cancellation process was confusing, slow, and completely inadequate for an issue caused by the airline itself. The so-called “low cost” model completely disappears when something goes wrong: the passenger is left alone, without real support, and forced to absorb all the costs. My recommendation is clear: do not buy tickets from this airline if you need reliability, real customer support, or accountability in case of cancellations. The risk is simply not worth it.
They exclude access to Lounges on the Business Value Fares. Guess its a one time for me.

Check-in smooth but unfortunately unable to select seats as flights were part of Air India codeshare. Luckily it resulted in an aisle and a window seat. Delhi-Munich on the A380 left almost an hour late but managed to arrive just in time. Plane was rather old, even no USB charging options, but clean and sufficient legroom and seat width. The IFE was just as dated but didn't bother me too much as this was a night flight. Service from the crew was spot on, fast distribution of the meals and timely cleanup and with several passages for additional drinks. Even received a hot towel, long time since I've seen this in economy. Got a tight 50 minutes layover in Munich, but it took only 20 minutes in total from disembarking the first flight to being on board the next flight - this including clearing security and immigration! Very efficient airport and would for sure prefer it over a 2 hours layover in Frankfurt. A319 to Brussels - standard no thrills short EU flight, arrived on time and the baggage made it so that's what matters.

Boarded my first segment at 9:30 PM going from Kuala Lumpur to Singapore and plane broke down on the runway. Finally disembarked at 3 AM, but it took them until 7 AM to release all passengers. They rescheduled the segment to Singapore which departed at 10:30 AM and arrived at 11:30. Went to the Scoot transfer counter upon arrival expecting to immediately receive my boarding pass for the next segment to Qingdao, but nothing. Only 2 agents trying to service several hundred passengers, and then one of the agents decided to leave. After 4 hours at the transfer desk and still no boarding pass. They knew they had hundreds of passanges needing flights changed since the proceeding day, but made no efforts to prepare. I even called their customer agents and was told I was a no-show for my segment from Singapore to Qingdao. Of course I was a no-show, I was sitting in their broken down plane in Kuala Lumpur. The agent did say they would escalate my issue, but could not commit to any resolution or assure me that I would get a boarding ticket. The level of incompetence is beyond all comprehension. I will never consider Scoot as a viable airline for any business or pleasure, no matter how inexpensive.

Good flight for fair price. The plane was very old and not clean, but with very good leg space. They offering a cold meal with Soft drinks, but coffee was not available (technical problems they said). Flight on time. Would fly with them again.

I recently flew with United Airlines on a multi-leg trip to and from Houston, and what I experienced was not a single mistake — it was a full-stack failure across every layer of service.  Airport kiosks were out of service. Front counter staff were gossiping instead of assisting passengers. My luggage was lost and delayed for over 72 hours. When it finally arrived, bags were opened, dirty, and damaged. One bag (out of six) was completely unusable. That is a verifiable collapse of service from curb to baggage claim. Frontline staff on the ground showed empathy and ultimately processed my baggage refund. They understood what had happened. Corporate customer care did not. I was contacted by United’s Care Management team who did not acknowledge the extreme additional expenses I absorbed. They offered a dismissive “goodwill” amount of roughly $35 — despite documented damage, lost property, and hundreds of dollars in out-of-pocket costs — and initially refused even a baggage refund.  This was about refund for services not delivered.  Fortunately, other departments within United ultimately corrected parts of this.

Seattle to Singapore with a stopover at Tokyo-Haneda, with both sectors operated by a Boeing 787-9. Having booked this ticket as a United codeshare and originating from Dallas, I could not check in online either due to the system detecting an IP location mismatch or the server being down. Upon arrival at Seattle, I tried checking in via the kiosk and was surprised to see me being assigned a middle seat. I stood in line for around 3.5 hours before the flight, and I asked if there were window seats available. The agent was willing to switch my seat to a window for the Tokyo-Singapore leg, but told me the window seats were full for the Seattle to Tokyo leg. After I took the Seattle Underground, I proceeded to my gate only to hear a gate agent mispronouncing my name; I clarified, and I was glad I did - I got upgraded to an aisle bulkhead seat. As I boarded, I then proceeded to my seat, which, of course, had very generous legroom. It took me a while to get familiar with the tray table and the IFE latch mechanism, and the back padding of my seat had either shrunk or was a bit poorly padded, but in general, the seat was decently easy to operate, was comfortable with generous recline and legroom, and had a decent amount of amenities. I would personally love it more if the magazines were also included in the seat pocket. Takeoff was only a few minutes late, and then the service started. In total, 4 meals were served on this sector, plus an endless round of drinks, all of which were beautiful in taste and presentation. The crews on this sector were beyond friendly, courteous, and attentive. They were energetic, cheerful, and even gave my seatmate and me some photo ideas that they helped us take. Knowing that it was my first time flying ANA, they then gave me tons of souvenirs and a vanilla mouse cake from Business Class with a chocolate, hand-glazed message "Thank you for flying ANA". I then transferred to Terminal 2 by bus, and while both flights had clean cabins in good condition, the temperature was set a bit too warm on both flights. The seat on my Singapore-bound flight, however, was better-padded and more comfortable. Being a red-eye flight, only 2 meals were served, but an endless round of drink service was still served. All of them had great presentation and taste as well. On both flights, the in-flight entertainment was super responsive for its age and had tons of content, although the layout was not the best in efficiency (vertical list instead of horizontal, requiring tedious scrolling and clicking to figure out things). The Wi-Fi was not programmed to auto-display the captive portal, and I had to type it on my own using the provided guide, which caused me to incorrectly assume on my Haneda-bound flight that the Wi-Fi failed; I tried the Wi-Fi on the Singapore flight, and it was speedy and stable, albeit being available only for texting. The crews of this Singapore-bound flight were less energetic compared to my Haneda-bound flight, but they were still friendly and polite. Landing at Changi was a few minutes early, and the bags did take a while to arrive. However, for my first flight with ANA, I immediately fell in love with them.

Exceptional Recovery by AZAL Customer Support! ​My journey from Istanbul to Islamabad via Baku hit a major snag with a 24-hour delay. While delays are frustrating, Azerbaijan Airlines’ response was top-tier. Not only did they provide hotel accommodation, but their claims department handled my compensation (Case #3241707) with zero hassle. They were professional, transparent, and paid out the statutory compensation directly to my bank account within weeks. Truly a passenger-first airline!

Kuala Lumpur to Yogyakarta. I did not check in online or select a seat, but this time, my travel party and I were not scattered apart; we were seated in adjacent rows, still with nobody in the middle seat. The check-in process was wholly digital and automated, but the staff managing crowd control and directing passengers made the check-in experience feel like enlisting for a military boot camp. However boarding was orderly and efficient, with slowdowns again tied to the capacity of the plane and some passengers in the earlier zones boarding with the later. The boarding gate staff members were friendlier, albeit still on the colder side, and once on board, I was welcomed enthusiastically by the lead flight attendant. Despite finishing boarding early, we pushed back and took off 40-ish minutes late due to a last-minute no-show. Soon after, the service started, and all of the crews were nice, warm, cheerful, and energetic. There was no Wi-Fi due to this plane being an ex-MYAirline plane, but I kinda wished that all AirAsia planes were like this; seats slimline and thin but well-padded, decently pre-reclined, and easy to use, and the cabin so pristine, well air conditioned, and clean that I had no idea this plane was 16 years old.  Even though I was in the hot seat, the slimline design of the seats gave me 1"-2" extra pitch. Landing was not terribly late, and we only needed to wait a while for the baggage to arrive. It's amazing how AirAsia turned an uneventful flight into something memorable, and this time, I can see their real potential as the world's best low-cost airline.

Yogyakarta to Kuala Lumpur on their 186-seater Airbus A320-200. As I did not prepay for a seat, my travel parties were scattered everywhere in the cabin from rows 16 to 32, but by sheer luck, none of us were assigned the middle seat. Everybody working the front line at YIA was friendly, efficient, and accommodating, and most importantly, they stood their ground, resulting in a very orderly boarding process; the slowdowns only occurred due to the plane's capacity and the passengers who didn't hear their zone being called, and, as a result, boarded late. Takeoff was obviously late due to the late arrival of this aircraft, but soon after, the services began. The cabin was clean, comfortable, and in great condition, considering the airframe being almost 7.5 years old, with the only minus point being a minor coffee spillover in one of the window sheds. The seat was well-padded and generally comfortable, with the only minus point being the thick design, which made the legroom very tight. The cabin crews serving me on this flight were mixed in friendliness, with most of them leaning on the "friendly, attentive, and courteous but cold in body language" side. There was a Wi-Fi entertainment onboard, but I couldn't connect without figuring out what the captive portal was. We landed not terribly behind schedule, and our bags came out not a minute after we passed immigration. Overall, I can see why they are the best in the low-cost airline category, and with just a bit more energy on the crew's side, this flight would have been a 10/10.

Singapore to Jakarta on an A320. The high score I gave for this flight was a result of the smooth and friendly ground experience at Changi, the baggage handling wait time at Jakarta, delicious bread, and friendly cabin crew. However Batik's hard product left a lot to be desired; as part of their cabin standardization, they removed the IFE and replaced the seats with the same model but with a different design and tighter legroom; the legroom is comparable to a low-cost carrier.  The seat was well-padded and easy to operate, but the thickness of the seat defeated the slimline design of the seat, and I would say such seats (legroom and design-wise) do not belong to an airline proclaiming to be a full-service carrier. Some of the cabin panels had yellowed and accumulated wear and tear. The air conditioning was also not the coldest, but the crew apologized for this. Overall, I would say that this time, the soft product and service have saved Batik Air on this flight, but if they cannot find a way to improve their hard product while still claiming themselves to be a full-service airline, I would start asking questions.

I booked this flight PEN - HKT to connect to a flight on to Koh Samui, unfortunately the airline re timed the flight meaning I could not make the connecting flight to USM. I tried to cancel using the online agent, but it was unable to understand what I was trying to say or explain. I was forced to book an alternative with Singapore Airlines. Passengers be aware they are okay on board but incompetent if anything goes wrong, I will never use them again.

Dallas/Fort Worth to Seattle on the A220-100. I went to the airport 3.5 hours before departure, and at that time, the check-in counters were not open yet. The kiosks were, and I was able to get my boarding pass and bag tag before queuing. The number of early morning flights departing out of Dallas meant that the line was long, but Delta did a great job managing crowd control. The ground staff members at Dallas were helpful and communicative, but not the friendliest, as if they were not having a great night's sleep and hated working opening shifts (which is understandable). I then proceeded to my gate and boarded at the very last group, welcomed by a team of flight crews who were more passionate. Take-off was only a few negligible minutes behind. My seat, being a row behind the Comfort+ row and ahead of the emergency exit, did not recline, but it came with 1" extra pitch at 32" and was decently comfortable, clean, and user-friendly. Delta provides both IFE TV screens that were locally developed by DFP as well as Wi-Fi connectivity. Both were super responsive, and their interfaces were laid out beautifully. The contents on the TV were loaded and plenty, with the only issue being the flight map not advancing past the information screen. The Wi-Fi was surprisingly also very stable, even when playing 1080p YouTube videos. The meal, despite only being snacks, was decent - the crews offered 3 rounds of drink services on this 4-hour flight. My aircraft was around 6.5 years old at the time of my ride, and the cabin condition made it seem like the aircraft was only half its actual age. The air conditioning was set at a great temperature, and I didn't see any cleanliness issues on board. Having flown other US carriers, I must say that Delta's cabin crews have proven on my flight that they are a league above anyone else; they were super friendly and energetic, treating everybody with a smile, respect, and attentiveness. Landing was a few minutes early, but disembarkation was delayed due to the gate staff not being ready, which added to the lateness. Upon arrival, my bags were already waiting for me. Overall, Delta barely put a foot wrong on this flight, and I feel appreciated as a Skymiles member.

Flight departed slightly late but arrived on time. Meal service did not commence until a couple of hours into the flight. Food portions were too small and no additional snacks available mid-flight despite the length of the flight. Quality and quantity of the breakfast provided prior to landing was poor. IFE entertainment was great. Leg room for Plus seats was reasonable. Priority boarding was honoured. Cabin crew were friendly. Overall the flight satisfied the function required but the food provision is somewhat lacking.

Yogyakarta to Singapore on board their A321neo. I was not sure whether this was because of the load of the flight or my other travel party's status, but a week before the flight, Scoot was kind enough to assign me a block of 3 seats for me and my travel party in the middle of the plane, with me being in the window seat. As a result, I could relax at check-in, and all I needed to do was drop my bag. Boarding commenced on time, in order, and was surprisingly very fast despite the capacity of the plane and the load factor. As I boarded, I left behind the cold and depressed-looking ground staff members at Yogyakarta; I didn't observe any smiles, only faces of fatigue or sorrow that gave me the silent treatment. That said, it all ended there - even before we took off, which was just 3 minutes late, the crews, known as Scootees, were already so friendly, attentive, courteous, energetic, and cheerful, which are great hallmarks that I observed from Scoot's "Scootitude". It has been a long time since someone greeted me with a "how are you", to which I returned the favor. The cabin was cool and comfortable, with the air conditioning doing its absolute best to control the temperature on board. It was also clean and basically close to brand-new, with the exception of a few wear and tear, mostly from finger, pen, or pencil scratches. Scoot picked the right seat design. It was slimline and thin, boosting legroom by an inch or two, but it was also well-padded, easy to operate, and generally very comfortable. The recline was honestly quite generous, too, for a thin, low-cost airline seat like this. Landing was 15 minutes early, and after passing immigration, which took less than 30 seconds, my bags were already on the belt. The only other minus from this flight was that ScootHub, their Wi-Fi, did not work whatsoever, but that was no big deal since this was only a 2-hour flight. Aside from that, and the ground staff at Yogyakarta, I would say Scoot knows how to produce a memorable flight, especially a low-cost but fun one of that.

I experienced a significant disruption on an Air Canada flight in December 2025 due to adverse weather. I understand that safety comes first and that weather is outside an airline’s control, the disruption caused my three international connecting flights to be cancelled and rebooked, resulting in a delay of three days and causing substantial inconvenience and stress. Customer service communication was polite, but no goodwill gesture was offered despite the length of the delay. I was disappointed by the lack of flexibility in handling such an extended disruption. I hope Air Canada will consider more customer-centric goodwill practices for situations involving prolonged delays, even when they are caused by weather.

Singapore to Seattle via Tokyo Haneda. ANA's service on the ground and in the air was perfect from start to finish., I was able to check in online a day before, and that resulted in me having more time to sleep and relax in Singapore. When I arrived the next day, I simply needed to reprint my boarding pass and drop my bag, all of which involved kiosks and a computerized process. While I was familiar with it, not even 2 steps in, the Changi ground staff members jumped into my assistance with a very helpful and professional attitude. The temperature control was so much better than my previous 2 flights, while the cleanliness and condition of the cabin was pristine. The seat had improved back padding. I got a full row to myself, allowing me to sleep as if the seats were my couch, even though the legroom was generous and the seat had a footrest. Meals were beautifully presented and divine in taste. The IFE was the same, old, but loaded and responsive IFE TV with a slightly inefficient layout. A horizontal list would've been nicer with the amount of contents they have. The Wi-Fi was fast and responsive. The crew were energetic, cheerful and easy to talk with, and orchestrated two surprises for me upon realizing this was my 3rd flight on ANA. They served me a chocolate cake and a selection of chocolates 45 minutes before landing, still with a hand-glazed thank you message.  The second flight to Seattle was more crowded, however, the same friendly and polite service remained . They handed me several souvenirs nearing the conclusion of the flight. The Wi-Fi and in-flight entertainment remained consistent, and the seat was equally comfortable. The cabin was clean and in good condition as well, but the temperature control was so hots. The meal  texture-wise, lackluster compared to my Singapore-Haneda leg. The chicken curry could have used more sauce and alternative cooking techniques so that the breading would not be soggy. The sandwich's bun was very tough and rough to eat, which was a shame because both dishes actually tasted rich. I appreciate how ANA varied the Häagen-Dazs flavors on both flights. Baggage took less than 10 minutes to arrive in Seattle.

Seattle to Dallas onboard one of their younger Boeing 737 MAX 9. I checked in around 12 hours before the flight, and after clearing immigration, I went to the dedicated check-in counters for transit passengers. After rechecking my baggage, I went to my gate using the Seattle Underground and the process only took 37 minutes from the moment I disembarked my previous international flight to reach the N gates. All the ground staff members, both in Seattle and Dallas, seemed to be in a very upbeat mood after the New Year. Boarding started on time, and considering the flight was only 37% full, there were so many empty seats that boarding finished very quickly. I was welcomed enthusiastically by the cabin crews, and a pristine and comfortable cabin. Being in a preferred seat, I had access to two (USB-A and a normal 110V) power plugs, a tablet holder, literature pockets, and an easy-to-operate seat. The slimline design of the seat meant that what was advertised as 31" legroom felt like 32"-33". I got the whole row to myself, and I experienced one of the best short naps on this flight. Despite being delayed for deicing, we managed to make up the time in the air. The pre-booked Chicken Salsa Verde was one of the most delicious Latin American cuisines I have tasted on the plane, although less corn would be more appreciated. It was presented nicely, and the taste enhanced the presentation. I was also served several snacks alongside it, plus three rounds of drinks, which was very generous of Alaska. The Wi-Fi entertainment was very stable, even when I tried watching Full HD YouTube videos. It had plenty of contents laid out in a tidy manner. The crews were  very energetic, cheerful, friendly, and well-mannered. I was given a chocolate bar and a thank-you message from them. They were also conveying their instructions firmly but politely, including when I had no idea that cameras count as larger electronic devices that must be stowed. Upon arrival my bag only took 10 minutes from the promised 20 minutes to arrive. It seems like since they merged with Hawaiian, they improved the service attitude, soft product, and hard product altogether; I can safely say they are my favorite US carrier for domestic routes, and I am looking forward to my next Alaska flight!

I have taken Breeze many many times between Pittsburgh to Raleigh to see my grandchildren and have loved the airlines. They are clean and have ample room, much better than Spirit. As for customer service, forget it. I had to add on my granddaughter recently so that she could come back with me for a week. It took over an hour to settle everything. I ended up with a major headache. No matter how frustrated I got I was not allowed to speak to someone by telephone. I used the Live Chat. I was happy to know that I did not have to cancel my reservation and rebook because the rates had gone up, but could book a separate one and they could link hers to mine. Well the joy was short lived. They set it up so that I could go into my account and click on the booking which was now available and just pay. So the chat person stayed in the chat while I tried. This would go on and on at this point. I tried numerous times and it did not go through, I went back and forth with the agent trying and retrying. She asked me to do many different things to make it work. This went on for an hour. I begged to talk to a person on the phone, but was ignored. Finally she said that they did something on their end end to try again. It finally worked. I wish we could go back to the day when you could actually talk to someone live on the telephone.

We had a holiday planned from 10 to 15 January on the route Larnaca – Male via Abu Dhabi. We booked separate tickets: Larnaca–Abu Dhabi return with Wizz Air, and Abu Dhabi–Male return with Etihad (our first time flying Etihad). On 10 January, just as we were leaving our home to start the trip, we received a message that our Abu Dhabi–Male flight was delayed by 24 hours and moved to 11 January.
