This meant we immediately lost one full day of our very expensive Maldives vacation. After arriving in Abu Dhabi, we went to the Etihad Travel Desk. We spent around three hours speaking to a manager. We were told we were entitled to a hotel for one night and a small compensation. I specifically asked if we could rebook our return flights, because our holiday dates were fixed and we were losing a day. The manager said it was possible, but refused to do it at that moment, explaining that a long queue had formed behind us and he had to assist other passengers as well. We were taken by bus to the hotel. The next day (Sunday), we tried to find an open Etihad office in Abu Dhabi, but could not. At the airport, the queues were so long that we could not wait for our turn because we had to depart. We flew to the Maldives. There was no Etihad office there either. To avoid losing another day, we rebooked our return for 16 January instead of 15 January. As a result, we had to buy new tickets at our own expense: Male–Abu Dhabi and Abu Dhabi–Larnaca. I contacted Etihad customer support and explained the situation, including the overbooking and the fact that we had to pay for new return flights ourselves because the Travel Desk did not help when we asked. The response was extremely disappointing: Etihad refused any reimbursement, stating that the issue should have been solved at the Travel Desk. When I explained that the manager refused to assist at that time, I was told nothing could be done. This was a very stressful experience and a complete lack of customer care. I rate Etihad 1/10 and I will not fly with them again.

Slow boarding at Sao Paolo. Boarding groups 2 and 3 were made to line up in one line, losing the distinction between the two groups. Onboard the cabin crew expect the passengers to close the overhead cabin luggage compartments themselves (some airlines where the crew do that after boarding is completed). Pushback was delayed due to loading of the cargo hold. After take off, there was a long delay before dinner was served. The food was good but portions were too small. Service was ok and crew were professional and spoke Portuguese and English fluently (and sometimes Spanish). Good communication from the cockpit at the start and end of the flight. No food available again till an hour before landing. The condition of the cabin was generally good. Excellent IFE system. Toilet floor was messy and there is an asymmetric number of toilets on the left and right side of the aircraft. The seat of the person sitting in front of me had a fault meaning it would lean back to the maximum whenever he lent back even without him pushing the recline button. (He apologised even though it wasn’t his fault). The flight landed 45 minutes late due to late departure from Sao Paolo, and luggage took a very long time to come out on the conveyor belt at Heathrow. However, all luggage arrived safely and so did we, so overall the flight served its purpose pretty well and I would feel comfortable repeating this journey with this airline.

Seattle to Dallas onboard one of their younger Boeing 737 MAX 9. I checked in around 12 hours before the flight, and after clearing immigration, I went to the dedicated check-in counters for transit passengers. After rechecking my baggage, I went to my gate using the Seattle Underground and the process only took 37 minutes from the moment I disembarked my previous international flight to reach the N gates. All the ground staff members, both in Seattle and Dallas, seemed to be in a very upbeat mood after the New Year. Boarding started on time, and considering the flight was only 37% full, there were so many empty seats that boarding finished very quickly. I was welcomed enthusiastically by the cabin crews, and a pristine and comfortable cabin. Being in a preferred seat, I had access to two (USB-A and a normal 110V) power plugs, a tablet holder, literature pockets, and an easy-to-operate seat. The slimline design of the seat meant that what was advertised as 31" legroom felt like 32"-33". I got the whole row to myself, and I experienced one of the best short naps on this flight. Despite being delayed for deicing, we managed to make up the time in the air. The pre-booked Chicken Salsa Verde was one of the most delicious Latin American cuisines I have tasted on the plane, although less corn would be more appreciated. It was presented nicely, and the taste enhanced the presentation. I was also served several snacks alongside it, plus three rounds of drinks, which was very generous of Alaska. The Wi-Fi entertainment was very stable, even when I tried watching Full HD YouTube videos. It had plenty of contents laid out in a tidy manner. The crews were  very energetic, cheerful, friendly, and well-mannered. I was given a chocolate bar and a thank-you message from them. They were also conveying their instructions firmly but politely, including when I had no idea that cameras count as larger electronic devices that must be stowed. Upon arrival my bag only took 10 minutes from the promised 20 minutes to arrive. It seems like since they merged with Hawaiian, they improved the service attitude, soft product, and hard product altogether; I can safely say they are my favorite US carrier for domestic routes, and I am looking forward to my next Alaska flight!

The flights in Business class were full but the crew were excellent and attentive. The food on the Dubai to Birmingham flight was excellent, a starter of prawn, scallop and fennel and main of trout. Excellent service which must be down to the Cabin Managers who have my compliments

Check in at Colombo was quick and there is a priority immigration queue at Colombo that saves a bit of time. Emirates Lounge is of a decent size and is comfortable, with a reasonable choice of food. Flight to Dubai was on a refurbished B777 with the new seating, very comfortable. We chose the smoked salmon starter and roast chicken as the main, genuinely nice. Flight had Wi-Fi onboard but not the latest StarLink and service was a bit unstable. Due to congestion we were 45 minutes late into Dubai. This meant a very tight transit in Dubai. At the time of booking our trip the leg from Dubai to London Gatwick was on an A380, unfortunately Emirates changed the aircraft to a B777 two weeks before travel but did not have the courtesy to advise the passengers, This aircraft was the older config B777 (some 20 years old) with the 3 seats in the middle business class. Whilst I understand Emirates right to change the aircraft type, this was a big step down compared with our expectation of comfort and service, which we had paid for. Their failure to communicate the change was disappointing. The disappointment didn’t end there as the aircraft then suffered a recurring technical issue, which meant the flight was almost 4 hours late departing and almost 3 hours late arriving into Gatwick. These things happen and you must accept this, however frustrating! The service provided by the crew was brilliant and whilst we were on the ground and we got airborne, they were very attentive and the meal and drink service was very good.

Check in at LGW was quick and easy. Flight to Dubai was on an A380, which we prefer to the B777. My wife and I had seats 9E and 9F, which are the middle ‘honeymoon’ seats!. Service was very slick with a good cabin crew. We both chose the beef fillet as the main course, which was tender and juicy. Flight was uneventful with no turbulence. Toilets kept clean and nice to enjoy the bar at the rear of the cabin. Flight landed ahead of schedule. Transit through Dubai was easy with minimal queuing at Transit security. Connecting flight from Dubai to Colombo was on a refurbished B777. We had seats 5E and 5F, very comfortable and the overall ambience on the cabin was very nice. Aircraft was fitted with StarLink so super stable and free Wi-Fi available, very impressive. Flight was only 4 hours, so we didn’t bother with the cooked breakfast offered, so just had the fruits and pastries prior to landing on Colombo. Flight arrived slightly ahead of schedule, immigration was quick and the bags were already on the belt! Overall, very good job by Emirates.

I couldn’t emphasize enough how much we love Mark his supervisor and the crew was very energetic and welcoming, but he made the entire process so incredibly easy, professional fun and he helped so much! He’s got the best smile and responses

Hanoi to Munich on 21st January 2026 in Premium Economy. The flight was delayed by approximately 8 hours due to technical issues. Passengers were required to remain on board the aircraft for nearly 5 hours, followed by an additional 3 hours waiting at the gate after deboarding, resulting in an overnight stay at Hanoi Airport. During this delay, no hotel accommodation, rest facilities, or adequate assistance were provided. I am still awaiting for a fair resolution.

I traveled with Turkish Airlines on a journey consisting of 4 flights, along with my family (2 adults, 2 children, and 1 infant). Unfortunately, the overall experience was quite disappointing. The biggest issue was that we were assigned seats in the last row of the aircraft with children. Airlines should show basic consideration and provide more suitable seating for families. To make matters worse, on one of the flights, our seats were not even in the same row, which made managing children even more difficult during the journey. Overall, this was not a family-friendly experience, and based on this journey, I would seriously reconsider choosing Turkish Airlines for future travel with my family.

This trip from start to finish was horrible. First flight from Narita on Hawaiian was delayed several hours. The food was horrible in route, and there was no wifi as well. When we finally arrived at Seattle, we then sat on the tarmac for a prolonged period before we could deboard the plane. The second leg, on Alaska, was then also delayed 2.5 hours as well, unrelated to the first HAWAIIAN delay in Narita. Overall flight experience was terrible, fares are too expensive ensure such discomfort and disruption of people’s lives.

On the ground all good, efficient and early lounge access for silver and above. Seats very cramped in economy. I’m not tall and it wasn’t great. Food service basic with little finesse but it’s a short flight  Crew are fast and efficient but don’t have the hospitality you’d get on some airlines.

Avoid the BA Cityflyer Embraers Flew from STN to FLR on Feb 8. Funny smell on the plane, which was quite unpleasant, seats rock hard and don't recline, limited legspace. The only plus points of the flight was the very cheap price, getting airbridged onto the plane (a rarity at Stansted) and the friendly enough crew. Also, these Embraers are based at London City.

I sometimes wonder of the veracity of some over praiseworthy reviews, or were we just unlucky? Our our Manchester to Dubai flight business class was atrocious, we were stuck in the middle two of three centre business class seats - most airlines premium economy is better than this, and the plane was tired and fixtures worn and tatty. Service was abrupt and staff disappeared into the kitchens and stayed there for most of the flight. The food was okay, at BA standard from my recent trips with them. Luckily our transfer in Dubai was fairly brief, because it is an awful place. Our trip in April to Thailand is with Qatar Airways, who are a very long way ahead of Emirates in my experience - a bit like comparing Waitrose with Lidl.

Extremely unhappy having discovered the Finnair changed the aircraft from London to Helsinki next week from the A350 to an A321. Finnair claims it is within their rights to do this and are refusing to change my booking. Finnair is misselling their advertised product and has no interest in fulfilling its promise to customers.

For the return flight back to Kolkata,  the check in was at T2. Even though the queues at baggage drop were long, it was well managed. The departure was slightly delayed by 30 mins due to the late arrival of the incoming aircraft. For this flight also the loads were on the full side. Thankfully we were able to make up for the lost time en route. Landing into CCU was timely and the crew seemed professional.

Initially when I had booked this flight it was supposed to land at T2 terminal, however due to a flight change it was scheduled to land at T1 instead but with the same timings. Online check in was smooth and I had also pre booked a paneer sandwich along with tea for this flight. Boarding and Baggage drop at CCU airport was fine and timely. The crew was also attentive to the fact to not serve hot beverages during turbulence. Arrival and baggage collection was swift and timely. Overall a pretty routine flight which was on time.

Good flight. Departed and arrived on time. A light lunch was served but the portion was a little too small. On-demand entertainment was available via own devices through plane WiFi. A good range of movies and TV shows in English. Surprisingly poorer selection of Spanish and Portuguese language original productions, despite the home continent of the airline. Cabin crew were very friendly and helpful. The seat pitch was a little tight but no different to that of other airlines for flights of a similar length. Queue cutting during boarding was annoying and nothing was done by staff to stop it. Priority boarding was irrelevant given we all went on the same bus to reach the aircraft to board via stairs. Disembarkation via aero bridge was efficient.

My daughter and I travelled on a Thai Airways Boeing 777-200ER(77E) from Chengdu to Bangkok and back. Both flights were more than wonderful. The seats were comfortable, with ample legroom. The cabin crew on both flights were very polite and friendly, spoke fluent English, and the service was outstanding. Something happened that astonished me and that I had never encountered during my numerous travels around the world on different airlines: During our first flight from China to Thailand, we were travelling in economy class. When it was time for our meal, they offered us a variety of options. My daughter and I chose chicken, but because we were seated at the back of the plane, the economy class chicken meals had run out. The flight crew apologized and asked us to wait a few minutes. After a few minutes, the cabin crew supervisor came, apologized, and brought us chicken from the first-class kitchen. This was wonderful and a pleasant surprise, demonstrating the professionalism of the flight crew. Thank you for such outstanding service!
Punctual, pleasant, excellent onboard service and reasonably priced. Its one of my favourite company, every year repeat our flys and always the same good service

This trip from start to finish was horrible. First flight from Narita on Hawaiian was delayed several hours. The food was horrible in route, and there was no wifi as well. When we finally arrived at Seattle, we then sat on the tarmac for a prolonged period before we could deboard the plane. The second leg, on Alaska, was then also delayed 2.5 hours as well, unrelated to the first HAWAIIAN delay in Narita. Overall flight experience was terrible, fares are too expensive ensure such discomfort and disruption of people’s lives.
Avelo has very unprofessional staff and zero customer support.  It's not worth taking Avelo for the low sticker price, because you will pay in so many other ways.

It was a good solid business class product with a few minor issues. First leg LHR to VIE on a A320Neo. Crew and food were excellent but as always the inter European business class seat leaves a lot to be desired even on the these shorter flight and more annoyingly there was no WiFi at all on the flight, not even the internal for entertainment was working. The lounge in Vienna leaves some to be desired, especially the hot food selection was poor and while it was a nice touch to have someone serving it, the portions were very small. I believe Austrian is working on a new lounge which is not a moment too soon. Second leg from VIE to BKK on a B777-200. Again the crew were excellent, food good and service after take off was speedy to get people ready for sleep. Apparently you can pre-order your food on their website but they keep that very quiet. The seat was comfortable but very dated and the cabin is screaming for a refresh. Austrian have new 787's coming but they are hand downs from Lufthansa . Again WiFi was absent, a big miss from Austrian. All in all a solid flight given the price point but there is room for improvement.

Business Check-in was a bit of a trek from the metro station, but I appreciated the priority tags and also my ski bag being taken from the check-in counter, rather than me having to drag it to the other side of the terminal. Emirates have organised their lounges so they're above the gate you leave from. The lounge had a good array of foods for breakfast. I was pretty annoyed that they didn't give us a jetbridge to board, but bus instead.  On board the crew spoilt us, meals were beautifully presented and they tasted great and there was an array of snacks available. The seats were not the refurbished seats, but were still very comfortable. The cabin was only about 1/2 full, so plenty of room to move around. We were delayed in immigration at Denpasar due to me not following the correct procedure with the airport tax and our bags were waiting for us at the carousel. I'll definitely give Emirates another go.

Robert and Nancy at DFW went above and beyond in exceeding expectations for a much needed flight change for our teenage daughter. I sent a desperate email on Saturday (02/14) to change my daughters flight from Monday to Sunday after we unfortunately made the mistake of purchasing a non changeable or refundable flight. They both took time out of their day to help assist and avoid hardship for our family. I never expected to receive a call from Ms. Nancy on Saturday, especially when I didn’t even leave my cell number in the email. She jumped several hurdles to reach me, and I will be forever grateful and touched by the efforts of these two individuals. Thank you for your kindness, support and grace after it was clearly our mistake. We will be sure to pay for the extra changeable ticket in the future, but will never forget the generosity you showed. I will continue to speak your praises to anyone I see.

Nothing worked on this flight: customer service (online and live), unfortunately this airline has gone downhill over the years. Their "automatic" systems do not work and you are unable to reserve seats, meals, luggage etc. They sent twice wrong payment link of services reserved on phone (customer service), they wanted me to pay the flights twice etc.

I was able to avoid the self check-ins and find staff to check our bags in. He argued with us that we were over our weight limit, even though we were entitled to 2 bags at 23kg each and our ski equipment. He instructed me to repack the bags, which worked out better for me in the end, making my ski bag lighter, but weightwise - made no difference to Finnair. Onboard the A321 to Helsinki, the cabin and seat pitch felt very cramped, but the flight went quickly. The crew onboard were welcoming and friendly. We used the lounge between flights. The food and drinks were pretty good, but the lounge had no windows and the toilets weren't particularly clean. The crew on the A350 (OH-LWB) weren't particularly friendly to me, apart from a Japanese crew member, but they did their jobs. The meals were acceptable, but I didn't think the curry was the best choice. The entertainment was good enough, but I spent most of the flight following our journey looking out the windows at the scenery. The seat was comfortable enough for the 6 hour flight. It was a bit of a long trek to immigration and the baggage belt at Dubai and my ski bag took a considerable amount of time (over 1 hour) to turn up.

I travelled on a single FlyDubai ticket (Yerevan – Dubai – Colombo). I arrived in Dubai at 14:40. My connecting flight was at 02:15. I was present at the gate until 02:10. No boarding call was made. A staff member confirmed the aircraft had not departed yet. Despite this, FlyDubai later stated that all passengers had boarded and refused any rebooking or reimbursement. I was forced to purchase a replacement ticket for USD 640. Multiple attempts through customer care and even visiting their office in Armenia resulted in the same refusal. I am sharing this experience so that other passengers understand how missed connections are handled.

Garuda Indonesia completely ruined the start of our family holiday. Our flight was delayed three times in one day, wiping out the entire first half of our carefully planned trip and turning what should have been an exciting start into hours of stress and frustration. Even worse was how it was handled. The response was slow, disorganized, and frankly pathetic. Staff appeared to deliberately slow the process and tried to palm the situation off rather than take responsibility. Communication was poor, there was no urgency, and no real care shown toward affected passengers. For a national carrier, the service was shockingly disappointing.

They’re absolutely ridiculous. Cancelling a flight with less than 24 hours’ notice leaves passengers with virtually no realistic options — you’re stuck scrambling for expensive last-minute alternatives, or you miss your plans entirely. What makes it worse is the domino effect: hotels, tours, meetings, connecting flights, airport transfers — all of it can become non-refundable or massively more expensive to change. So you don’t just lose a seat on a plane, you lose money, time, energy, and you’re left dealing with the stress and disruption they created.  Reliability matters when people plan around a flight, and based on my experience, this airline simply isn’t dependable. I wouldn’t book with them again unless there was absolutely no other choice.

I wanted to add an extra bag and called customer service they said no problem, Silver members can bring up to three pieces. At the airport I am told the last leg is not included and need to pay US$100 because is operated by a oneworld partner (latam). Partners website says is only $25. I asked if I could see why is it $100 and I am told by staff this information cannot be shown to customers. If only we had more options in Australia! Food is usually alright

There was a gate change that staff at Denpasar didn't bother to tell passengers about - I found out by chance, so I took it upon myself to let everyone in the original gate know about the gate change. The new Group boarding system which I was pretty sceptical about works pretty well. We were on VH-EBA, Qantas' original A330-200. The seats were comfortable enough, but = a bit worn out. Cabin crew weren't particularly warm, but did their job. I was not impressed with the fact that Qantas have taken out the IFE replacing it with a tablet. Meals were adequate, but I hate the wooden disposable cutlery economy passengers are given. The flight to Albury was on a Q400. We departed and arrived on time, the seat comfort was adequate for a 45min - 1hr flight, but they may as well not have bothered with the snack - a miniscule packet of chips. While we were waiting for our bags, I observed a baggage handler abusing bags he was taking out of the hold (including 2 of mine). He threw them a good 1m distance, grabbed them by the wheels. I spoke to the gate agent and complained. She went out and spoke to "Tweedle Dumb" about the issue and he began handling the bags correctly until she left then went back to his old ways. As soon as my bags I checked the contents and luckily nothing was damaged (my skis also). I put in a complaint to the company, but have not received a response. I'm done with Qantas - I'm not going to stay faithful to them again. Qantas are only interested in their Platinum members now.

We arrived to the domestic airport 59 minutes before departure, and they not only would not let us on our flight, but charged us full price for another flight.,This after last time we travelled with them, they moved our flight time twice, causing us to have to change vacation plans. The agent was extremely rude and laughed about the situation.

We were told to arrive 3 hours early to pay a reduced overweight baggage fee. We arrived early but could not find or access the required counter, were directed to long check-in lines, and were charged a large fee. On a second flight, we followed instructions to arrive early but the counter was closed. The airline’s response was inconsistent with their own signage and instructions. They also damaged our luggage and offered us $20 for the damage. Overall very poor experience with Thaivietjet. They don't care about their customers at all. The staff are extremely unfriendly. We will never fly with them again.

What should have been a routine domestic flight turned into an display of disrespect and hostility by a member of the cabin crew. I was seated in the aisle next to a friendly couple. During beverage and snack service, they needed to use the washroom. One of the flight attendants serving snacks and drinks instructed them to use the bathrooms at the front of the plane so they wouldn’t get stuck behind the beverage cart. They said thank you and followed her instructions. The woman was allowed to use the front washroom without issue. The man — her partner — was abruptly stopped and told he was not allowed to use the front washroom and had to walk to the back of the plane instead. There was no explanation just a dismissive refusal.  When we landed and began deplaning, the female partner attempted to calmly address the issue with the flight attendant. Instead of showing professionalism or basic customer service, the FA responded “Keep walking. File a complaint if you want. I don’t care.” After this experience, I will think twice before choosing WestJet again.

Ridiculous rules. I tried to check in online, it didnt allow me. I had a long time at ICN airport and would like to relax at a lounge. I had no checked bags. I tried to check in at the counter but they didnt allow me, saying i had to wait until 3 hours to flight departure. I just wanted a simple check in! Unbelievable bad will.

Brussels Airlines is the worst flying experience and worst customer service experience of my life.  On my simple flight to Prague I experienced delays on both ends, each delay being as long as the flight was supposed to be. Furthermore, on my return leg I called the airline help number to ask about the probable delay, as it was 10 minutes to boarding time and no gate had been assigned, and the agent was only able to tell me that the flight was on time and everything looked good. The flight was not on time, a few minutes later I was called to the gate and told that it was delayed. Which I already knew because I had gone to the airports information desk and been informed that the plane had not yet left Brussels. On top of this, I had the privilege of paying twice for the lack of service. When I initially booked my flight, their website reassigned my dates from February 13-16 to March 13-16, a mistake I didn’t not catch until the night before my trip in February. There was the same flight available, although for a higher price as it was now last minute. The customer “service” told me that there was nothing to be done when I said there had been a mistake and I was willing to pay the difference but needed a flight for the 13th of February. When I asked to speak to a supervisor I was told I would be called back within 3 hours. I waited 4 and never received any contact. I took the next step, as per their customer “service” guidelines, and submitted proof that I had searched for a February flight and been booked in March. No response. To sim it up simply, Brussels Airlines has failed at every single point of customer service contact. They charge for service they do not render properly and are apparently institutionally incapable of managing their own flights or providing information to customers. The only reason I flew with them for this trip was because I had no choice by the time I realized the mistake, and even so I regret it completely.

This airline is a complete bait and switch. We booked the dream class for laydown flat seats for the five hour flight home and paid higher fee. They changed the aircraft to one that didn’t even have leg rest, no TVs, no Internet and absolutely no amenities like to dream seats and I requested the fair difference back. As a matter of fact, we couldn’t even get a pillow. Of course, they refused saying it was their prerogative to change the aircraft at any time and they don’t have to to compensate the difference even through their website, clearly outlines this as a circumstance where alike product was not provided and they should do a fair difference refund. Buyer beware this is a bait and switch.

Quick check in at Mumbai airport, with a friendly check in agent. No fast track seemed to be present at the airport and nothing was said at check in but security and immigration were both very quick. The lounge at Mumbai is a generic airport lounge used by all airlines. It’s actually fairly good, and being there for breakfast there were various Indian and international options, including an egg station for made to order eggs/omlettes, which was a really good option. Alcohol wise it wasn’t great, with the lounge offering fairly limited or poor options but providing a menu where you can pay for better quality products… the free wine offerings were pretty disgusting (and I’m not very fussy). The staff in the lounge are very attentive and will take orders at your seat for some food and drink options. Boarding was very quick and efficient. Welcome drink was only water/OJ apparently due to Indian regulations preventing them serving alcohol on the ground. Flight was very good as is consistent with my experience on club suite. Food was beautifully presented although the crab starter had very little flavour. Between the meal service and access to club kitchen I was well catered for. I particularly like the club kitchen for being able to grab a drink or a snack between meal service without having to bother the crew. Bathrooms stayed fairly clean through the flight. Outstanding cabin crew, Kelly, showed the very best of BA crew .. professional, efficient whilst also friendly, helpful and personable. I used the free messaging WiFi connectivity for club members.. it worked for basic messaging but picture messaging was apparently too much for it. I didn’t test the paid WiFi options. IFE offered a good selection but resolution of the video on the screen was fairly poor, and weirdly different to my outbound flight I could not find a search function for shows/films so had to look through the various lists to try to see the full content. The seat was really comfortable as always, as this was a day flight I didn’t attempt any sleep although I relaxed in various lounging positions very nicely. On the ground in Heathrow things were fairly tainted by the exceptionally slow return of luggage. Some bags started soon after the passengers reached the belt then there were sporadic additions of new bags every now and again with my priority bag coming about an hour after landing… approx 75% of the passengers still seemed to be waiting for their bags when I left.

I had an involuntary downgrade from Business to economy class, and promised a refund after my flight and was basically told 'please contact customer service after your flight to process your refund'- I did not raise any issues here as I tried to understand that they may have overbooked etc, as long as I got my refund. When I contacted them, I was intially tossed around and told to apply for a refund via the booking agency I booked the flight through. I did that and next thing they say is they cannot issue a refund because "the booking class you purchased corresponds to our full Economy Class fare, and as such, no refund is applicable for the ticket". How is business class fare equals to economy, you can simpy check on line and and see it is different- I checked it for the very flight I flew. I have been offered vouchers which I do not want. This company provides false information and false assurances or compensation. Very difficult to get a hold of I feel taken advantage of and very upset considering how hard I work to pay for the services I pay for. If you value your money, would like to be treated with an ounce of dignity, please avoid at all costs

I am extremely disappointed with the way my pre-purchased baggage allowance issue was handled by Singapore Airlines, resulting in double payment for the same baggage and weeks of unhelpful, repetitive responses. 7 December 2025: Purchased an additional 10 kg baggage allowance for AUD 419. I received a receipt and was assured by customer service that the allowance had been added to my ticket. Contacted customer service again, who reconfirmed that the allowance was successfully added and that my receipt would serve as proof at check-in. 12 January 2026 – Melbourne Airport: At check-in, my ticket reflected only the base 30 kg allowance. Despite presenting my receipt for the extra 10 kg, the ground staff were unable to locate the additional baggage in the system. I was directed to the service desk, where, after waiting two hours, I was told I had five minutes to either pay again for excess baggage or throw out my belongings because the counter was about to close. Under pressure and the stress of potentially missing my flight, I paid AUD 582.05 for 8 kg of excess baggage.  Post-flight (Singapore): I contacted customer service, submitted receipts and bank statements, and an inquiry was raised.  19 January 2026: Received an email offering a refund of only AUD 419 (the pre-purchased baggage), but not the AUD 582.05 paid at the airport.  Responded expressing dissatisfaction and requested for a reevaluation of my case.  21 January 2026: Received another email stating that the AUD 582.05 could not be refunded because it was “utilised for the excess baggage carried.” I expressed my dissatisfaction. 22 January, 26 January, 2 February, 7 February 2026: Repeated follow-ups resulted in the same generic response that the case was still under review.  12 February 2026: Received another email stating that the airline was unable to refund the airport charges due to “established guidelines,” and again offering only the AUD 419 refund.  13 February 2026: I reiterated my strong dissatisfaction and am still awaiting the refund of the amount AUD 419, given the lack of resolution My Concern This situation resulted in double payment for the same baggage allowance, caused entirely by a system error or oversight by the airline. I had proof of my original purchase and had even confirmed it twice with customer service before my flight. Yet I was left with no choice but to pay again under duress at the airport. If the expectation was for me to pay the significant airport charges regardless, then there was no purpose in contacting the airline ahead of time or securing the baggage allowance in advance. Singapore Airlines’ customer service standards emphasise accuracy, accountability, and care when service failures occur. Unfortunately, none of these was demonstrated in my case. Instead, the burden of the airline’s mistake was placed entirely on me. I have only requested the amount rightfully owed to me, not compensation for the stress or inconvenience caused at the airport. Yet weeks of emails and calls later, the airline still refuses to refund the airport charge, offering only the original AUD 419. This experience has been stressful, time-consuming, and deeply disappointing — especially from an airline known for its service quality.

I cannot recommend this airline. They had a hidden subscription fee of 159.99 euros and they are not willing to refund it. Be careful before using their service because they will not send you any email or comunication about the subscription. That way, you don't realise and then they claim your money. I would recommend using a different airline.

I have flown with a dozen different airlines over the last 5 years. After multiple heart, lung and back surgeries (I am 80 years old) I always request a wheelchair from the checkin desk to the gate, and from landing to luggage and taxicab. Batik Air refused, even after seeing the heart surgery medical cards I must always carry with me. Of course for a cash payment I could request one in Bangkok (about $60 USD) and another one in Kuala Lumpur (about $50 USD). I did my best to walk, planning to arrive at the plane taking off from Bangkok at the exact time boarding commenced per my boarding pass. However, while trying to get there, taking breaks to rest, they announced final boarding! They grudgingly reopened them to let me on and told me they weren't doing anything wrong!

Easyjet informed the passengers about 1.5 hrs before the flight that they changed the airplane to a smaller one. Around 30 passengers lost their seats. Around 20 people were left behind and were offered to stay in a hotel and get another flight but not on the same day. I was lucky to get a seat but it was unfair and the process of choosing who would go and who wouldn't was totally random. So careless and badly organised. I am not flying with easyjet again, it was a terrible experience!

The worst airline experience ever. My brother is a wheelchair passenger and informed Flydubai in advance while booking. They confirmed assistance from check-in to arrival. At the airport they said if he cannot walk inside the aircraft they will refuse check-in. They refused a front seat and forced him to walk through the aircraft even after explaining his medical condition. No humanity, no responsibility, badly trained staff, and zero respect for passengers with disabilities. Completely unacceptable and unsafe.

The airline failed to deliver all three of my checked bags. Two of them were returned after a week, and the third was disposed of by customs after nine days. This happened because the frozen food inside the luggage spoiled and contaminated the bag. None of this would have occurred if my luggage had been delivered on time. The nine-day delay caused the damage. In addition to losing over 50 pounds of items, I paid $290 for the extra luggage and $80 for overweight fees  for a bag that was ultimately destroyed. I was instructed by customer service to purchase clothing and necessities while waiting for my luggage. I did so and submitted the receipts as requested. Despite all the inconvenience, financial loss, and time wasted — over 15 days of emails, uploading documents, and phone calls — the airline offered only $49 in compensation after returning two bags late and disposing of the third. This amount is unacceptable and does not reflect the seriousness of the situation.

The service, both outbound and return, was excellent. Despite the schedule changes and flight delays, which were anticipated due to the conflict in Venezuela and are beyond the airline's control, both journeys were pleasant. I would like to highlight the friendly service provided by the Arajet staff.  El servicio, tanto de ida como de vuelta, estuvo muy bien. Más allá de los cambios de hora y las demoras en los vuelos, previstos por el conflicto en Venezuela, y lo cual le es ajeno a la compañía, resultaron amenos ambos viajes. Quiero resaltar la amable atención de la gente que trabaja en Arajet.

Had an absolute nightmare getting home there a couple of months back coming home from Palma with Easyjet. Long story short, we were left there at the last airport terminal and the flight left for Belfast with our bags etc.. we have to get new flights into Dublin (after rebooking hotels and travel etc for the night were ment to fly home. Two days later we were back in Belfast and Swissport who had the bags informed me that what has happened had breached so many CAA rules and were blown away in how the bags got there without me,my wife and 2 kids. I thought the best thing was to contact Easyjet thmeselves instead of all that. I submitted a case, was given a case number and have been ignored now for months. I am disgusted to be honest. I have next years holiday booked with easyjet (done it whilst on the last) and will have to cancel that too if I dont get this resolved. To be honest, acknowledgement of some sort would probably have done at the start, but being ignored etc has me annoyed now.

Extremely disappointing experience with refund process. I was promised a refund within 45 business days for a ticket booking due to a date mismatch. It's been over 3 months with no refund or clear update despite multiple follow-ups. Customer care was unhelpful and didn't provide any concrete solution.

Very disappointing experience with Etihad Airways at the Phuket check-in counter. The service attitude was extremely unhelpful and unprofessional. The staff showed no willingness to assist or explain anything properly. This has nothing to do with the long waiting time — although the queue was the longest in the terminal with very few open counters — but everything to do with how we were treated. We were 1 kg overweight on our baggage amd were told we must pay 100 USD for excess weight. When we asked if we could remove 1 kg from the suitcase, we were told that we would need to leave the counter and rejoin the queue — meaning another 30–40 minutes of waiting. There was no flexibility, no effort to help, and no customer-oriented thinking. To make things worse, the staff members were whispering among themselves while looking at us, which felt disrespectful and unprofessional. Very disappointing customer service experience.

LEVEL cancelled our return flight without explanation and continued to change it between the day before and day after with no communication. Called customer service and they refused to do anything to help, asked if it was my first time calling then next time and hung up on me instantly, then stopped taking my calls all together. I have never experienced customer service this worthless and openly hostile. The cheaper ticket comes with a price attached - they will screw you over without end.

Check-in was quick and efficient. Friendly ground agents greeted and treated priority customers politely prior to boarding at the gate. Very professional conduct. Flight took off and landed on time. Airbridge was used at Mendoza airport for boarding but disembarkation was via stairs and bus at Sao Paolo. Inflight entertainment was available via one’s own device (phone or tablet), with only a brief disruption to it mid flight. Light lunch was provided but the portion was rather on the small side. The fittings of the aircraft interior was in good condition, toilets clean and each seat was provided with cushion and a blanket. Crew were professional and polite.

The airport experience at Gdansk Airport was nothing special. A bonus was an upgrade to an economy-comfort seat after a request at the check-in counter.  A complimentary sandwich and a variety of drinks was offered.  The seats were comfortable with charging ports, and enough space in the luggage bins. The crew are laid back, helpful, smiling and positive and made me feel welcome. The pilot announced that the flight is going to be delayed but the crew handled the situation professionally and were updating passengers with a tight connection (including myself) about the situation. A bonus was a small gift from the crew working on the flight as a compensation for my missed connection. I was rebooked on a later flight before we had arrived.

Check in chaos and bag drop took over one hour mostly due to extensive documentation checks by staff and oversized baggage. Boarding chaos and staff dealing with people in raised tone to control the volatile situation. Food main was tasty if the whole tray was rather small and main was cold (but tasty and edible). Cabin groomed to a high standard as were the staff.  I ordered a beer and it didn’t appear until a polite reminder 20 minutes later. Ticket was cheap so no real complaints. Would try again and hope for an improvement in check in and service levels.
This is the worst airline in Indonesia, delayed the flight about 8-9 hours, what a joke.
Once again a full flight meant a long boarding process. Once on board I quickly tuned in to the IFE. Good IFE options and good crew but, yet again, mediocre catering lets down the airline.

We were on time to our flight leaving Tampa-Fort Lauderdale. For some reason the flight got delayed once we had boarded. We had a connecting flight to Guatemala. When our flight arrived we ran the entire airport, made it to the gate 10 min prior to departure. Door was closed and the gate attendant said that because it was just the 2 of us they couldn't hold the plane. She sent us to re-ticketing, we were then told there was no more flights till next day and sent us off to speak to a supervisor. The system wasn't showing any delay so he said he needed to make a phone call to find out the reason, no compensation was granted. After an hour wait, an attendant at the desk went to find the supervisor who had left for lunch and forgot to inform us he had placed us on the next flight at no extra charge, yet we had to pay for a hotel. We lost over $300 in hotel and excursion in Guatemala. Not even water is free in this airline, water is over $4. On our way back our flight leaving Guatemala was delayed an hour and another 26 min on the runway in Ft Lauderdale due to staff shortage. It took us about 45 min to go through customs and another 20 min to pass TSA. Ended up missing the flight, again. We were placed in a hotel (thankfully) and booked for the 6:35 am flight. At 6:05 am, we were informed that the flight got canceled and the next one is a 7:56 pm. We had to pay $208 to get a room to at least rest since we only had 3 hours of sleep last night. Will never fly Spirit again and I would not recommend it to anybody.

Baku to Sharjah. The pre-booked meal provided onboard was satisfactory. Sharjah (SHJ) to Kuala Lumpur (KUL) The second leg of the journey involved a transition to a full flight bound for Malaysia. This overnight segment experienced intermittent turbulence throughout the flight.

Sharjah to Baku on 17 January 2026. I experienced an initial delay as the aircraft waited for a connecting flight arriving from Chennai. Although the departure was originally scheduled for 7:50 AM, the boarding process—conducted via shuttle bus—and the wait for transit passengers meant the plane only began to move at approximately 8:20 AM. Despite the late start, the flight proceeded smoothly.

Although the cabin doors were closed ahead of schedule  the flight was delayed on the tarmac due to heavy airspace congestion. The aircraft, which was at full capacity, finally pushed back at 9:57 AM and took off at 10:13 AM. The journey featured some intermittent turbulence. As the flight was around 7 hours, the plane should be a larger aircraft.

GYD to TBS on an Embraer E190—my first time flying on this specific aircraft type. The flight departed 15 minutes behind schedule. The pre-booked food, featuring a chicken shawarma that, while served cold, was tasty, accompanied by orange juice. The approach into Tbilisi, however, proved challenging due to heavy snowfall that completely obscured the runway, forcing the pilots to execute a "go-around" for safety. When the aircraft finally touched down at approximately 11:10 AM, the cabin erupted in a round of applause as passengers expressed their collective relief and gratitude for the safe arrival.

I took the flight back from Tbilisi to Baku on 21 January 2026. The flight was on the Airbus A319 which began with a bus boarding process under harsh weather conditions, as passengers contended with biting cold and strong winds on the tarmac while waiting to board. I remembered waiting for about 10 minutes to board the plane. Boarding was completed by 11:27 AM, following the aircraft's early arrival at Tbilisi, and the flight pushed back for departure at 11:31 AM. After taking off at 11:41 AM, the climb to cruising altitude was marked by some initial turbulence. The in-flight service included a pre-booked Muslim meal (MOML) consisting of chicken salami, though the experience was let down by a hard bread bun and the meal being served cold. Additionally, the seat 19A proved restrictive, as the backrest could not recline due to its proximity to the emergency exit. Despite these minor discomforts, the flight concluded with a very smooth landing at approximately 12:26 PM in Baku.

Our recent experience with British Airways was deeply disappointing and stressful — especially as we were travelling as a family with two very young children. On 18 February 2026, we flew from Brussels to Dubai via London Heathrow: BA 387 – Brussels to London BA 107 – London to Dubai From the moment of booking, I questioned whether a 1 hour 15 minute transfer time at Heathrow would be sufficient, particularly when travelling with a 4-year-old child and a 5-month-old.  Upon arrival at Heathrow, we faced long security queues No meaningful assistance for families with infants An attempt to confiscate our baby formula Security staff attempted to discard our baby’s formula, stating: “You can buy it everywhere.” After significant protest and escalation to a manager, we were eventually allowed to keep it. We l made our connecting flight to Dubai at the very last minute. Upon arrival in Dubai, we discovered that our checked luggage had not been loaded and remained in London. Since then, reaching British Airways has been extremely difficult. Communication has been unclear, and we have been repeatedly redirected without receiving a concrete solution.

I have not flown AA in several years, having moved to north Jersey and finding UA from EWR more convenient. I was very disappointed to see the deterioration of AA on both of these flights. In both cases, the aircraft were tired. The A321 in J from SEA-CLT had broken seatback pockets and seats themselves were worn. While an overnight flight departing at 9:45pm, service was even more minimal than virtually any other red eye I've flown. A small bag of chips or cookies and a beverage with no refills offered. CLT-EWR departed 7:30 AM and while just a short 2 hour flight, a breakfast hour flight in J should at least include a yogurt, fruit, sweet roll, muffin or the like. Nothing but an even smaller bag of pretzels than on the transcon SEA-CLT. Matter of fact flight attendants on both legs.The 737 was in likewise poor condition. No inflight entertainment on the A321 transcon. Gate agents pleasant enough but not seeming to go out of their way to be helpful. All in all, a very poor to mediocre flight experience far beneath what should be the standard of a major US legacy carrier. At least both legs on time. I contrast this to part of this trip on Alaska (ewr-sea-fai) and return FAI-SEA to connect with the AA. Alaska was far superior in terms of aircraft maintenance, flight crew and inflight service. Shame on AA's deterioration.

I was extremely disappointed to learn that they wanted to charge to assign an appropriate seat. Charging someone with a disability for necessary seating accommodations feels unacceptable. To make matters worse, the customer service agent was incredibly rude and dismissive. When I politely requested to speak with a manager, I was simply told “no” without any explanation or attempt to resolve the issue.

My review is mainly about my experience with the IndiGo customer service, which was a nightmare. All I wanted was to submit a retro claim for the BluChip points, which wasn’t working on my App, so I requested help. Several “issues” were “discovered”: a name mismatch (my booking contained my middle name), then an incorrect DOB on my account, which isn’t even true. My impression was that they looked for any reason they could to avoid adding those points. In over a week that they were „trying” to resolve my issue, I have received 23 emails from their service, which were basically automated repeating messages about the name mismatch, requesting my consent to add my middle name on my account by sending my ID picture, later the DOB mismatch and statements that they have detected my request running under several cases - FIVE in total - which they have had to merge again and again. Chaos and confusion. My responses via email - all six of them - have been ignored as if they never happened. Additionally, I started receiving calls from their service representatives at completely inappropriate times (IST) - past midnight or at 4:00am. I picked up the phone three times, had two conversations that didn’t resolve anything but just confirmed that their email “service” is an absolute mess - I was basically asked to send a third email with my passport ID and name change agreement, since the two previous ones “could not be found”. The calls I ended up answering were completely unnecessary, did not contribute to resolving my request and additionally, since I was in India, were chargeable. The third time I answered their call at 6:00am to basically request closing all the cases on my behalf, no one was even responding. What I learned is that IndiGo customer service is an absolute disaster; I hope to never have to deal with them ever again. While IndiGo was my preferred airline on my annual stays in India, I will be choosing the other airlines whenever possible in the future. I can not imagine what it would be like if I had to deal with them in case of flight cancellations or other related issues.

For this 3-hour flight, lunch was served. I had the Thai style chicken with rice which was delicious. Service was on a single tray due to the short duration of the flight. The seat is the fully flat reliable seat controlled by the touch screen panel. There is no need to fold down the seat back to convert to bed mode on this seat product. The inflight manager was very sociable and friendly. He came around to greet each business class passenger apologising for the late departure. The flight stewardesses were attentive and polite. WiFi was working only during the second half of the flight due to unavailability of signal. It was reasonably fast.

On 02/16/2026, we were deplaned from our original flight from Las Vegas to Tampa, via Los Angeles due to weather conditioned in LA. We boarded the original flight on group 3, and took two small, brand new Samsonite carry on bags and my purse. After deplaning, we had to change flights because my husband had to work at 6:30 am next morning. Southwest scheduled a flight back to Tampa via Saint Luis, flight WN2277, gave us from seats (7C and 9D), but placed is in group 8. We had already heard that group 7 and 8 had to check in carry on bags to final destination; thus, we begged the gate clerk to change our boarding group to 5 or 6 and allow us to bring our carry on bags. The gate clerk refused to help us, checked our brand new carry on luggage, and upon arrival in Tampa the bags were scratched, stained, marked every where. I filed a claim upon arrival in Tampa, but received an answer from Southwest indicating "they are not responsible from luggage scratches, stains, marks, and they will NOT reimburse us for the damaged luggage." Of course, we are not able to return the incorrect purchase (again, my fault) and we are stuck we two super small, damaged carry on luggages that we cannot use in the future. It only would have taken a simple act of kindness from the female gate clerk to allow us to board in an early group to prevent all this.

I took VN680 flight from Kuala Lumpur to Hanoi on 06 February 2026. Cabin was nearly at full capacity, but the service remained efficient. The pre-booked Muslim Meal (MOML) was okay; it consisted of chicken curry with long-grain rice and fresh fruit slices. The journey encountered occasional turbulence at cruising altitude. We landed at Noi Bai International Airport by 10:38 PM. The arrival was with a bus transfer to the terminal building.

I took the flight back, which was Flight VN681 from Hanoi to Kuala Lumpur on 09 February 2026. Took the bus which transferred passengers from the terminal to the plane on tarmac. The flight was under capacity. The MOML food I had onboard was barely adequate and can be improved in terms of taste and quality.

They changed my flight for 3 times and has been delayed for 20 hours resulting in waste of our time and non-refund booked accomodations. We're just off a long flight and this is a horrible transit place. The worst part is they keep on changing the gates around and take zero accountability, none of the staff want to corporate with you so they push you around to the next person. Be careful and avoid at all cost it's not worth it, just spend it on a slightly more expensive reliable airline.

Food was ok staff were good. There were a few seats on the plane broken. Paid for extra leg room seat but it would not recline. Spoke to the steward during the flight who was very helpful. He said that he would lodge a complaint with customer relations and I would get a refund for the extra I paid to select the seat since it was broken. Customer relations contacted me and said no refund would be given the plane got me to my destination. Very disappointed they don't honour what their staff say. Won't fly with them again.

I would like to give a special shout out and thank Michael of delta airlines counter staff at MCO airport for being so helpful and friendly. It means a lot to get assistance when traveling internationally and there are unfamiliar procedures and routes

On arriving at Frankfurt, I am informed my manual extension of German resident permit is not recognised in Abu Dhabi.  I wasn't able to board the flight but I met the boarding crew Alexander tried every means to help me get on the flight or at least the next one. I have never seen anyone try so hard to help someone, let alone a stranger. A gem of a person with empathy, kindness, patience, commitment and responsibility. Thank you so much Alexander, I appreciate your efforts.

I was not able to check in online as they ask for visa number of the country you are travelling to. I was going to Saudi Arabia and I was travelling for visa on arrival so I don’t have visa number. They charged us £45 each as we don’t check in online. When boarding the flight they tell me that trolley bag is not allowed and I have to pay £68.50 each bag.

I recently flew with Batik Air OD 216 and had a very disappointing experience. My seat was 1C, and boarding was supposed to be done according to zone numbers. However, they started boarding from the last zone instead, which resulted in me boarding last.  When I entered the aircraft, there was no overhead space left for my luggage.  The first flight attendant told me I had to place my bag at the back of the plane. I agreed to move my luggage, but not my backpack.  I told her I had no problem cooperating, but I needed to know exactly where to put it. She avoided eye contact and continued relaying messages through someone else. It felt dismissive and unprofessional. Eventually, another flight attendant stepped in and showed me where to place my bag. That simple act of proper communication made all the difference. During landing the plane tilted to the left, couldn’t land, and took off again. What was most concerning was the lack of clear communication from the captain. He only briefly mentioned that we couldn’t land and would attempt again. Very disappointing service from Batik Air.

This was the last leg of a trip to Dallas from Sydney via Hong Kong. Three of the prior legs were on A350 aircraft which were great. This leg was on an older B777 with older style 1-2-1 Business seating configuration. It was a slightly disappointing way to finish an otherwise great trip. The B777 unrefurbished aircraft are getting a little tired and the IFE was slow and clunky. Cabin crew were polite however seemed to lack some spark and were quite robotic. Food was pretty good however when it came to service it was hit and miss. The two main meals were served about three and a half hours apart and when it came to drinks the service was rather lacking. At no point was I asked/offered another drink after the initial service - unattentive is what I describe the service as. Overall, a disappointing final leg after three really good experiences. Whilst I’d generally recommend Cathay, avoid the older unrefurbished B777

This flight was delayed by 24 hours.  We were given a hotel overnight in SSH it wasn’t as nice as where we had stayed but was adequate. There was no transport organised to the airport leaving passengers to make their own way. The transport to the hotel - only 1 bus was organised not nearly enough for all the passengers and their luggage. No delay vouchers provided and text message to say no food for the flight home. We were then further delayed as the aircraft developed a hydraulic problem. The way BA handled this delay was appalling, no apologies or anything. The crew onboard the aircraft were friendly but clearly very young and inexperienced. In all fairness BA let them down just as much as they had no product to serve into the way home, even toilet amenities ran out. I was even more disappointed to find out 32 bags were left behind in Egypt. When we were at the carousel in LGW ours being 1 of them. Based on the service from this BA flight alone I would avoid BA at all costs. You will get a better service from Jet2 or EasyJet who are more geared up towards this type of flying. The BA Club is now ridiculous too. Unless you’re a Gold which is unachievable for anyone who doesn’t fly regularly or isn’t super rich. Just a shame to see the airline that this has become.

The airline exceeded my expectations, friendly staff on the ground and in the sky.  We also have slight overweight for the checked luggage but the staff didn't notice it. I flew for the first time with them but will use TUI Fly again. I didn't use the flight as pre-booked package, but rather like a normal airline.

Domestic flying in the US is, in general, the pits. It is a reminder of just how basic the air transport product has become. That said, our flight from San Francisco to Boston on United was tolerable. As a Star Gold member, we were able to score exit row seats which had generous legroom. The crew, however, was superb. The flight was not full and they took on the job of reseating people who were in cramped rows or middle seats, which I found both thoughtful and helpful were constantly in the cabin and provided multiple offerings of drinks and snacks. Overall, they made the long flight both comfortable and well supplied with goodies(such as they were). Most importantly, they kept a positive atmosphere in the cabin. So, within the confines of current day standards, they provided a satisfactory experience.
