Another delayed flight and missed connection. Each of my last four flights with American Airlines / American Eagle has been delayed or canceled. None due to weather. Zero assistance from American for lodging, meals or transportation for canceled or missed connections due to delays.

Etihad’s A380 has inconsistent service standards on Indian subcontinent routes. If you are flying for the seat, you will be happy. If you are flying for a seamless, premium end-to-end journey, you may find the inconsistencies and upselling frustrating. On the YYZ–AUH leg, the cabin was exceptionally quiet, spacious, and the crew was highly efficient. However, the experience becomes fragmented on regional legs (AUH–COK). Service quality dipped significantly, and one crew member lacked the basic professional tact and sensitivity expected in a premium cabin. Beyond service, two major drawbacks hinder the experience. Compared to other major carriers, the Etihad app is insufficient. It lacks essential real-time luggage tracking, which is a standard expectation in 2026. Despite holding a premium Business Class ticket, the airline continues to play "upsell games" for seat selection. This nickel-and-diming is a low-cost carrier tactic that devalues their brand. While check-in at YYZ was straightforward, the boarding process in Abu Dhabi remains disorganized and needs streamlining to match the quality of the new Terminal A.

This flight reinforced a growing concern about product dilution. Ground handling was disorganized, with a last-minute change to the furthest gate, followed by boarding via rear stairs. An unusual experience for an airline previously positioned as 5-star. For a 2.3 million IDR ticket, one expects a certain baseline of premium consistency. Upon arrival at CGK Terminal 3, the aircraft was again parked at one of the furthest stands, resulting in a notably long walk to baggage claim. The absence of seatback IFE persists, replaced by wireless entertainment that triggered an untrusted Sectigo SSL security warning every 20 to 30 seconds — hardly confidence inspiring. Catering remains unchanged with the predictable fish-or-chicken selection, offering little variation. Garuda Indonesia overall delivery increasingly resembles a lower-cost operator rather than a premium flag carrier.

Cabin crew were genuinely warm, attentive, and professional, which remains the strongest asset. Ground service was functional but unremarkable. What continues to undermine the experience is the absence of seatback IFE, replaced only by wireless streaming — a setup that feels distinctly below expectations.  The meal was good, with the fish option well prepared and enjoyable, but beyond catering and crew, the overall hard product increasingly feels average rather than premium.

I’m not even sure this airline exists. I think it must be running a scam. I booked flights through lastminute.com and straight away became suspicious when I couldn’t access anything other than the corporate website for PAS which has no booking check/online check in facility. I emailed and got no reply. Tried to call and the line was dead. I thought ok, I’ll check in at the airport. I received no communication in the interim from PAS or lastminute. I turned up at the airport and there was no check in desk, and no mention at all of the flight on the departure board. It had disappeared. No PAS presence whatsoever. There was no one else to ask. A rep from a Nile cruise operator kindly helped us confirm that the flight was no where to be found. I tried to contact PAS and lastminute with no success. Because we had a boat to catch in Aswan, we decided to book flights with another airline at short notice to get to Aswan on time. Whilst boarding that flight, lastminute told us PAS had changed not just the flight time, but the airline, the flight time and the flight number and we had not been informed by either them nor lastminute. Lastminute is blaming PAS, PAS are not even answering emails or calls.

The aircraft was questionable. it looked like it needed repairs done, inside of the cabin was falling apart and one of the overhead baggage compartments didn't close properly. The PA system used by the hostess had issues and we could not hear her at all. The aircraft was loud, unlike anything we had heard before, the entire flight of 1.5 hours was agony. Seatbelts aren't as long as on standard aircraft, as myself and my friend have no issues on those, however on this aircraft they don't fit our frames. The aisle is very narrow and the hostess bumped into my friend multiple times with the trolly. We paid a ridiculous amount for this short flight and it did not meet our expectations. Disappointed. Will not fly with them again.

Extremely poor coordination and passenger-blaming culture at SpiceJet. I arrived at the gate at 8:12 AM for an 8:45 AM flight, only to be told the gate closed at 8:05 AM. Even though their own staff guided me through security with my e-ticket, the gate staff refused to help me print a boarding pass and instead marked me as a "No Show." They tried to charge me ₹12,000 for a new flight.

My sister and I had to catch a flight from JHB to RHB. Our flight was scheduled to depart at 10:35. We reached the airport around 8:00, we immediately checked in our bags and went to have a meal. The flight board showed that our flight was delayed and scheduled to leave at 11:10. A message on my phone verified this. We finished and headed through security. We first went the wrong direction before finding out gate at around 10:30. We waited at the gate for them to call our number, but when they didn't we started getting worried and went to find an airlink employee that worked at a nearby gate. She was quite rude and said that our flight had already boarded and we had missed it. She instructed us to head back through security and to the check in counters. (I believe our flight had not yet left and if she had helped, we could have still made it.) At the check-in counters they said that the flight had then been updated to depart at 10:45, only then did an sms come through, to say that the plane was boarding, this was at around 11:00. They said they could not help us and instructed us to buy a new ticket. It turned into a very expensive trip, a late evening for those who had to fetch us on the other side. I am disappointed that Airlink was unwilling to help in any way. If the first employee had tried to contact someone, we could have made our flight. Besides this horrible experience, the second flight departed without any hiccups and the cabin crew were friendly.

Second worst airline experince of my life. Was instructed to arrive at the airport three hours before take off only to find out that they would not check us in until two hours before departure. After experiencing several gate changes and an hour-long delay out of LAX, we were informed that the wifi was inoperable. This meant that, in addition to the entertainment being shut down for a five-hour flight, there was no food or beverage service since nothing is free. (Apparently not even water). The crew couldn't be bothered to do anything to help passengers who were apparently a detriment to them enjoying themselves. The aircraft was not particularly clean and the seats are downright uncomfortable. All in all, the lack of advertising on the overhead is the only thing keeping this airline from joining Spirit at the bottom of the list. Avoid it at all costs.

Have used China Eastern to Shanghai since Virgin Atlantic stopped flying to Shanghai. Decent business class seats, food acceptable - flights comfortable and efficent. Much better costs than Emirates and direct from Gatwick or Heathrow.

A fairly horrendous experience. Our flight at 18:10 was cancelled just before 20:00. Prior to being unloaded we had to endure a cold, awful meal which I think was an attempt to save money. Left to our own devices and back to the airport the next day. You would have thought the ground crew were the victims, miserable, rude and abrupt. Having to eat the exact same meal again, which was even worse 24 hours later, was awful. The crew spent practically the whole flight chatting and catching up, and nothing in "raid the larder:. To add insult to injury our first online compensation claim was reviewed and closed with 24 hours, the second one even quicker. No promised e-mails giving us details of the outcome. I've resorted to old school tactics and sent a recorded post claim. Fingers crossed. They really don't make it easy to be liked.

We had in Nov 25 a flight with Kuwait Airways from Bangkok to Frankfurt with transfer in Kuwait City. Due to late arrival in Kuwait we have been rerouted by Kuwait Airways on a Turkish Airline flight to Frankfurt via Istanbul 14 hours later. Baggage allowance Kuwait Airways was 32 kg each. The staff at the transfer desk in Kuwait who issued the new boarding pass insisted to pay 50 KWD for 4 kg suitcase overweight or they will not load our suitcases into the aircraft. She referred Turkish Airline has on our booking class only 23 kg luggage allowance. Even we payed this unauthorized claim our 2 suitcases arrived 2 days later in Frankfurt. Since Nov I'm trying to get a refund for this 150 KWD by multiple emails but till today there is no reply.

The agent at the business class check in at Berlin airport mishandled our bags, which resulted in a great amount of stress. We checked four bags with her, and she made two mistakes,  checked two bags under the same claim number and apparently did not tag one of our bags. When I did check the claim tickets she gave me - which were stickers stuck together - I realized that she only gave us 3 tags for the 4 bags. Thus began our odyssey of trying to track our fourth bag which had special items in it. We started with the agent at the business class lounge, and she attempted to help us. Long story short, every person we spoke to along our journey - other than her - was unhelpful. We had an Apple AirTag in our bag and could show them exactly where our bag was - sitting in Berlin airport. We offered to share the tracking information with them but they refused to accept it. Then we arrive in SFO and fill out a missing bag claim with their "lost and found." That person blamed other parties and systems and was unhelpful. I acknowledge that our flights were on time and the service in the business class cabin from Munich to SFO was quite attentive and good. The wifi was incredibly slow and why they charged us for it when we already were paying an exorbitant fare I cannot understand. Eventually our bag was delivered to our home..

We have regularly flown Ryanair 3 times a year on the CGN-OPO route for the last few years, always booking priority and taking our standard carry on bags with us that fit perfectly in the overhead bins (whether on Ryanair or any other airline we fly). This last time an extremely rude female gate agent suddenly insisted that my daughter's usual carry-on was too wide. If looking very closely this was really a very borderline case as the excess width was at most 2cm. I was then forced to pay a Euro 75 fee. I don't have a problem with airlines enforcing rules with oversize cabin luggage (or weight) but it should also be within reason (i.e. allow for a minor tolerance). Importantly, it was also the manner in which I was spoken to and treated. This experience felt like pure harassment and like the agent was enjoying pulling me out of the line. I know it is company policy for the agents to receive a bonus and this was surely the lady's main motivation. However, this overzealous/unreasonable and inconsistent application of rules also leads to the airline losing customers. It did not help that after reporting this to Ryanair and following up to their pat response I received no acknowledgement or apology for the rude treatment. We will from now on go out of our way not to fly Ryanair again and choose a more customer friendly alternative.

This was the most uncomfortable flight I ever had. We flew from Cancun to Vancouver, which took about 6.5 hours. The seats were ridiculously tight, both in terms of width and length. The seats were very narrow (and we are not overweight), and you had to sit with your arms awkwardly in front of you. My spouse is kind of tall and the space was not sufficient to accommodate his legs, which made for an awkward twisted position for him. I'm less tall but even I had to shift all the time. It was not possible to recline the seats. My entire body hurt after the flight. I don't mind that they no longer provide meals on these flights because I can take my own food in the plane. But the seating situation is unacceptable and I won't use WestJet again

This is the fourth flight I have taken with easyjet and I found them to be excellent. The crews have always been friendly and efficient, the seats are comfortable and the seat pitch is OK. As long as you know what you are paying for there are no surprises or unexpected a extras. I can't rate the catering as I didn't purchase anything but from what I saw it looked like standard airline fare. I enjoyed the flights and wouldn't hesitate using easy jet again.

I recently had the pleasure of flying GA89 with Garuda Indonesia from Amsterdam to Jakarta, and the airline delivered an exceptional First Class experience I was collected from my hotel in Amsterdam and transferred to the Schiphol VIP Centre, where the VIP team handled check-in and immigration formalities within the lounge. The VIP Lounge offers an elegant and tranquil environment, with an à la carte pre-boarding dining menu and an extensive selection of premium beverages. Service was professional, warm, and attentive. I was personally escorted directly to the aircraft door, where I received a warm welcome from the outstanding First Class crew — Endang, Dressya, Ayu, and Chef Toni. Dining was available on demand, with an extensive menu. Each course was beautifully executed. Chef Toni deserves recognition for delivering cuisine that rivals fine dining on the ground. Despite arriving in Jakarta approximately 1 hour and 40 minutes behind schedule, upon landing, I was met at the aircraft door and escorted through immigration, baggage collection, and customs. A waiting car arranged by Garuda Indonesia ensured a smooth and comfortable transfer home. My sincere appreciation goes to the entire First Class team for their impeccable service and professionalism.
This was a disappointing experience because onboard Wi-Fi was not functioning during the flight, and the cabin crew did not appear to be well informed when assistance was requested.

Took over 2 hours to get a snack or drink. They sold out of alcohol before the drink cart made even one pass through the plane, non of the alcoholic drinks were complimentary. Most of the workers were good but some were impolite to me.

The positive - airplanes and cabin service are great with a lot of attention to kids. The negative is the ground staff in Astana. We had two adults and two kids with 23kg checked luggage each. Instead of 92 kg, we had 1 x 26.5kg bag and the ground staff called it overweight and tried to charge us for 3.5kg. As a result we had to make one more cabin luggage piece.

An A320 plane with Business and Economy class, very clean and staff were very helpful. During boarding they lend us umbrellas because it was raining. Departed on time and they offered snack during the flight. Plane was spotless and legroom was fine.

I booked a last-minute flight from Lima to Cali via Panama with Copa, based on a local recommendation. OAairport staff were unwilling or unable to assist with a booking and told me to contact the call centre. So at 9pm I returned to my hotel, connected to Wi-Fi, and attempted to book online. At 9:30pm my card was charged, yet the booking failed. I only discovered this by chance when checking my email. The message instructed me to either use another credit card or return to the airport for assistance. With a 7am flight and no realistic way to get to the airport at 2am, I tried another card. Same result. Charge → cancellation → refund. This repeated four times.  I checked out at 3am and headed back to the airport and that’s where the nightmare began. Airport staff had no clue why the bookings were being cancelled. Eventually they suggested the system may have flagged the last-minute booking as fraudulent. Fine, so I asked to simply pay and have the ticket reissued, exactly as the cancellation email suggested. Instead, I was quoted USD 225, despite showing my earlier attempted fare of USD 195. When I politely questioned why I should pay more for what was clearly a system failure on their end, things went downhill fast. I asked for a duty manager and was repeatedly told: 3 minutes, 5 minutes, 7 minutes, while staff stood there texting on phone with supervisor and I waited for 90 minutes. Eventually supervisor appeared, unapologetic, and stated my only option was to pay the higher fare.  I cut my losses, walked away, and booked with LATAM Airlines instead for just $7 more.

Boarding in Hong Kong was chaotic. During the flight average food, no choice due to fact it was finished before reaching me. After arrival noticed damage on the suitcase. Got a report number and waited. After 4 months still waiting. Phoned several times, emailed but Cathay do not respond at all.

London to Hong Kong the cabin crew was unprofessional and not helpful to me and did not help me with my overhead luggage. They might get your order for your food and drinks wrong. There were barely any services provided to me.

We recently went through a horrific experience with Etihad Airways. The airline appears to be overbooking its flights. The experience begins when I attempted to check in online and the system refuses to allow me to do so. At the check-in counter, the staff politely refuse to issue my boarding pass and direct me to another counter for further assistance. The staff at that counter ask me to wait for 1–2 hours and say that if space becomes available, I  will be allowed to board the flight. At first, we (a group of four) thought this was just a one-off incident, after numerous arguments and discussions with third-party staff we were left with no option but to take the next available flight to Colombo the following day. They offered us hotel accommodation 30–40 minutes from the airport. Upon reaching the hotel around 3:00 a.m. we came to the conclusion that this seems to be a policy by Etihad to generate additional revenue. Therefore, please be very careful when choosing to fly with Etihad, especially if you are short on time or have a tight connecting flight, as there is a significant risk of being denied boarding.

Very unhappy with customer service. Courteous and apologetic but no efforts to help. Meals booked were not provided with no effort to even try to help. Booked on corporate seat with full meals but was provided vegetarian (just one snack).. on the return flight, again, we were entitled for a full meal but were provided only snacks with excuse saying flight was delayed and we ran out of meals. Forced to check in, our carry-on on the excuse that they were fully booked. But shouldnt airlines be prepared for full flights and arrange for all the needs required without putting passengers into difficulties. If that is so, then refunds should be provided for services not provided

I flew with my newborn son and the flight was smooth that’s the only thing that was good about the flight. Nobody was at the counter until it was time to board the plane, it was unorganized, I wasn’t even sure what I was supposed to do with my sons stroller I just copied what other people were doing with theirs (when I was purchasing my flight I was not directed to put insurance on his stroller by the way) when we landed our strollers were not on the path and I’m asking people at this point where are the strollers at? I was the last one to get my stroller which is ok but I was able to see that other peoples strollers were not damaged , I opened up my stroller and it was damaged. The net at the bottom was broken and the pole was missing, so all of his stuff I had I couldn’t put it in there and struggled to hold his stuff and mine. I proceeded to make a complaint because none of the attendants would help me they kept telling me to go online, I uploaded pictures and everything to open a case just for them to ask me again to upload pictures so I did it again just for them to tell me our policy states that we will not be responsible for your strollers being damaged if you don’t purchase insurance or in a hard case. The company made me go through all of that consent me help, so I now have a $300 stroller that I can’t use with the bassinet because that bar is missing. I also bought 3 tickets at once and we all should have been sitting next to each other but they had me sitting in a middle seat with 2 strangers with my baby on my lap with no foot room. It was very uncomfortable. Lastly we can’t even get a cup of water you have to pay for everything on that flight, at least give us some water. We all pay so much to fly, there should be no reason they should be careless with our luggage especially baby stuff. I don’t have the money to buy another $300 for my baby being a single parent. I will never fly with this airline again

The flight was to depart 05:30, at the airport boards at 06:00, finally we departed at 06:30. The plane was an old Boeing 737-500. I love old planes, but seats were narrow and legroom was tight. They offered snack.

I had a very positive experience flying Qantas - my first trip with them in decades. These were two ultra-longhaul flights (17 hours and 15 hours), in Economy Class, but both were excellent. The seats were very comfortable and felt quite spacious, with good legroom, and a well designed seat-back storage and table. IFE was very good - a wide selection of movies and TV shows, across many genres, and I found plenty to keep me occupied. Best of all though were the staff - they were consistently friendly, upbeat, cheerful and engaged. I found the food to be mediocre - though the garlic bread was a nice touch - and it's a pity they don't invest more into both the quality and presentation. I didn't like the wooden cutlery and the cheap, flimsy nature of the containers. Two very good flights, and I would happily fly Qantas again.

I have been flying Westjet for a very long time now and I loved them but not sure what they have done with their planes. It is so tight in here. I am sitting with people who are lean but it feels claustrophobic. There is barely any leg room.

Horrible company, they love canceling flights or delaying flights. They also charge you for upgraded seats if you want them but after paying extra, they still end up putting you on a uncomfortable economy seat anyways. I will never fly with them again.

Extremely Disappointing Experience – Zero Accountability from IndiGo I had one of the worst flight experiences of my life with IndiGo on February 19, 2026, on a flight scheduled to depart at 10:45 AM from Hyderabad to Prayagraj. I paid ₹7,000 for this ticket and arrived at the airport by 8:00 AM, well in advance. At around 8:00 AM, IndiGo’s system was completely shut down for nearly one hour, which caused chaos at the airport. I managed to complete web check-in at 8:15 AM and then stood in the baggage check-in queue. Due to the system failure and poor crowd management, I was forced to wait in line for almost two hours. When I finally reached the counter at 9:55 AM, the staff coldly told me it was “too late” to check in my baggage and instructed me to go directly to boarding. I reached the boarding gate at 10:25 AM, only to be told that I had missed my flight. Despite the delay being entirely due to IndiGo’s system failure and mismanagement, they said they “can’t do anything.” I was sent to airport assistance, where I was told to call customer service. Customer service then kept me on the phone for over an hour, repeatedly saying they couldn’t help and that airport staff must handle it—passing responsibility back and forth with zero resolution. I was forced to book another flight for ₹15,000 to Lucknow and then take a cab to Prayagraj. For a one-way journey, I ended up paying ₹22,000, all because of IndiGo’s incompetence. I followed up with customer service for four days requesting a refund for the missed flight caused by their own poor management. Eventually, they denied the refund, absurdly claiming I didn’t provide photos of myself standing in the queue for two hours. What kind of justification is that? I have been traveling internationally for the past 8 years and have flown in several countries. This was my first domestic flight after coming home, and it was shocking to experience such extreme mismanagement, lack of accountability, and disgusting customer service. No one respected the customer or took responsibility at any step. This experience has ensured one thing: I will never fly with IndiGo again. Every step of this journey was ridiculous and handled with complete indifference. I truly wish there was an option to give zero stars.

The trip was a nightmare! They charge for everything and the tv did not work (but that’s complimentary as they say). I guess seat is not , they stuck us on the back because I did not choose a seat - seat cannot lean back, they had other seats empty but they didn’t gave it to us because we did not pay. I had my son with me and we wanted to seat together, we were the first one to ask.  The flight attendant were very nice but couldn’t do anything!

Flight was sensational apart from a little delay. Great to have them flying into Brisbane again. The crew the food the seat was top knotch. Malaysia Airlines know how to do business class right, Great menu selection but can't go pass the satay.

We booked a flight from Dubai to Muscat in early January, with the tickets purchased several months in advance. On the evening before our flight, I checked in online. During the check-in process, the website suggested that I needed to add all our checked-in baggage in order to proceed, which I did, as it appeared to be mandatory. After completing check-in, I was prompted to pay an additional fee for the checked baggage. I was surprised by the charge and the amount, but I could not recall nor access whether our original ticket already included checked baggage. Later that day, when I was able to review our original ticket, I confirmed that checked baggage was already included.  The following morning, we arrived early at Dubai Airport to speak with staff and resolve the issue before departure. The ground staff confirmed that our original ticket included baggage and that the extra charge was not required. They reassured us that the issue would be easily resolved and advised us to contact customer service after landing in Muscat for a refund. Unfortunately, from that point onward, the experience became extremely frustrating. I made multiple phone calls and sent several emails, receiving conflicting information each time. I was told initially that a refund was impossible, then told it was possible only if action was taken before the flight—which I had already done. Later, I was told I could not receive a refund because the flight had already been used, despite the fact that I raised the issue before departure and followed up repeatedly before our return flight, with no response. The root of this issue lies in a poorly designed and misleading online check-in system. Once the error occurs, customers are left with no real support, caught between unresponsive customer service and shifting explanations, only to be told later that nothing can be done. I am extremely disappointed by the lack of accountability and acknowledgment, despite having acted promptly and fully within their stated policy. The money was simply kept, leaving me with no resolution. This experience has left a very negative impression, which is unfortunate given how much we otherwise loved the country. I would not recommend using this airline.

As a Senator level there’s no way to speak to somebody. Everything must be submitted online and nobody replies. Ripped off, sold me an expensive (double) economy ticket that I could upgrade it with vouchers and miles. Once I’d paid the money the upgrade was no longer available. Won’t refund it, nobody to complain to.

Unfortunately due to the weather the flight was delayed over an hour. The new aircraft was very comfortable and the staff were efficient and friendly.  It was nice that they offered free beer and wine. The snack, cheese and biscuits was a bit small. Aside from the delay, an enjoyable flight .
The flight experience was extremely disappointing, and I would not recommend SpiceJet. This has been the worst flight experience of my life.
I enjoyed the flight. Check in was easy and the flight left on time. Staff were very friendly and efficient. Coffee , Tea and Water were free which is ok on such a short flight.

Last week, I flew with AJet for the first time. The outbound flight went smoothly and entirely to our satisfaction. Unfortunately, the same cannot be said about the return journey. The problems already began at Hurghada International Airport. We were traveling as a group of six. Upon arrival at the check-in counter at 01:45 AM, we were informed that one of our tickets was “not active,” even though I had completed the online check-in. We had to wait until 03:25 AM before it was finally confirmed that she was allowed to travel after all. This caused unnecessary stress in the middle of the night. The flight from Hurghada to Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen International Airport went smoothly. For our connecting flight to Düsseldorf, we had already checked in online. Nevertheless, in Hurghada we were also issued physical boarding passes for this segment. Before boarding, our boarding passes were checked and even stamped — to this day, we still do not understand why this was necessary. What happened next was unacceptable. Shortly before boarding, we were pulled out of the queue and told we had to pay an additional €150 for “excess hand luggage.” According to the staff member, we were only allowed four pieces but had seven. While this is numerically correct, I had pre-purchased one additional carry-on trolley, and each of us had a small personal item. Everything fit easily into the overhead bins. On none of the three previous AJet flights (Düsseldorf–Istanbul, Istanbul–Hurghada, and Hurghada–Istanbul) had anyone raised any concerns about our luggage. No baggage was measured or checked. In addition, approximately 25 other passengers experienced exactly the same issue and were all required to pay the same €150, under the threat of being denied boarding. It was not possible to speak to a supervisor; the staff member claimed she herself was the manager. Other ground staff did not offer any assistance. Ultimately, 15 minutes before departure and under considerable pressure, I paid the amount to avoid missing our flight. I have never felt so pressured and powerless as a passenger. Once on board, I immediately reported the incident to the purser, who stated she would file a report and forward it to the airline. In my opinion, this situation constituted a clear abuse of power. Passengers in such circumstances have no real choice. I sincerely hope that AJet takes this matter seriously and investigates it thoroughly, especially as I have since read multiple similar complaints, particularly concerning Istanbul SAW.

I traveled on the Curaçao – Bogota – Montevideo route. Due to problems with the airline, the connection was missed, and we were diverted to Panama before returning to Montevideo on Copa Airlines 24 hours later. My luggage was also lost, arriving 36 hours later, and the customer service process was slow and unhelpful. While I eventually received my bags, the compensation offered for the missed flight and the inconvenience was minimal and in the form of a voucher, not cash. When I requested compensation for expenses incurred due to the lost luggage, the response was negative. Beyond the amount, what leaves a bad impression is the lack of flexibility and customer focus in a situation clearly attributable to the airline. I'm not a frequent flyer, but this type of experience directly influences my decision about which airline to fly with again. When an airline prioritizes closing cases over resolving them properly, it loses something more valuable than $100: it loses trust.  Viajé en la ruta Curazao – Bogota – Montevideo. Por problemas inherentes a la aerolínea la conexión se perdió y fuimos derivados a Panamá para luego volver por Copa a Montevideo 24 h mas tarde. Además mi equipaje se perdió, llego 36h más tarde y el proceso de atención fue lento y poco resolutivo. Si bien finalmente recibí las maletas, la compensación ofrecida por la pérdida de vuelo y las molestias generadas fue mínima y en forma de voucher, no en dinero. Al solicitar una compensación por los gastos incurridos por las pérdidas de las maletas, la respuesta fue negativa. Más allá del monto, lo que deja una mala impresión es la falta de flexibilidad y enfoque en el cliente ante una situación claramente atribuible a la aerolínea. No soy un pasajero frecuente, pero este tipo de experiencia influye directamente en la decisión de con qué compañía volver a viajar. Cuando una aerolínea prioriza cerrar casos antes que resolverlos adecuadamente, pierde algo más valioso que USD 100: pierde confianza.

I booked a return trip from London to Manila after reading good reviews but I was very disappointed. As a solo traveler I booked he flight as Cathy advertised a 1x2x1 seat configuration aboard a A330 but shortly after booking I received an Email to say the aircraft had changed to a B777 with a 2-3-2 seat configuration which was a downgrade. I complained to the airline but it was not answered. The evening prior to my flight which was less than 24 hours notice I received an email to say the business lounge was closed and no alternative could been found with any of the contract lounges . On my arrival the following day at the Cathay check in I was advised again that the lounge was closed but I could use one of the contract lounges at my own expense which was i direct conflict to the email so there was availability . I made another complaint in Writing to Cathay Pacific which was also not answered.

At Jakarta, I was assisted by a Personnel Assistance Representative who escorted me through immigration and into the lounge. On board, I was warmly welcomed by Purser Gloria, Putri, Della, and Chef Ramdan. As this was a night flight, a hot snack was served shortly after departure, followed by breakfast approximately two hours prior to arrival. The breakfast selection was excellent, with eggs prepared to order by Chef Ramdan. Despite the overnight schedule, I was able to rest comfortably for several hours. In Shanghai a Garuda ground staff member met me at the aircraft door and escorted me through immigration, baggage collection, and out to a taxi. She also assisted with translating my destination to the driver, which was particularly valuable given the changes in China since my last visit eight years ago. Her support was greatly appreciated. My sincere thanks to the entire Business Class team for their outstanding service throughout the journey, and to Chef Ramdan for an excellent breakfast experience. I would recommend that Garuda consider refurbishing parts of the aircraft interior, as there were visible signs of wear despite the aircraft being relatively young.

After a fantastic vacation in South Africa, check in at CPT airport was much less impressive! After me had already entered all the necessary information prior to going to the airport, the staff at Kenya Airlines Business Class check-in (Zinze) took forever to print my boarding pass. I asked whether a window seat available, another staff member had to help her with my query. Fine, I said nothing! Then I informed her that my second bag was close to the limit, wondered if I could still add two books. The bag was 32.6kg, ever so slightly over, I put the books in my carry on instead. Got my boarding pass and walked to the men’s bathroom, where she chased me down! Telling me that I must remove a few kilos from my suitcase, as it was too heavy. I told her that 600gr is not “a few kilos” and I was not going to remove “a few kilos”. I then spoke to the supervisor, who solved the issue easily. I had to get the bag off the belt at the check-in counter and carry the bag myself to “oversized baggage”. One staff member was willing to help me to go to that counter, but by that time, I was done with Kenya Airways staff and declined their “help”. Mind tou, I book wheelchair assistance as I am physically challenged (cannot walk long distances) but declined the service at CPT airport as it is a smaller airport. What I dont understand it this: On the aircraft, Kenya Airways staff are very nice and kind and I had a good flight to Johannesburg from Bangkok. but they are grumpy and unpleasant at Cape Town airport, how does that work for the airline?

In the past their premium economy meals were tastier and far better. They offer now metal cutlery  but my food options were pasta or pasta on the ICN-CDG leg. The portions are small, the bread is a sort of processed bun, the cheese was some sort of spread,  and the appetizer a Korean seaweed salad.I didn't eat any of it because it was not appealing. No menu was available, which has been the norm for some time now.

I have been on dozens of Alaska flights since I started living in Seattle, and I'd estimate that like 90% of them experience some sort of inane delay at the gate that makes the travel process take an hour longer and be deeply miserable. Also, the change to the monkfruit pretzels is genuinely insane - they are unpleasant tasting, smelly (especially for the plane), and generally a downgrade from the generic flavor. Their staff is civil but the chronic operational delays make interactions feel more disingenuous than even standard customer service. I am currently sitting on the tarmac writing this review to blow off steam as my Alaska flight becomes more and more delayed.

Last week, I travelled on a multi‑sector Kenya Airways itinerary and by the time I reached Dar es Salaam, not a single flight had operated on schedule. The chaos began with a six‑hour delay on the JNB–NBO flight, causing me to miss my NBO–MBA connection. Arriving in Nairobi well after midnight, I was forced to exit the international terminal for a domestic transfer, only to find the terminal shut. I had no choice but to sit in a coffee shop from 2:00 a.m. to 8:00 a.m.only to face yet another delayed departure. I had a business class fare! The pattern continued relentlessly. Every flight leading up to Dar was delayed, and the EBB–DAR sector alone ballooned into an unnecessarily exhausting 11‑hour journey. These delays were not isolated events; they reflected systemic mismanagement, poor coordination, and an alarming inability to run basic regional operations reliably. Eventually, I abandoned Kenya Airways altogether [a business class return] and purchased a one‑way South African Airways ticket just to ensure I could return to Johannesburg without further disruption. As soon as I reached home I cancelled another KQ business class return flight to Nairobi as I didn't want KQ mismanaging my time yet again. Equally unacceptable is Kenya Airways’ disregard for passenger health and safety. At Johannesburg Airport, “pre‑boarding” meant forcing passengers into the airbridge immediately after the inbound aircraft arrived—trapping them in a cramped, poorly ventilated space for about 30 minutes while the aircraft was cleaned. Requests to open side doors for airflow were refused by security personnel who insisted it was “not allowed,” even as the heat and lack of ventilation worsened. I have raised these safety concerns with numerous red‑jacketed KQ managers since 2022, yet all I ever receive is the perennial empty assurance: “We will attend to it.” Nothing has changed. The same unsafe conditions were present at Entebbe Airport, where passengers were made to wait on a steep, congested staircase with no adequate ventilation.

I paid an additional fee to select and secure a specific seat, but I was reassigned to a different seat, at the time of boarding, due to what the airline described as an aircraft change. When I boarded, my seat was given to someone else - the aircraft type was the same one. The airline later claimed the new seat was in the same category, but that is not the issue. I paid for a specific seat, and it was not honoured. There was no apology, compensation or meaningful explanation. If seat selection cannot be guaranteed, this should be made clear before customers pay extra.

Last week, I travelled on a multi‑sector Kenya Airways itinerary and by the time I reached Dar es Salaam, not a single flight had operated on schedule. The chaos began with a six‑hour delay on the JNB–NBO flight, causing me to miss my NBO–MBA connection. Arriving in Nairobi well after midnight, I was forced to exit the international terminal for a domestic transfer, only to find the terminal shut. I had no choice but to sit in a coffee shop from 2:00 a.m. to 8:00 a.m.only to face yet another delayed departure. I had a business class fare! The pattern continued relentlessly. Every flight leading up to Dar was delayed, and the EBB–DAR sector alone ballooned into an unnecessarily exhausting 11‑hour journey. These delays were not isolated events; they reflected systemic mismanagement, poor coordination, and an alarming inability to run basic regional operations reliably. Eventually, I abandoned Kenya Airways altogether [a business class return] and purchased a one‑way South African Airways ticket just to ensure I could return to Johannesburg without further disruption. As soon as I reached home I cancelled another KQ business class return flight to Nairobi as I didn't want KQ mismanaging my time yet again.
