I have been on dozens of Alaska flights since I started living in Seattle, and I'd estimate that like 90% of them experience some sort of inane delay at the gate that makes the travel process take an hour longer and be deeply miserable. Also, the change to the monkfruit pretzels is genuinely insane - they are unpleasant tasting, smelly (especially for the plane), and generally a downgrade from the generic flavor. Their staff is civil but the chronic operational delays make interactions feel more disingenuous than even standard customer service. I am currently sitting on the tarmac writing this review to blow off steam as my Alaska flight becomes more and more delayed.

I chose the "Saver" option. During checkout it asked me to upgrade for $57 to choose my seat. I chose an aisle seat, it showed 31C in my confirmation. When checking in my seat was changed to a center seat 28E. A middle seat. I could have got that poor seat without upgrading. When I complained they said even if you upgrade no seats are guaranteed. So what’s the point?

I have never experienced such consistently lousy service as I have with Avianca Airlines. If you’re considering flying from Bogotá to Miami, do yourself a favor and look elsewhere. From the moment you check in, it feels like the airline is doing you a favor by letting you board. The customer service agents are dismissive, unhelpful, and borderline hostile. Any issue — whether it’s a seat assignment error, a baggage problem, or a delayed departure — somehow magically becomes the passenger’s fault. The flights were uncomfortable, poorly managed, and disorganized. Delays with zero clear communication. Gate changes announced last minute. Overhead bins already full because of their own boarding chaos. And when you ask for help, you’re treated like you’re the inconvenience. What really pushes it over the edge is their favorite move: blaming passengers for their own screw-ups. Missed connection because they delayed the first leg? Somehow that’s your responsibility. System glitch that drops your seat assignment? You should’ve “checked earlier.” Lost baggage? You must have done something wrong. It’s infuriating. Instead of taking accountability, they gaslight customers into thinking the airline’s operational failures are personal mistakes. It’s unprofessional, it’s exhausting, and it’s completely unacceptable for an international carrier. Flying is already stressful. With Avianca, it becomes a masterclass in frustration. Lousy service, lousy flights, and absolutely zero ownership of their own mess. Never again.

The price wasn’t so different but, I decided to book anyway, saving maybe lass than 100 dollars. During checkin everything is extra, even seat in any place is charged. Terrible situation where I’m felling tricked by this situation. If I don’t pay an extra 25 to 73 dollars I can’t assign a seat and need to be somewhere far from my wife (with is the clear definition of obligate the customer to pay extra) it’s not optional. Additionally it’s for each part, as my flight have a connection I’ve to pay for both parts.

I am very disappointed with Emirates. I booked my tickets almost a year before travelling as I like to carefully select my seat and more importantly, the type of aircraft I will be travelling on. Emirates changed the second half of the inbound journey from an A380(which I had booked) to a 777-300. They did not even inform me. I found out when I was looking something up, which resulted in me phoning them and writing to them to ask to move me back to any A380 going into any London airport at any time that day. My e-mail, I never got a reply to, and the telephone conversation resulted in them saying I could pay an additional £400,- for the honour of changing my ticket due to what they had done, not me. They later put a disclaimer on the booking saying “mixed fleet”. The 777-300 was an old and noisy aircraft with an illuminated Non Smoking sign above my head, and nowhere to put my bag anywhere near me. To me, it felt more like a Premium Economy than business class. I have flown with Emirates many times, and I booked the A380 for a reason. Buyer beware.

American Airlines – Saint Kitts (AA3084, Feb 27, 2026) Paid over $100 for seat assignments so my wife and I could sit together on an international flight. We were not seated together. When we politely asked gate agents (T. Caines and Ms. Boward) if anything could be done, we were dismissed with “the flight is full.” No effort. No system check. No attempt to assist. When I asked if they could identify passengers who might switch, I was told that information was “classified” and essentially told to walk the plane myself and ask strangers. The issue wasn’t a full flight — it was attitude and indifference. Add in a delay for “operational issues,” over $140 in baggage fees, and inconsistent policy enforcement regarding checked electronics. Customer Relations responded with a $50 future flight credit. That tells you everything you need to know about how they value accountability. If you pay extra for seats on American Airlines, understand that it does not guarantee service — and if something goes wrong, don’t expect meaningful resolution.

Frontier Airlines is absolutely the worst airline there is.  I had a flight at 10pm, as soon as I get done with check in and pass security I get a notification saying my flight has been delayed until 1am. I call customer service, they basically give me a word salad to say they can't switch my flight or do anything at all other than give me a $75 flight voucher which i have 90 days to use (I'm never flying with them again so I won't) and a $15 food voucher which first of all is not enough for anything in a restaurant and worst of all they make it crazy hard to claim. They also take every opportunity to force you to check in bags that are small for $70 and will even charge you another $45 if you check in in person.

What a fantastic airline, instantly gone into one of my favourites. At the gate the staff said they have to change my pre booked seat. However they said as an apology they will block out the seat next to me. First flight to Amman was fine meal was very tasty and IFE more than sufficient. The second leg from Amman to Bangkok was 7 and a half hours and was perfect. My seat was 36c the very back row. I prefer that as it’s only two seats. The food on this leg was the best I’ve ever had, it was restaurant food quality. It was a chicken burger that was a juicy fully seasoned chicken fillet, with cheese, mushrooms with a sesame seed bun. It was exceptional. The female cabin crew were very friendly but the males were a bit cold. Would 100% fly Royal Jordanian again.

By sharp contrast to their 787 fleet, it seems at least that Scoot have got their act together with the A320neo. The aircraft is an all around better design in so many ways. Seats are bigger and more comfortable, getting in and out of the aircraft is relatively easy. No in flight entertainment available, so take a book or tablet. Surprised that there is no USB charging on any of the Scoot aircraft that I flew on. Such a simple thing that should really be addressed. Cabin crew on this flight were very good, but I would advise the company to change the name from "Scooties".

There is something that Scoot does not bother to tell you about seat 1C - yes, it is an extra legroom seat, but the divider between economy and business class is diagonal, and as a result the walkway (and the service trolleys) are cutting into your leg and foot space.  I know it was a red eye flight, and nobody likes those, but I had to wait ~20 minutes to get to the bathroom because the staff were there with the trolleys, trying to sell Scoot merchandise. Their attitude towards me was apathetic to say the least. For me, this was the decider. I'll never use Scoot again.

I'm not exactly sure what Scoot are up to with the Perth to Singapore leg, but there was plenty to complain about. Aircraft was extremely messy inside, and even though I paid additional money for a "Scoot in Silence" seat I was absolutely cramped in this aircraft. As well as this, I'm not sure who designs the seats, but these need looking at for sure. The passenger in front of me reclined his seat and leaned back hard, and the result was the round metal plate that is near the armrest pushed into my kneecap. Quite a painful experience I can assure you. Also, as an afterthought, I added 20kg of baggage to my flight, and an onboard meal. What can I say? The baggage pricing was exorbitant to say the least, and as well as this my food was served cold. All in all, the flight cost me perhaps $150 less than flying on Thai International, which I will be doing in future. I used to be a supporter of Scoot, but not any more.

I chose the "Saver" option. During checkout it asked me to upgrade for $57 to choose my seat. I chose an aisle seat, it showed 31C in my confirmation. When checking in my seat was changed to a center seat 28E. A middle seat. I could have got that poor seat without upgrading. When I complained they said even if you upgrade no seats are guaranteed. So what’s the point?

Lost my suitcase. Cramped cabin with a seat pitch of 29 inches. The food was overly salted chicken breast full of tendons. The experience was diabolical, with a cheap and nasty feel to the entire dining experience. Waited one hour at luggage carousal to then find my suitcase left behind.

I experienced the same baggage problem twice while travelling to Juba with Ethiopian Airlines and was disappointed by the airline’s inability to effectively follow up on the issue, even when travelling in Business Class. In both cases, my baggage was left in Addis Ababa instead of being transferred onward. I contacted Ethiopian Airlines immediately and was assured that my bag was already on the same flight to Juba. However, this information proved incorrect, and my luggage arrived two days later each time. The main concern was not only the delay itself, but the lack of accurate tracking, follow-up, and ownership once the issue was reported. Despite reaching out proactively and travelling on a premium ticket, there was no visible effort to monitor or expedite the baggage transfer. For an airline positioning itself as a major international carrier, stronger case follow-up and more reliable passenger support — especially on tight regional connections — would significantly improve the customer experience.

My last trip with Icelandair ever, if I can help it. Although the tickets were expensive, the Economy cabin was extremely cramped and uncomfortable. What concerned me the most, however, was the way we were treated on board. A simple and polite request led to me being reprimanded at length by a flight attendant. We were told in a rather rude and confrontational manner that we had to keep our seats reclined at all times and the flight attendant attempted to recline our seats despite our preference not to. Given the price they put on their tickets, I expected a far better level of comfort and flight attendants with at least basic manners.

Lovely flight crew onboard, excellent service, food was very good. Loved my flight! Flight was delayed by over seven hours (due to floods in Lagos), and that in the middle of the night. No food in the lounge after I think 1am, not even some snacks. Battled to get a sandwich! Breakfast was available from about 5am onwards. I was lucky that one caring staff offered me a blanket in the meantime. Kenya Airways could have done better! Boarding was chaotic too, one staff handling the entire process, just ridiculous! If there are no delays etc, this airline is great. Otherwise, you are on your own, even as a business class passenger!

Checking in at BER with carry on 10 kilo so 2 kilos over the limit. When I flew business nobody did even check the weight or size last time.  I had to take out my necessities and meds blocking the counter. I guess my carry on went down to 9 kilo by then but it had to go on a journey. My bag been checked all the way to IAH. Been loaded on the belt go through system to be loaded to the plane BER-FRA. Had to be unloaded in FRA transferred to United plane in FRA and loaded in there to make its way to IAH. My question is why making it miserable for all involved waisting time, manpower and forcing meaningless stress.  I do not understand the meaning behind al this stupid stress generating rule.

My traveling companions and I lost our pre-booked seats on flight TG941 (MXP-BKK) due to an aircraft change. I contacted the Thai Airways call center to fix the issue. The agent manually assigned us seats 59H, 59J, and 59K. Unfortunately, the agent omitted a crucial detail: these seats have no window whatsoever. To make matters worse, the space on board is borderline habitable. My food quality was decidedly mediocre. The In-Flight Entertainment selection is extremely poor, with only two or three movies available in Italian.  Instead of addressing the specific mistake made by their call center agent, they simply copy-pasted a generic policy about automatic seat reallocations. Very disappointing.

Lovely flight crew onboard, excellent service, food was very good. Loved my flight! Flight was delayed by over seven hours (due to floods in Lagos), and that in the middle of the night. No food in the lounge after I think 1am, not even some snacks. Battled to get a sandwich! Breakfast was available from about 5am onwards. I was lucky that one caring staff offered me a blanket in the meantime. Kenya Airways could have done better! Boarding was chaotic too, one staff handling the entire process, just ridiculous! If there are no delays etc, this airline is great. Otherwise, you are on your own, even as a business class passenger!
The worst airline ever. They completely damaged my  suitcase and offering only 20euro. At first, at the airport, they refused to give me the PIR.

In the last year, I booked six trips for my four family members with Arajet, a total of 24 flights. The result: one problem after another. Delays, cancellations, lack of response. In short, besides being a hassle, it was a waste of time and money. One flight was canceled outright for the next day while we were at the check-in counter. Unfortunately, you can't book a trip with such an irresponsible company. I will never use their services again, and obviously, I don't recommend them to anyone; you're guaranteed to have problems. There are more reputable airlines, and the price difference isn't significant; the cost ends up being higher.

Our flight was delayed by almost 6 hours due to a mechanical failure (engines not powering up resulting in brief blackout in cabin during safety presentation. To American Airlines' credit, both the pilots and ground staff kept everyone informed. A rescue plane was flown in and departed at 00:45 hours the following day. Initial departure was 19:21 on 2/22. AA also credited AAdvantage members with points and provided food vouchers of $12.00 per person. They accepted the offer of Emeral Coast Grill to reopen and provide a limited menu. The flight to DFW was uneventful. Flight Attendant greeted every passenger with a welcome aboard and smile. The overhead cabin in First Class is not large but my 21" carryon fit comfortably. Overhead bins are larger of starboard side.

Ontime departure and arrival. Flight very smooth for the most part. The A321neo is a gorgeous aircraft with spacious overhead bins and plenty of legroom in Main Cabin Extra. Service as is the norm comprised of beverage service and biscotti biscuits. IFE was easy to log in and had a wide variety of films, tv shows and music to watch or listen on your personal devices.

Flew on March 2 AA1572 from Toronto to Miami. Check in fast, friendly and efficient. Flying with pet in cabin necessitated some paper work which was dealt with speedily. Boarding was quick and as we were flying business class priority boarding was enforced and very pleasant. Flight left on time and arrived before schedule. Flight attendants were very attentive, helpful, knowledgeable, friendly and one has to say “very nice”. I got the impression that they loved their work and were proud to represent AA. Information from the cockpit was informative. Plane - even though it was around 26 years old - was clean and must have had a recent refurbishment. Food was good, presented nicely and served on time. Luggage arrived after a short wait. A great flight.

Flair does every possible thing to ruin your trip and squeeze extra money. Baggage rules are the strictest and most unfair I've seen — tiny allowances, random reclassifications at the gate, $100+ fees for nothing, and no consistency (same bag free one leg, charged the next). No free water. Rude staff: dismissive, sarcastic, unhelpful, and sometimes hostile.  My Toronto to Cancun trip was a nightmare from start to finish. The cheap ticket illusion disappears fast.  Worst experience ever.

I am extremely dissatisfied with the service provided by IndiGo. This has been, without a doubt, one of the worst travel experiences I have ever had. In-flight experience: The food served on board was absolutely disgusting and practically inedible. To make matters worse, the staff were incredibly rude and lacked any sense of hospitality. Baggage Damage: My suitcase arrived completely destroyed, with a wheel missing. This is unacceptable handling of personal property. Customer Service Nightmare: It has been over 50 days since I filed my claim, and I still have not received a refund or a proper resolution. Lack of Accountability: Their phone support is abysmal. Every time I call, the agents are clueless and unable to provide updates. It is impossible to speak with a manager or anyone in a position of responsibility. IndiGo is completely unprofessional from every point of view. I strongly advise travelers to look elsewhere if they value their money, their time, and their belongings.

Service is generally good from Cabin Staff. My Main Issue was at Check In they Dont Advise that you have to have a Paper Boarding Pass at some Airports. Another Issue is they start serving drinks to Business Class Passengers before others have fully boarded. This causes cabin crew to block the aisles.

We want to express many thanks to the Wings Air staff in Ende, Flores. We booked a flight at 11:40h to LBJ. But that one was canceled and we were rescheduled to the early flight 8:30h We booked through Agoda and so the staff did not have our phone number or email. They tried to find us and think about LCR hotel in Ende. That was at 7:55h so no more then 35 minutes before departure. We were still in bed. A taxi was ready to drive us to the airport, quick check-in and we were in time to catch the flight. Again many many thanks for the efforts to the staff in cooperation with the staff of LCR hotel in Ende. The flight was very comfortable but for the announcements In the plane in English, please speak them a bit slowly so passengers really can understand what the message is

They weigh your personal backpack at the gate and enforce an 8kg total limit for carry-on and personal items combined. ​I was flagged at 12.6kg for my workstation and camera gear and was hit with a massive fee. To make it worse, they refused to split the payment between card and cash, forcing me to use a faulty airport ATM that ate my debit card while my flight was already delayed. ​If you’re  carrying tech or gear, avoid Condor. T

Just before boarding at Gatwick, my small suitcase was found to be roughly 1 cm too tall. I was charged £48 to upgrade my bag. On my return flight, the bag wasn’t checked at all—highlighting how inconsistent and arbitrary these checks can be. EasyJet’s bag checks are extremely strict, inconsistent, and leave no margin whatsoever. Measure everything very carefully or go with a different airline.

I booked a flight, rental car and hotel with Delta. Their hotel was the “airport” hotel but there was no information about the hotel on the app and when I finally found it, it was an hour away! Terrible. And it was a half hour wait to reach customer service

Safair is a basic, no-frills airline that gets you from point A to point B efficiently. We checked in online 24 hours before departure via their website. Check in and bag drop at the airport starts no more than two hours before flight departure time and counter staff at FALE (Durban) strictly enforce that. There's no IFE, no complimentary food or beverage on board. The big, big plus Safair offers customers is none of the seats can be reclined. For that reason alone, I will always choose Safair first. Otherwise, a very pleasant flight experience. Will definitely ride with Safair again!

SkyBoss is a rip off. Shambolic check in at Brisbane by rude, aggressive staff. We received 3 different seat assignments from pre-booked seats (SkyBoss), to check-in seats, to a further change at the boarding gate. The VietJet staff's attitude: "Take it or leave it". SkyBoss is a rip-off: pay a bit more and choose a 'proper' airline.

My husband and I experienced great service from Junior on this flight as he relocated us when my husband's chair was broken ensuring that we had close access to our onboard luggage, instead of walking all the way to the back if the plain. He was eager to help and a clear communicator. Unfortunately we can not say the same for the in-flight manager that day as our requests were completely ignored and unattended to by other staff.

Paid for extra legroom seats and never received them. At 6'3", I was crammed into a standard seat with no consideration shown for what I had paid for.  I have requested a refund and have been given nothing but endless run-around responses from bots and so-called “live agents” who clearly have no intention of resolving the issue. The customer service is beyond useless — it feels deliberately obstructive. This airline has ruined a good trip to the Philippines for us and left a very sour taste with us.

I really like the A350, comfortable and quiet. Cathy’s hard product is excellent, especially the seats. I became quite unwell on this flight and the crew were amazing, especially Winnie who was so caring and kind. Thank you so much for looking after me so well. The inflight entertainment is quite good and what food I had was good.

On India routes they are simply awful. CX698 March 3rd Delhi to Hong Kong, there was basically minimal service by a very surly crew. Travelling Premium Economy, no welcome drink, not hot towels. No pre meal drink. Crew served a meal about 45 minutes into a 41/2 hour flight, then not seen again. No tea or coffee served. No service at all. The positive is their hard product is really good. Seats and room very comfortable.

Boarding on time well performed by groups. FA, nothing special, they just did their job. Nice full meal for lunch time, chicken, salad and dessert. Drinks served several times. IFE available connecting your own device. Seat comfort ok, nothing special, usual middle seat empty. Arrival on time.
Nice flight and very nice crew. Weekend trip, on time departure and arrival. Boarding by groups, seat comfort ok for a 50min flight time. Food for purchase, arrival ahead of schedule. Well don

I'm a StarAlliance Gold member. CDG to IST Economy seat 09A. During check-in, they only gave me seat that required an upgrade, otherwise I could not get my boarding pass.  So I had to pay for a premium (emergency exit) seat. The in-flight entertainment system didn't work on this 3 hour flight. They asked me to sign a document acknowledging that I'm aware of this and that I agree with it, which I declined. They said, "Please file a claim", which I did. They lied about this and said everything was working as it should. Very disappointed with this service. Hence the review.
Good trip and very good crew. The aircraft was disgusting with a filthy carpet and dirty seat.  Seems this route gets good load factors since not much competition.

The airline cancelled the pre ordered hot seats BKI-KUL and on the return all hot seats were withdrawn due to fleet changes and aircraft deployment. The airline does not refund or credit the fares difference for such incidence.

Avoid this airline as much as possible. The flight attendants were unfriendly, multimedia is not operational, seats looks worn and torn, disgusting bathrooms, plane looks old. Multimedia did not work properly. My luggage was not loaded onto my connecting flight and I was struggling to receive it for more than 30 hours after arriving. There was zero support from airline office.

My experience with Vietnam Airlines on flight VN126 from Ho Chi Minh City to Da Nang on 29 January 2026 was one of the worst airline experiences I have ever had. The flight was diverted to Hue due to military activity at Da Nang Airport, which I understand can happen. However, the way the situation was handled afterwards was completely unacceptable. Passengers were told that another aircraft would arrive to take us onward to Da Nang, but there was almost no communication from airline staff and no clear information about what was happening. After waiting for hours with very little explanation, it became clear that the promised onward flight was not coming. When passengers asked to collect their checked baggage so they could leave the airport and arrange their own transport, it took over three hours for the airline to release the bags, again with no explanation. At that point we had no choice but to organise our own transport to Da Nang, which is around 80 km away. The taxi cost 1,508,000 VND – a completely predictable cost for that distance. Vietnam Airlines has since refused to refund the flight despite failing to transport passengers to the booked destination. Instead, they are offering a fixed “transport subsidy” of 300,000 VND for an 80 km journey, which is absurd and does not come close to covering the real cost of getting from Hue to Da Nang. Even more frustratingly, they have stated that this small subsidy can only be collected in person at a Vietnam Airlines ticket office in Vietnam, which is impractical for international travellers who have already left the country. Diversions can happen in aviation, but abandoning passengers in the wrong city and expecting them to pay the majority of the cost to complete the journey themselves is unacceptable. The lack of communication, the delay in releasing baggage, and the refusal to provide reasonable reimbursement demonstrate extremely poor customer service.

Avoid this airline as much as possible. The flight attendants were unfriendly, multimedia is not operational, seats looks worn and torn, disgusting bathrooms, plane looks old. Multimedia did not work properly. My luggage was not loaded onto my connecting flight and I was struggling to receive it for more than 30 hours after arriving. There was zero support from airline office.

My wife flew to Banjul upon international arrival in Dakar. Air Senegal preponed their departure which disabled her to connect the same day as a later flight was cancelled. She became a rebooked a day later though through to a more complicated routing via Cap Skirring near Guinea Bissau. Aircraft was on a leased A320, quite nice. No service onboard. Luggage arrived. In conclusion, the airline is unreliable and cannot be recommended, particularly for regional and domestic flights

Flair Airlines cancelled our flight during a serious security situation and is now failing to honor the refund they promised. Our flight F8 2623 from Puerto Vallarta (PVR) to Toronto (YYZ) was cancelled by Flair due to the ongoing emergency situation in Puerto Vallarta. Being stranded abroad during that situation was stressful and concerning. Flair confirmed the cancellation by text message and email, stating that the flight was cancelled due to the emergency situation at PVR. We were automatically rebooked on another fligtt but the rebooked flight was 15 days after our original departure date. We were told that if the rebooked flight did not work for us, we were eligible to cancel and receive a full refund to the original form of payment. The system itself displayed a notice stating that we could cancel the flight for a full refund at no extra charge, and that once the request was submitted, a dedicated team would cancel the flight and process the refund back to the original payment method. We also spoke with a Flair representative who confirmed the same thing — that passengers affected by this cancellation were eligible for a full refund if the rebooked flight did not work. Following Flair’s exact instructions, we submitted the refund request on February 27. Despite this: the reservation still shows the flight as “confirmed”  The cancellation has not been processed The refund has not been issued  No confirmation has been provided Flair’s own disruption policy and Canadian Air Passenger Protection Regulations state that when an airline cancels a flight and the passenger declines the alternative offered, the passenger is entitled to a refund to the original form of payment.

My partner flew Kigali-Nairobi-Abidjan-Dakar early March 2026. Aircrafts were the Embraer 190 and Boeing 737-800, respectively. First flight KGL-NBO was cancelled 4 days before departure. This triggered a forced rebooking to become a most inconvenient night-flight. Second flight got also seriously delayed with very short notice, first by 4 hours and, while waiting in the aircraft, another 1-2 hours. Arrived in Dakar 5 hours late, which recently happens very often for KQ on this route. KQ did not provide compensation for the changes/delays and no lounge access were provided in Nairobi – my partner could only purchase access by using mileage which became a good deal as the delay extended. Eventually, however, the flights went smoothly and FAs and service onboard were impeccable. Spacious priority seats given on both legs; the preordered food was tasty and plenty, which rendered a personalized experience and feeling valued. No entertainment nor WiFi functioned onboard. Luggage arrived in Dakar without problems.

Flew Premium Business LHR - GRU in Brazil on our way to Uruguay, and then Argentina and Chile. Had access to the standard BA Lounge in T3, LHR which was OK for a snack and a couple of drinks. Boarded in good time to a very comfortable cabin and seats - not suites. Row 7 not so good as immediately behind a "serving area" where the crew gathered to deal with meal service etc. so privacy was a bit limited. Fortunately, it was a night flight so actually no one came and stood there so still private. The upside was that we could chat and engage with the very nice cabin crew who kept us entertained. In-Flight entertainment not bad - a reasonable choice of films and TV shows in EnglishDecent meal - beef as I recall - and very, very good service all the way. Fairly small and average omelette prior to landing. Took off on time, smooth flight is a quite comfortable seat converted into a nice flat bed with mattress topping and fleecy blanket and big pillow. Amenity kit ok in nice bag (we had a choice of colours!). Landed on time and disembarked quickly so made our connecting P/Economy flight to Montevideo in good time. Enjoyed it and can recomment Premium Business - maybe not Row 7 though....

IFE failed on a 14 hour flight. First class was booked and catered to 4 - but then 4 upgrades at gate so not enough food. Vegetarian options very very limited and quality was mediocre. Lufthansa’s response to the service failure? 8300 points - equivalent to €25 off a next flight. So Lufthansa doesn’t care or value its First Class catering or IFE.

I paid for a specific seat (CHF 15–20). Shortly before departure the airline changed the seat to a worse one and sent emails saying your seat has changed. At that point the paid seat selection becomes meaningless. Passengers seated in the back placed their hand luggage in the front cabin compartments and those in aisle seats who board later found no space left for their own luggage.

I purchased my Volotea flight through Kiwi.com on January 7, 2026 — fully paid, confirmed, weeks in advance. The flight (Olbia to Venice, February 15) was operated by Volotea. The day before departure, I tried to check in online. The system simply would not allow it. No explanation. No warning. No assistance. The next day, I went to the airport to resolve the issue in person. That is when I was told I had been placed in overbooking because Volotea’s algorithm had selected me. Despite booking more than a month earlier, I was apparently chosen by their system as the passenger who might not fly. I was told they could not guarantee me a seat and that I should come back later and “wait to see” if one became available.  Because of this absurd situation, I was forced to buy two entirely new flights just to get to London on time for a critical work commitment.  No prior warning. No transparency. No real assistance. Just uncertainty, disrespect, and complete disregard for customers’ time, money, and responsibilities. I will never fly with Volotea again. I strongly advise anyone to think twice before trusting this airline with their travel plans

My partner flew Kigali-Nairobi-Abidjan-Dakar early March 2026. Aircrafts were the Embraer 190 and Boeing 737-800, respectively. First flight KGL-NBO was cancelled 4 days before departure. This triggered a forced rebooking to become a most inconvenient night-flight. Second flight got also seriously delayed with very short notice, first by 4 hours and, while waiting in the aircraft, another 1-2 hours. Arrived in Dakar 5 hours late, which recently happens very often for KQ on this route. KQ did not provide compensation for the changes/delays and no lounge access were provided in Nairobi – my partner could only purchase access by using mileage which became a good deal as the delay extended. Eventually, however, the flights went smoothly and FAs and service onboard were impeccable. Spacious priority seats given on both legs; the preordered food was tasty and plenty, which rendered a personalized experience and feeling valued. No entertainment nor WiFi functioned onboard. Luggage arrived in Dakar without problems.

I paid extra for an AJet Premium ticket expecting better service, but the experience was extremely disappointing. When our flight from Van to Istanbul was cancelled due to weather, the airport staff could not even communicate in English, and I had to find someone to translate. The information provided was unclear and not consistent with the Premium ticket rules. Despite paying almost double the price of a regular ticket, I saw absolutely no priority or meaningful difference in service. The replacement flight was also delayed for more than an hour, and overall the experience felt no different from a basic economy ticket. Very disappointing. In my experience, AJet Premium offers little to no real value for the extra money.

I selected a window seat in the front of the airplane via online check-in. At the airport they assigned me a totally different seat in the last row of the airplane in front of the toilet. The lady at the check-in counter had an attitude. However, the lady in the airplane was lovely. We asked her for a seat change, she was understanding but couldn’t do anything because the flight was fully booked. At least she had more empathic skills than the one at the check-in counter.

I had a positive experience flying China Southern Airlines economy class. Sats comfortable with foot rest. On board entertainment, on board catering, on board cabin crew courtesy. Efficient and organised boarding by airport agent. On time departure and arrival and an excellent ticket price.

At the gate for flight LS1543, several passengers including myself were told we had to place our cabin bags in the hold because the flight was supposedly “low on bags” and there would not be enough overhead space unless you had purchased guaranteed cabin luggage. The issue is that once boarding was complete the aircraft was only around three-quarters full and there was clearly still overhead bin space available. This made the whole situation very frustrating and difficult to understand. It creates the impression that inconvenience is being introduced at the gate so that passengers are pushed towards paying extra for “guaranteed cabin luggage” in the future. To be fair, the gate staff appeared to be following instructions, but the communication started with “you must check your bag,” which set the wrong tone. Overall a poor customer experience and not something I would expect when cabin baggage is advertised as included in the ticket.

Our third Premium Business Flight on this holiday, and back to London. Transitting from the Santiago flight was a breeze - baggage checked all the way through yo London so in 20 minutes from getting off the Santiago flight we were in the LATAM lounge in Sao Paolo waiting for the London Flight. Boarded more or less on time, but the gate was very crowded as it appeared to be stuck right away in a far corner of the airport as an afterthought. Chaotic. Once on board, we had the same Premium Business seats as before: comfortable lie flat seats with a mattress topper, fleece blanket and nice pillow. Choice of amenity kit bags - usual contents. The Meal Service was interrupted by some turbulence so not as good as previously had. Once again, very friendly and engaging Flight attendants who came round frequently before the usual night flight "lights out". Uneventful flight with average omeltte for breakfast. Landed on time, and baggage off quickly. Enjoyed the premium business flights with LATAM - very comfortable seats and great crews on all flights. Would fly again with them and definitely recommend this product.

Travelled Premium Business Santiago to Sao Paolo to pick up our London connection. Check in was a breeze. Took a little while to get through Immigration and Security, then we went through to the very, very nice LATAM lounge (covered in a separate review). Boarded on time, and had the same format of Premium Business lie flat seats. Took off on time and watched a film on their pretty good IFE - noise reducing headphones were comfortable. Did not eat as planned to do so on our next flight home to London. Very nice engaging and pleasant crew - BA crews could look and learn here. Landed on time with plenty of time to catch our London flight - so went to the not-quite-as-nice Sao Paolo lounge. All in all LATAM have been very good.

The staff were friendly and attentive.  The aircraft was quite new and in good condition.  I was served by Miss Jo on my flight into Seoul and my return back to Vancouver, who remembered having me on the flight inbound into Seoul a week ago. The crew served meals and beverages with. The food isn't the best but the price reflects that.

6 year olds A350-900, my food was inedible, and my entertainment system only worked spasmodically and with old movies and Vietnam promos. The footrests on both my and my wife’s seats were broken. The WiFi didn’t work. I asked for butter and jam for my breakfast croissant and was told that’s not how the Vietnamese eat croissants. Very puzzling having just spent 2 weeks in the country and never served a croissant without either. All in all a massive disappointment, if given the choice will not fly with them again.

Airplane A321, clean and both flights were on time. Exceptional service and very friendly crew. Food was great, during pre-departure drinks (on Cairo rute) were not serving alcoholic drinks because they were touching muslin country, on the air they offered full bar.

I had a great experience on AirAsia flight AK700 from Singapore to Kuala Lumpur. Even though it was a short flight, the service from the cabin crew made the journey very pleasant. All the cabin crew were professional, attentive, and welcoming throughout the flight. A special thanks to Cabin Crew Faizal, who was exceptionally friendly and provided excellent service. His warm attitude and helpfulness really stood out and made the flight even more enjoyable. Overall, it was a smooth and comfortable flight. Thank you to the whole crew for making the trip enjoyable despite the short travel time. Great service and a wonderful experience!

Discover canceled our flight from Orlando to Frankfurt a few hours before our flight without giving any reason and had us drive 3 hours to Tampa for another flight. To add insult to injury they then seated my wife and I away from each other in a middle seat when months ahead of time we had booked aisle seats next to each other. The ticketing agent at Tampa was in the process of ticketing our aisle seats when he said that he had given the seats to another passenger in the line next to us.

Very poor experience with Ethiopian Airlines. Our flight from Addis Ababa to Vienna (ET724) was overbooked. On 7 March, my partner and I were denied boarding in the middle of the night at the last minute, despite having confirmed tickets, and were rebooked for the following day. On 8 March, the airline attempted again to cancel our seats, even though my wife had already been allowed to board, and it felt as if they were trying to separate us at the gate. This caused extreme stress and uncertainty. Promises about guaranteed seats and correct baggage handling were also not honored. I have submitted a formal complaint to Ethiopian Airlines. This experience shows how passengers, even with confirmed tickets, can be subjected to chaotic and stressful situations.

Leg space was terrible, worse then Spirit Airlines and Frontier, The table trays are smaller then any other airline and the TV’s have no “Live” Tv to watch live sports or news. Very disappointed with the leg space and how close seats are to eachother. Also, the seats do not go high enough so it’s very difficult to lean your head back.

I want to share my extremely disappointing experience during the travel disruption following the Dubai shutdown after the Iran missile attacks on 28.02.2026. During an already stressful and uncertain situation, our Dubai–Sofia flight was marked as “affected” twice in a row. Each time we were pushed to either rebook or request a refund ourselves, even though the flights were not actually cancelled. Being put through this process repeatedly left us with the strong impression that passengers were being treated like pawns that could simply be moved around depending on the airline’s operational or commercial priorities. In practice, this felt like we were being forced to release our seats so they could either be given to higher-priority customers or resold at significantly higher prices. What made the situation even worse was that the airline was practically unreachable exactly when passengers needed assistance the most. We could not reach anyone by phone, emails were left unanswered, and with very few physical offices available it became almost impossible to speak to a real person. When travelers are stranded in a crisis, not being able to contact the airline at all turns an already stressful situation into a nightmare. This uncertainty caused us far more stress than the already frightening situation with missile alerts and security concerns in the region. Instead of providing reassurance and stability during a difficult moment, the airline’s handling of the situation created confusion and pressure to make immediate decisions without reliable information. In the end, we were forced to purchase alternative tickets on another airline at a very high price just to ensure we could leave safely and predictably. After securing those seats, we deliberately cancelled our flydubai bookings even though we knew we would likely lose the money. We did this simply to free the seats for someone who might genuinely need them. Passengers deserve transparency, honesty, and support during crises. Unfortunately, this experience made it very difficult to trust flydubai in the future.

Flair Airlines is the worst airline with the worst service. They call themselves a “low cost carrier.” Let me tell you it’s a joke! After you pay for your luggage and your carry on and any other expenses you may have it’s the same as any other airline. Except with other airlines you get food, drinks and better service. They nickel and dime you for everything. Even their customer service agent said to me, “nothing is free with Flair Airlines.” The agent was rude and loud shouting across the floor for people to get their ID out and forcing everyone to measure their bags in these tights small spaces. She was watching everything and seemed to be gloat with people’s disappointment and challenges. Their service is inconsistent because going out to Calgary I paid for nothing - coming back all the customers were checked at 3 different locations. It seemed so militant, not friendly or kind at all. The price for a ticket is not worth the lack of service, empathy or kindness from their staff. I will not be flying them again, twice now and both times disappointed in a big way. Save yourself the trouble and fly with a professional airline.

My experience with LATAM on a domestic flight from Puerto Montt to Santiago was disappointing. The planes feel old and outdated, something I wouldn't expect from such a large airline. There was already a delay this morning, and now we're facing another one, but the worst part is the complete lack of information. The problem is the total lack of communication and available staff. There's no one to answer questions, and when you do manage to get some information, it's often incorrect or contradictory. Passengers are waiting at the airport with no updates or explanations. Delays can happen, but the lack of information and customer service is unacceptable. Overall, a very frustrating experience. LATAM needs to improve its communication, its airport staff, and how it handles passengers during delays.  Mi experiencia con LATAM en un vuelo nacional de Puerto Montt a Santiago fue decepcionante. Los aviones se sienten viejos y muy anticuados, algo que no esperaría de una aerolínea tan grande. Ya hubo un retraso en la mañana y ahora nuevamente estamos enfrentando otro retraso, pero lo peor es que no hay absolutamente ninguna información. El problema es la total falta de comunicación y de personal disponible. No hay nadie que responda preguntas, y cuando se logra obtener alguna información, muchas veces es incorrecta o contradictoria. Los pasajeros estamos esperando en el aeropuerto sin ninguna actualización ni explicación. Los retrasos pueden ocurrir, pero la ausencia de información y de servicio al cliente es inaceptable.En general, una experiencia muy frustrante. LATAM necesita mejorar su comunicación, su personal en aeropuerto y la forma en que maneja a sus pasajeros durante retrasos.

I was greeted with a welcome hand wipe upon boarding, and cup of tea & apple bun half way through the flight. Personable cabin crew, informative pilot, and a high degree of comfort with wide leather seats in the Embraer. Hard to fault, and am surprised LOT does not rate higher as an airline. Will be using them in the future instead of a few others due to the baggage allowance, and a free cup of tea in flight is a very nice touch.

Milan-Oslo-Tromso in Airbus A320 Neo. The aircraft looked pretty new and clean. The departure from Malpensa was delayed of 35 minutes, but all in all the flights were smooth and without problems. Seats were rather cramped. The free service was only for the, coffee and a glass of water: the rest was for payment. I had to pay also for the hand baggage. I believe this is really unacceptable for a flag carrier like SAS is . I expected more from them.

On our journey Bangalore – Bangkok – Siem Reap, our baggage was delayed by 28 hours, and we had to purchase essentials at our own expense. After repeated emails over 2 months, the airline offered only $60 total compensation, which we were asked to collect at Siem Reap Airport after we had already left Cambodia, making it impossible to receive. Despite multiple follow-ups explaining the circumstances and why purchase bills were unavailable, no response has been received.

The seats on the long haul leg were in a 2-3-2 configuration and very outdated in this day and age. The staff were quite curt in the way they interacted with me. This was felt in the lounge at Istanbul (very overcrowded with nowhere to sit down) when I tried to queue for the showers, I was lectured that the wait time would be two hours and that if I didn’t like it I could leave (I did not argue or prompt her in any way, this was her first/immediate response upon enquiring). On the flight, I (with a Japanese sounding name) was surprised to be served the Japanese meal without being asked for my preference. My food was pretty lackluster. The free wifi was intermittent (did not work for much of the flight), but I appreciated it when it did. I am quite easy when it comes to the hard/soft product, but the rudeness was something I could not tolerate.

I will say that it was inexpensive but they are very rules-oriented. I was prepared for that and managed my baggage and food and so on knowing it wasn't going to be a high level of service. However, onboard (after a pretty chaotic boarding process in Narita), I saw just how rigid and inflexible ZipAir intends to be with its fliers. Once we were in the air, they brought us the food we ordered and the experience felt like we were being handled our slop. Seats were par for the course - not the smallest I've flown, but not roomy and not comfortable. I fell asleep about 90 minutes into the flight which was good. However, the flight attendant woke me up to tell me to put on my seat belt (I took it off to get more comfortable). The seat belt sign was not on and there was no turbulence or other issue that required my seat belt to be on. I was more than annoyed, as I don't fall asleep easily on planes and wanted to sleep. 5 minutes later, another poke telling me to put it on. This continued throughout the flight. I explained that if the seat belt sign is on, I will put it on, but I'm leaving it off for my comfort so that I can sleep. This was unacceptable to them and they kept coming. They woke my wife up to tell her to tell me to put my seatbelt on. They had plastic placards that they walked up and down the aisles with, showing that they wanted seatbelts on. It was the most important thing that everyone comply with having their seatbelt on.

I purchased 2 first class tickets. Alaska oversold First Class. They downgraded one of our tickets to economy and handed me the 1-800 number for fare reimbursement. Now I’m 1.5 hours into waiting on hold to talk to someone about my reimbursement. This is not a quality airline and I would caution anyone from spending extra money on first class seats if they are not honored. At a minimum, they should have reimbursed my fare immediately at the gate.

The low fare they give is not worth the hassle of waiting in long check-in lines, departure delays and poor customer service.  Ihad arrived at the airport two hours early anticipating that there would be a decent-sized line but that it would only take 30 minutes maximum to check-in my baggage and get my boarding pass.  The line to check-in extended all the way from the counter to the entrance doorss. Due to the slow process of check-in, I had only an hour left before my flight was set to depart and I had to summon a member of the AirAsia staff to expedite my check-in. When I got to the counter after bypassing the line, I was informed by the agent that my flight had been delayed and that I would have to pay a fee because my luggage was more than the 15kg allowance I had paid for.  I was informed that they were charging me 2,799.98 THB (90.58 USD) in addition to the 385.20 THB (12.24 USD) I paid for my 15kg baggage allowance.  In total, my baggage fees amounted to 3,185.18 THB (101.29 USD). Once I paid the fee for my baggage, I proceeded through security to find out our flight was delayed.  After we boarded the plane, I saw that there were a couple emergency exit row seats available and asked one of the flight attendants if I could have that seat. They denied me the upgrade and said I had to pay for that seat.

At the gate, easyJet staff forced me to pay a very expensive oversize cabin baggage fee. While I understand that airlines have baggage rules, the way this situation was handled felt unreasonable and unfriendly. What made the situation even worse was the attitude of the gate staff. Instead of showing professionalism or explaining things calmly, the interaction felt rude and dismissive. As a passenger, you expect basic respect, especially when you are suddenly asked to pay a large amount of money at the gate with no real option to refuse. After this experience, I will think very carefully before flying with easyJet again.

This economy flight completely shocked me with how poor the service was. My route was LHR–MCO–LHR. On the flight to Orlando, the flight attendants were unbelievably rude. Their attitude was so aggressive that it genuinely felt uncomfortable. The “afternoon tea” consisted of a tiny sandwich and a single scone — that was it. The lunch portion was so small that even a child would still be hungry afterwards. Unfortunately, the return flight was no better. Once again, the flight attendants were rude and dismissive. When dinner was served, I asked for a tomato juice. The flight attendant, smiling, said, “I’ll get one for you.” Thirty minutes later, I had already finished my (again very small) dinner and she was clearing trays. I reminded her that she had forgotten my juice. Her response: “Oh, we’ll be serving that in a minute.” It never came. I eventually gave up waiting and tried to sleep. Perhaps they plan to send it to my home by post. Breakfast was the worst I have ever been served on any flight: a plain bagel. Nothing inside. No butter, no filling, not even a single leaf of lettuce — just a dry bagel. Even business class is not much better than economy, but I will spare the details to keep this review short. Virgin Atlantic used to have a reputation for good service. Based on this experience, that reputation is clearly long gone. Never again.

I purchased 2 first class tickets. Alaska oversold First Class. They downgraded one of our tickets to economy and handed me the 1-800 number for fare reimbursement. Now I’m 1.5 hours into waiting on hold to talk to someone about my reimbursement. This is not a quality airline and I would caution anyone from spending extra money on first class seats if they are not honored. At a minimum, they should have reimbursed my fare immediately at the gate.

Two weeks ago my wife and I flew Aeromexico from Toronto to Oaxaca via Mexico City. OThe flight was on-time; and the ground crew and in-flight crew were friendly and professional. A negative is that for a five-hour flight, there was no meal, only a snack comprising a modest sandwich and a bag of nuts. Also, no gluten-free alternative was available; I had called customer service ahead of time, and was told that since the flight had only a snack and not a meal, there was no gluten-free alternative. I had expected better. Also, I had originally booked economy but then cancelled in order to book AM Plus (premium economy). I received a refund for my economy fare, but the airline's policy is NOT to refund fees paid for baggage, seats, and what they call "Concierge Service". What other airline leaves you with seats on a flight that you've cancelled? In theory they will let you use your seat and baggage purchases for a future flight within a year, but since the AM Plus fare includes baggage and seats, the credits proved useless. I tried speaking to customer service about the matter on the phone, but the English-language agents that answered didn't speak English all that well, and also they gave me misinformation. I emailed the complaints department, but they saw their job as simply rigidly applying policies. As far as I can tell, the Aeromexico website doesn't disclose that the airline won't refund the entirely of a refundable ticket, but perhaps the information is hiding somewhere: their website is unintuitive, unreliable, and uninformative. We flew back on Air Canada, and were very happy with that.

I felt compelled to do a review of Air France as on the way out to Panama, especially the flight from London to Paris the service and the food was nothing short of excellent. On the way back from Panama to Paris, we had exactly the opposite experience. We were flying in business, only to be told that we didn’t have lounge access because we bought business light, the first l’d heard of it especially after we had lounge access at Heathrow! That aside, and because we judge an airline by its service and the quality of the food, what we were given on our flight from Panama was nothing short of poor. The starters came straight out of the refrigerator, making them tasteless because they were ice cold, that also included the cheese course. The main course was partly inedible because the carrots were sweetened and the sauce that went with the chicken seemed like it was a dessert sauce! The service was more like what would be expected on a two hour flight not a ten hour Atlantic crossing, as the cabin staff couldn’t get it down us quick enough, highlighted by the hot chocolate I had at the end of my dinner that would’ve been better served with ice. Just to add insult to injury, their Wi-Fi was not functioning and my inflight entertainment malfunctioned, the flight attendants didn’t seem too bothered about trying to attempt to fix either issue. Breakfast was a slightly better mix of good and bad! It seemed that if it were cold and just presented everything was fine, yogurt, fruit and croissant but if heat were applied it was nothing short of a disaster, my omelet was like a piece of rubber and the coffee was cold! It’s amazing how the two journeys with the same airline were so contrasting. One other thing I noticed was how grubby the aircraft was, stains, marks etc etc toilets that could do with a re-fit! I thought this was a relatively new A350? WThat will teach me to be influenced by price!

All airlines are not so strict regarding checked baggage weight. They leave upto 1.5 kg per person. Akasa air will not allow 100 grams also. A ladies hand bag and a computer bag is always allowed other than hand bag. They check your cabin bag weight also. The airline might be charging 300 to 400 rupees less than other carriers but they make money out of this. My weight allowance was 44 and the total weight of my baggage was 45.5. They charged for the excess. I bought two boxes of sweets which they pointed as hand baggage. My ladies bag was also pointed as hand bag. If you travel by Akasa be careful with your weight. Carry less kgs or be prepared to pay. Behaviour of the staff is also not good.

Both flights were on time and the flight from Manila to Melbourne was on a new A330-900 which was a huge improvement on the ancient 330 we traveled on recently from Manila to Brisbane. The staff were hard working and very attentive and polite. The food offerings were cheap and cheerful. The seats don't recline which I agree with and the plane was clean. When you have no expectations, it's great to be impressed by how great simple things like this are. I think for a 7 hour flight, you can't ask for more and it's nice to know that this is a cheap option to the full service carriers who charge so much more.

More like “Non Precision Air”. They issued numerous schedule changes, then delayed the flight and ultimately cancelled it and put me on a completely different flight number. The falsified online data and issued me a false boarding card to avoid triggering legal compensation requirements. 6.5 hr delay to my travel, no compensation, no customer service, no duty of care. On the return they changed the flight schedule again with no explanation, refused to book me onto an alternate flight or refund me. I had to book with an alternative airline to avoid significant costs and inconvenience. I would never recommend or fly them again. Suggest you review alternative airlines regardless of the cost because you’ll end up rebooking with someone else anyway and ultimately pay twice.

SAS is ignoring International Law  to avoid paying legitimate baggage delay claims. Our bags were delayed for 4 days in the Arctic (Lofoten). With no gear in sub-zero temperatures and a pre-paid ski itinerary, we were forced to buy technical safety equipment after 72 hours of SAS silence. Despite a documented loss of €2,020 for two passengers, SAS arbitrarily applied a 50% “lasting value” deduction, paying only €747. SAS has completely ignored our first claim for essentials, focusing only on applying illegal deductions to the second. Their customer service is a wall of copy-pasted scripts that ignore the law and the fact that we are two passengers with a combined legal limit of ~€3,700. Stop hiding behind internal policies and pay your passengers what you legally owe.

Return flights from Melbourne to Newcastle NSW. Smooth check-ins via the app in Melbourne, and at the counter in Newcastle. Priority boarding for Economy X worked well at both airports, and the seats had spacious legroom. The service was friendly and efficient. Hot beverages and water were available without charge. Baggage delivery was fast in Newcastle, much slower in Melbourne. On the outbound flight the pilot had to abandon their approach and go around again, but the plane landed on time. On the return flight, after boarding was complete the pilot advised that there was a technical fault and all passengers had to disembark. However, the disruption was handled well, with information and updates provided via the airport PA and the crew. The flight operated 90 mins late.

I booked a flight from San Diego Ca. To Minneapolis Minnesota & 1 stop in-between. While landing in Chicago to get to my next flight I get a text from united airlines saying my flight has been canceled. I ended up having to pay my sister to drive from Alabama to take me to Minneapolis $130 for gas. I didn't get the insurance for my ticket & I know that I couldnt be reimbursed but it wasn't my fault that United cancelled my flight due to weather. I asked to be at least half of my flight due to then canceling my flight & they told me no due to the weather. Nor would they reimburse me for having to call for a ride. They should have never booked my flight knowing what the weather was going to be like because they know.
