Flew business class Mumbai to San Jose via Amsterdam. Bad food on both legs, mine was almost non edible. The Amsterdam lounge is full & bursting with people. Most of cabin crew doing lazy customer service. Lastly, in the second leg the business class seat was broken. Not worth the money with this airline.

A quick hop internal UK flight London to Belfast. One hour of Fantastic flight. On time left early and arrived 20 minutes early. Pleasant crew. All for under $20 how can one fault Ryanair. I do use regularly and almost entirely enjoyed the experience which of course is a much different model to the legacy carriers. But spot on.

So disappointed. I’ve been flying Southwest for a long time. Their new changes are not making my experience better. But after a two hour delay, changing gates, and almost making me check in to a wrong flight, they made my daughter check in her overhead bag because it was a full fight. When we got to our seats, because we were group 6, there was plenty of space in the overhead bins. I will definitely start looking at other airlines when I make reservations. I’m not a frequent flyer, maybe twice a year. The Dallas airport was a big mess.

A nice experience flying Air India from Mumbai to Dehradun in Premium Economy. The check-in was smooth and pleasant. There is a separate check-in island for First, Business, Premium Economy which was not crowded. The flight was very pleasant, breakfast was tasty and adequate for a morning flight with multiple juice and tea/coffee runs. The aircraft was well-maintained and the only let-down was that the streaming entertainment service did not seem to be operational.

They may get you to come to the airport, wait hours, and delay it multiple times, only to in the very last minute cancel the flight and leave you stranded, barely an apology and no refund due to unforeseen circumstances even though in the speaker they advised that the very first 3 delays were due to crew requirement. Now we stranded in a Friday and the only next available flight is Sunday.

I was the first one in line to check in around 7.40 am on Sunday 8 March for flight from Brussels to Rome. The check-in took 30 minutes, with the woman saying that because I requested wheelchair assistance only certain seats could be assigned. Yet that wait, I was given the same seat, 7C, as the boarding pass on my Easy Jet app already showed! I walked to wheelchair assistance, waited around 10 minutes and was taken to the gate. No-one ever said there was a problem. Yet when I got to the gate I was curtly told that I was too late, the doors were closed. I had to wait 10-12 hours for the next EasyJet flight to Rome, which landed around 11 pm.  No apology at the airport. No interest in my plight.

Iberia lost my suitcase on this trip and I was reunited with it three days later. The response from Iberia washed their hands of any responsibility for losing my suitcase at Madrid Airport because they said the leg Madrid to London was operated by British airways. I quote: “According to the agreement between airlines, the airline that operated the last flight is responsible for the baggage delivery and its claim. When BA operated the first flight and we operate the last one, we are responsible for the baggage claim. However, in your case, BA is the one responsible.” I did receive an email from Iberia the following day saying: “Yesterday your flight landed on time in Madrid. We go the extra mile on every flight so that you can enjoy your planes as you have arranged”. Perhaps they are on time because they do not load luggage into the hold? Their position is absurd given that my trip started in Vigo with Iberia and unless I'm mistaken British Airways does not handle baggage operations at Madrid airport for Iberia or anyone else, Iberia does. Since 2021 I've taken 3 Iberia trips Vigo to London with checked luggage, and they have lost my suitcase twice out of the three times which is also absurd.  It is not possible to enter the Iberia VIP lounge at Madrid Airport terminal 4 as there is a very long queue shown in the photo where you would only gain entry if you had two plus hours to wait in the queue. Iberia does an excellent transformation of a product sold as premium into rubbish.

Traveling from Boston to San Diego on March 12, 2026, 2 1/2 hours into the flight we were told there was a problem getting fuel to the engine so we had to turn around and go back to Boston. Very heavy turbulence that day. The captain told us we would have to fly around in circles for a while to burn off the tool because we couldn’t land with all that fuel. My companion was very airsick. We got off the plane in Boston and were told we could see the gate agent to rebook. I spoke with the gate agent and requested to be put on the next days flight March 13. The gate agent was not at all friendly and seemed to put off by the fact that she had to do any work. My companion and I were discussing taking the next day flight and gate agent said so am I doing this or what? We told her yes we would like to be booked on the next days flight and she said you’re all set, I can’t check you into your flight tomorrow because it’s more than 24 hours away, but you should be able to check in 2 hours from now.I went to check into my flight for the next day and nothing had been updated. Turns out the gate agent put us in for a flight later on the 12th instead of the 13th and by now we were at a hotel and couldn’t make that flight. So I called customer service at JetBlue and the woman I spoke with was less than friendly and completely unhelpful. She told me that I couldn’t change the flight, I would have to cancel and rebook. I asked her if she could do that for me and she said no. I went to the app to cancel the flight and rebook and the app didn’t work for that. So I called customer service again, both times calling customer service. I had to wait over 45 minutes to speak with someone, this is unacceptable. I spoke to the second person at customer service and she told me that the flight on the 13th was fully booked but she was able to cancel that flight. so now we had no way to get to San Diego in our timeframe. We looked at multiple other airlines, and it was cost prohibitive because we still had money into the JetBlue tickets. In the end, we had to cancel our whole trip because the gate agent messed up our booking and not one apology or offer to help in anyway came from JetBlue. I called again later and was able to get a refund, but the whole experience left us disappointed, and disenchanted with JetBlue. I used to like this airline, but after being treated like we were an inconvenience when it was their mistake is a real problem for me. I won’t be booking on JetBlue again.

I had an awful experience with frontier. I was traveling alone with my two children from Minneapolis to Orlando. We have a short layover in Dallas. The first part of our flight was fine. Our flight from Dallas to Orlando was delayed 4 times. Then after 7.5 hours of waiting at the airport they cancelled our flight completely leaving my children and I stranded In an unknown city. Customer service was awful saying there would be no help with hotel comps and the next flight out was over 24 hours later. My children and I were left stranded in the airport for 18 hours before I could book a flight out with another airline (at the price of a small fortune). Frontier does not care and refunded me a couple hundred dollars which was not even enough to cover one ticket.

They did not weigh our bags at the check in counter, yet when we boarded the flight they weighed our carry on luggage and deemed it to be 10 kg overweight. If this was told to us during the check in process, then we would have checked in the extra kgs into our luggage, because we had all checked in luggage worth over 10kg of free space. They made us feel forced to pay 4000 baht and to pay this at the gate, and would not let us pay later by card or even listen to our explanation that we had paid for baggage that was not being utilized.

My experience with SWISS International Air Lines was by far the worst airline experience I have ever had. I was traveling from Geneva to Los Angeles via Zurich on a single SWISS ticket. My Geneva flight arrived on time, but we were forced to bus to the terminal and then take the airport train to the international gates. Passport control was severely backed up, and despite moving as fast as possible, I arrived at Gate E19 while boarding was still happening and the aircraft door was still open but I was refused boarding by the gate manager. I was told only that there were “several reasons” and that they did not have to tell me what they were. When I tried to explain the delays caused by airport transfers and customs lines, I was dismissed and treated with complete indifference.  I was passed between multiple desks with no clear guidance and ultimately told I had to pay to rebook my flight the next day. I was given no hotel, no meals, and no assistance despite being stranded overnight. Only days later, after I requested a refund, SWISS suddenly claimed I had engaged in unruly behavior. This was never mentioned at the airport and appears to be an attempt to justify their decision after the fact.  What should not happen is an airline refusing to explain decisions, treating customers without professionalism, and making questionable accusations afterward.

We paid £455 each for Premium Economy upgrade in May 2025 on an 8-hour flight. The in-flight entertainment system at both of our seats did not work. Cabin crew attempted several resets but it never worked. By the time meal service reached our row, the advertised meal choices had run out. The Wonder Wall snack area was also empty with no crew nearby to replenish it. In reality the experience ended up being worse than our outbound flight in Economy. Virgin Atlantic later offered a £100 voucher. Their terms state in small print that onboard services cannot be guaranteed – despite these being key features used to justify the Premium Economy price. For us, paying nearly £1,000 for an upgrade that delivered fewer working services than Economy was extremely disappointing.
Ground staff at NGO were rude to me and did not explain lounge information or put Priority tags on my bags, causing a delay at the luggage carousel in Bangkok.

My flight on Citilink QG680 from Soekarno–Hatta International Airport to Ngurah Rai International Airport aboard an Airbus A320 was an overall typical low-cost carrier experience: functional but unremarkable. The ticket was purchased via an OTA and felt somewhat expensive for an LCC, with the airline assigning a random middle seat unless passengers paid for seat selection, though the airport experience at the newly refurbished Terminal 1C was pleasant with friendly staff and a smooth baggage drop at 1 a.m. Boarding started slightly early but without a clear announcement and required a bus ride to a -very- remote stand before stair boarding, yet the process remained surprisingly orderly and better managed than some higher-rated airlines. The cabin was clean but showing age with tight legroom, no entertainment, Wi-Fi or charging ports, while the crew were friendly and professional; the flight departed on time, arrived about ten minutes early, baggage arrived in good condition after roughly fifteen minutes, and overall I would consider flying Citilink again if the fare is competitive.

We requested an upgrade on our seats for more legroom, paid the $90, and they charged my credit card twice, so $180. After 7 phone calls and 3 emails, the charges were supposed to be reversed, but never were. Airplane itself was shabby. I will not fly this airline again.

Yesterday I experienced the rudest customer service in my entire life. At nearly 11 PM, I went to the customer service desk near terminal C11 at DFW to get a hotel voucher, because delays had caused me to miss a connecting flight. The agent was dismissive of my situation and was whispering amongst his fellow staff as if he was at a high school lunch table. When I overheard whispers of my voucher being denied and asked for clarification, the agent exclaimed, "That's right, you get nothing!" with a smirk on his face. He claimed that, because the delay was due to air traffic control, the airline was not at fault, yet the plane in question hadn't even landed at the expected boarding time. So not only did his hostile behavior make me feel unwelcome during a confusing and frustrating time, he also didn't even do his job correctly.

They canceled the flight and scheduled another one over a day later. The airline didn't provide breakfast at the hotel, and after a long plea, they even gave me an Uber voucher. Despite having purchased tickets with reserved seats for the canceled flight, without giving a reason, just before boarding the flight, they ordered me to buy new seats, for which I had to pay twice as much as the first time, without any possibility of reversing the price difference, which is embarrassing. The next day, boarding took forever ... who knows how many classes in a ridiculous single-class A321. Boarding took 40 minutes, and the plane took off again with a delay. It's a travesty, not an airline. You're far from European standards.

My experience with KLM Royal Dutch Airlines has been extremely disappointing and unacceptable. On 20 December 2025 I was travelling on flight KL1257 from Amsterdam to Rovaniemi. Due to a delay of the incoming flight, we missed our connecting flight and were forced to stay overnight in Amsterdam. At Amsterdam Airport Schiphol, we went to the KLM service desk to request assistance. Instead of providing the hotel, meals and transport that airlines are required to offer in these situations, KLM staff told us to pay for everything ourselves and claim reimbursement afterwards. Trusting this information, we paid out of pocket for accommodation, food and transport and submitted all receipts afterwards through their official claims process. What followed has been a frustrating and exhausting experience. After more than two months of waiting and several emails, KLM Customer Care has refused to reimburse these expenses. Their replies completely ignore the actual issue and repeatedly refer to “extraordinary circumstances” as if this somehow cancels their responsibilities. This is misleading. Under Regulation (EC) No 261/2004, airlines have a duty of care toward passengers when delays cause an overnight stay. This duty applies regardless of the cause of the delay, including air traffic control restrictions or weather. The airline must provide or reimburse meals, accommodation and transport. Instead of acknowledging this obligation, KLM’s customer service has simply repeated generic responses and closed the case without addressing the legal basis of the claim. The most frustrating part is not even the delay itself. Delays happen and most passengers understand that aviation is complex. What is unacceptable is the way the situation was handled afterwards: passengers left to cover necessary expenses themselves and then ignored for months when asking for reimbursement. Customer service should exist to solve problems, not to exhaust passengers until they give up. After this experience, I cannot recommend flying with KLM. If something goes wrong during your trip, be prepared to handle the consequences alone and spend months chasing the airline for costs they are legally required to cover. This experience has completely destroyed my trust in the company and I will avoid flying with KLM in the future whenever possible.

My recent flight with VietJet Air was smooth and comfortable. The airport procedures were efficient. The cabin crew were polite, the aircraft was clean and the atmosphere on board was pleasant. Considering it is a low-cost airline, the service and overall experience were good.

This is the worst nightmare my children and I have ever experienced, the staff is so unhelpful and not trained, i felt terrible from the moment I checked in on top of that charged me for a flight with was full and my children and I were put on a stand by status without previous notice, I was told at check in I was assigned whichever seat they had available and when I get to Guadalajara to speak to agent to accommodate my children and I close to each other, but when arrived at Guadalajara not only was the flight delayed 3 hours but we were told they had a full flight.

Great airline! Efficient, mostly on time and full service. On the 50 minutes flight to Koh Samui and back you get a meal, water, tea or coffee and juice. And another round if you like. Hard working crew gets it all done in a short time. Fairly high price though because there's no competition on the BKK-USM route. They even own USM Airport, which has a great open feeling, Very good!

The cabin crew are friendly and the airplane is quite new, so that was a plus. Everything else was disappointing for the money paid. The seats look old already, and the finishing were dirty and broken. At least the seat was a private pod with full recline where you can rest. Service was pleasant and friendly, but the food was not good - dry and lukewarm. Service still was a bit lacking - promising things then never delivering, which happened twice. The inflight entertainment is very limited and the wifi was not reliable. The worst part is transferring through Addis Airport. The transfer process is very disorganized, crowded and stressful. The lounge is relatively new, but no coffee machines were working at 7am when I arrived, there were few places to sit and the food quality was very low. I definitely cannot recommend Ethiopian unless you have to take them. Could be much better.

American Airlines asks for $7,200 for a one-way flight in Business Class from London to Los Angeles. What they sell you over their basic economy product is a better seat, etter service, better catering. Well, they failed on every account on this flight. Seat was tiny had to contort my legs just to get into it. No power at the seat. No WIFI for the 11 hour flight (stewardess said it was because there were too many people using it, yet the issue was that it just doesn't connect. No pre-boarding drink unless you take something off the tray they bring (I do not drink alcohol and do not like citrus juice so had to wait 75" for a coca cola.  No menu, and they served an economy meal on stone plates. I especially like the classy touch of placing a bacon wrapped vienna sausage on a bed of pesto sauce -- it is as disgusting as it sounds. And the salty sauce over the chicken breast had little bits of salty corn kernels. The second meal was better but who eats breakfast at seven o'clock in the evening?  I sent a complaint about what I considered was "services not provided," and pointed out that the fare different between what I paid and what I received was in the thousands of dollars and asked for a modest measure of compensation in a future upgrade certificate. Instead, I was offered 10,000 miles (street value $100); when I said that's hardly adequate, they upped it by $25 (2,500 miles). If I'd known that they had downgraded their usual poor service even further, I could have flown to Dallas on Finnair and connected on a short / flight on AAL to LAX or could have chosen to fly BA LHR LAX, but how can anyone know about or predict such a fiendish and deceptive practice was in the works?

We had a shortish turnround in Quito. I asked for assistance from Iberia staff in Madrid, on the aircraft and would have done so in Quito had any Iberia staff appeared but I was met with a steely determination to do nothing. "You won't need assistance, you'll have plenty of time" was the repeated refrain. The departure was late, the arrival was late, the baggage was delayed and we duly missed our connection. Iberia staff were conspicuous by their absence, staying inside their office until they could go home.

The outbound and return flights were on time. Booking was easy, and the Iberia airport staff were wonderful. Extremely friendly, especially in New York—my compliments. Unfortunately, not everything was wonderful. And I'm not referring to the food we were given during the flight, which sadly left much to be desired and was quite disappointing. What was truly awful was the sandwich they gave us in the morning: soft and chewy, with horrible cheese and greasy, tasteless salami. In short: it was inedible, and most of the passengers had to throw it away. I would have paid 10 euros to see a flight attendant finish one (quite a challenge!). I honestly found it shameful for the airline, which is supposed to be a calling card, but also, incidentally, for Spain, since the food they offer on the flight is the first impression of our cuisine for many foreigners. It's possibly the worst sandwich I've ever been offered, because, despite being hungry after a 7-hour flight, I couldn't stomach it. Please, Iberia, put in a little more effort; you're making us look terrible. The safety instructions are very original; they appear in a video showcasing our beautiful cities, music, etc., and for that, they deserve praise. The flight crew was also very friendly and attentive. It's a shame that because of those inedible sandwiches, we all left with a bad taste in our mouths. El vuelo de ida y de vuelta han ido puntuales. Ha sido fácil hacer la reserva y el personal del aeropuerto de Iberia ha sido maravilloso. Extremadamente amable, especialmente en Nueva York, mis felicitaciones. Desgraciadamente, no todo ha sido maravilloso. Y no me refiero a la comida que nos han dado durante el vuelo, que desgraciadamente deja mucho que desear y es bastante decepcionante. Lo que ha sido realmente horrible ha sido el bocadillo que nos han dado por la mañana: blando y chicloso, con un queso horripilante y un salami grasiento y sin sabor. En definitiva: NO se podía comer y la mayor parte de los viajeros lo tuvimos que tirar a la basura. Habría pagado 10 euros por ver a un auxiliar de vuelo terminase uno (!todo un reto!) Sinceramente me pareció vergonzoso para la compañía que es un tarjeta de presentación, pero también, de paso, para España, ya que la comida que ofrecen en el vuelo es la primera impresión de nuestra gastronomía para muchos extranjeros. Es posible que sea el peor bocadillo que me han ofrecido en mi vida, pues, a pesar de que tenía hambre después de 7 horas de vuelo, no pude tragármelo. Por favor, señores de Iberia, esmérense un poco más, que nos están dejando a la altura del betún. Las instrucciones de seguridad son muy originales, aparecen en un video que muestra nuestras bellas ciudades, la música, etc y por esto hay que felicitarles. El personal del avión también ha sido muy amable y atento. Lástima que por culpa de esos bocadillos incomestibles nos hayamos ido todos con un mal sabor de boca.

I am extremely disappointed with LATAM Airlines and the misleading information provided by their call center. I contacted LATAM’s call center to get assistance purchasing a round-trip ticket for my minor daughter from Bogotá, Colombia to Sydney, Australia, and back to Bogotá. My main concern was the return flight. I explained that there was a possibility that my daughter might remain with me in Australia depending on visa circumstances, and I wanted to purchase the ticket in a way that would allow me to recover most of the money if the return flight was not used. The LATAM call center agent advised me to purchase the outbound ticket with the Light fare (the cheapest option) and the return ticket with the Full fare, explaining that if the return flight was not used I would be able to request a partial refund of the unused ticket. Trusting this advice, I proceeded to purchase the tickets exactly as recommended. Later, we used the flight from Bogotá to Sydney. Fortunately, thanks to a decision by the Australian government, my daughter was able to stay in Australia and did not need to use the return ticket to Colombia. I contacted LATAM again to ask how to request the refund for the unused return flight. To my surprise, the agent told me that the only amount that could be refunded were the airport taxes, approximately $200, even though the ticket had cost more than $2000. This was frustrating because it was different from the information given when I bought the ticket, especially considering that I paid a more expensive Full fare specifically to have refund flexibility. Even so, I submitted the refund request through their website hoping they would review the situation properly, since the ticket had been purchased under the Full fare conditions. Unfortunately, the result was exactly the same: LATAM only refunded the airport taxes. When I complained through their customer service page, their response was that I should have requested the refund before using the first flight of the ticket, which was never explained to me when I purchased it. This situation shows very poor customer advice, lack of clarity, and inconsistent information from their staff. I feel misled and very disappointed by this experience.

My flight from Bangkok to Prague on 15 March was canceled due to the Middle East conflict 3 days before departure via email. No alternative was provided other than a flight a week later. ​Zero Communication: I sent 6 emails, tried the hotline repeatedly, used Live Chat, and reached out on X but absolute silence. No offer of accommodation, meals, no realistic re-routing options. I was forced to buy a new ticket with China Airlines at my own expense to get home

By far the cheapest option on short notice between Amsterdam and Bangkok. Paid little over 800 euros for a return. which was a very good price. Got the chance of an upgrade to business class however for a good price and decided to treat myself. From the moment you step on board you feel welcome. Adressed by your name and the stewardesses introduce themselves. Welcome drinks, dine on demand, great food, a great lie-flat seat and the cabin almost felt homely. Second leg equally good. I love the lounge in the A380. Relaxed boarding and out in no time.  Unfortunately my return flight was cancelled 4 times due to the conflict in the Middle East. I must say that I saw a lot of complaints about QR in which the airline was accused of not responding or not being reachable. My experience is different. I had to call them 4 times and I must I got through pretty quick. Yes, off course there is a waiting time in such an extreme situation. They easily booked me on a new flight every time it was cancelled. Since I could work from Thailand, I was not in a big hurry to get a flight home. After the last cancellation I requested to book me on another airline. Which was granted promptly.

Bangkok to Taipei and Taipei to Kumamoto with Starlux, both were direct flights. I was in Economy class. I had a good experience except when I asked for white wine with my lunch, the flight attendant poured about 10 to 15 ml into the plastic cup and handed to me.
A good all round solid flight. No mishaps, flight left on time. The cabin crew were friendly enough. Food was ok to good. I did manage to get at least 7 hours sleep, so happy all round.

I will never fly with Spirit again. The flight wasn't the issue. The issue was the delayed flight leaving Cancun for whatever reason and arriving in Ft Lauderdale to find our flight for LaGuardia had already left. Poor poor planning on the airline, nothing rescheduled or rebooked. Just sorry. Sorry doesn't cut it. No comp offered. Nothing. Has to get a hotel for 2 nights, Uber ride to the hotel, not to mention meals until we can fly out Monday afternoon. Our pets have to stay at the kennel for an additional 2 days, more expense. The staff at Ft Lauderdale was rude. Flights are cheap and that's what we got. Cheap. Spend the extra money for your flight.

First they delayed our flight by 2 hrs. After landing we sat for >1 hr with seatbelts on. We had 12 people on our flight who missed their connection to Dallas. We had one passenger who missed international flight. Our family are exhausted. We are still sitting on the plane and there is no gate for us. They did not offer us a drink or did not let us use the bathroom.

Our flight ended up being canceled for mechanical issues. I was upset I was going to lose a day of spring break vacation and i had no idea how I was going to ask for my flight back to be extended a day later to not lose out on vacation time. With no humans to speak with i thought it was going to be a nightmare. I texted the number available on the app, and was pleasantly surprised when I got a response to my inquiry about changing my return flight. Whoever I was speaking to was great! Immediately gave me options for a nonstop return flight, unfortunately, it wasn't until sunday and I needed to be back by friday. They were able to offer me 2 choices of return flights with a layover for Friday. So all is well that ends well. Much appreciated Breeze airlines!

La Palma airport very easy to navigate and Check-in at designated Discover counters very quick. Unfortunately no Lounge available and = no Vouchers for the restaurant distributed. Boarding in Groups respected, friendly welcome of the motivated and young crew. Meals (2 choices) were ok, but nothing special. However, as the flight was full is business class, the staff had to work really hard, despite she offered numerous drink refills during the whole flight which was appreciated. Otherwise the usual European Businness Class with enough legroom and the empty middle seat. I would rate the service from Discover over Lufthansa and sure over Condor Airlines especially due to the motivated crew

I had a very frustrating experience with Delta Air Lines. I purchased two tickets in November 2025 for a flight from Buenos Aires to Dublin. Due to my daughter lacking a transit visa, we had to cancel the trip. A Delta representative told me that paying an additional USD 450 upgrade would make our tickets refundable. I followed all instructions, paid the upgrade, and was later assured that the refund (more than USD3000) was initiated. However, I have never received the refund, nor has Delta responded for over 30 days, despite repeatedly contacting them. At one point, Delta tried to replace the refund with an eCredit, which I rejected because I paid extra specifically to get my money back in my account. Additionally, the agent instructed me to send false medical documentation after my case was misclassified as a medical cancellation, something I refused to do. Throughout this process, Delta’s communication has been confusing, inconsistent, and unprofessional. I do not recommend relying on Delta for refunds, and I would caution other travelers about their customer service.

I’m at Maui airport right now and my flight from delta got canceled last minute, last night “due to weather” but many airlines still departing. I tried to find a delta employee or customer service in the airport and for my surprise no one could be found. I called delta customer service and the only option was to flight 3 days later, no help finding us a hotel, no vouchers for food or transportation, nothing! I purchased last minute Southwest and leaving here today. When I called customer service and asked details about getting refunded their reply was very vague and they were not sure of anything! I only flight delta and sky miles member for years. Terrible customer service. Don’t ever flight to Hawaii with delta. I’m done being delta loyal member.

How is this airline in business? An absolute joke. Sitting on the tarmac with no information after our flight was changed numerous times. Then we had to wait 5 hours for a pilot change. This is the most insane experience flying ever. Nobody tells you anything

Beware of checking bags with American Airlines. I had a nearly brand-new suitcase that had only been used once before this trip, and it came back damaged. The TSA lock and zipper were broken, also the rubber in the area appeared to be to be the location pried to break the lock. When I received the bag the zipper had been pulled all the way down to the bottom. I contacted Customs, and they confirmed they did not search my bag since I never received a notice of inspection. I then reported this to American Airlines, but their central baggage specialist claimed the damage was due to “normal wear and tear.” That explanation doesn’t make sense when the locking mechanism was broken and the zippers were repositioned to the bottom of the bag. If luggage were simply tossed around during handling, the zipper would likely only break at the lock, and not be fully moved down the track. On top of that, one of the foot studs on the bottom of the suitcase was also broken off. My luggage was completely intact when I checked it. It’s frustrating that their decision was based only on the three photos they allow you to submit with the claim. This suitcase was basically new and had only been used once prior to this trip. Based on this experience, I strongly recommend keeping your luggage with you in the cabin if possible.

The flight was delayed and the way they treat carry one is absurd. Why call it carry on and then take it away and throw it in the luggage compartment? Then the snacks were cheap ... they charge $400 dollars for a 3 hour flight and can't provide decent snacks and beverages? That is cheap.

Onboard we were addressed by name and pre flight drinks were offered and crew were very friendly polite. The meal was very good. Once airborne they very quickly came around confirmed our meal orders and were quick to offer drinks. There was 2 crew members working in the first class cabin and were excellent. I was slightly disappointed that the headphones that used to be handed out in domestic first were already discontinued and we had to bring our own. if not they only had the in ear earbuds available on request for free to first class passengers.

BKK-KWI-FRA in July 2025. Check In at BKK Airport was quick and friendly staff. BKK-KWI sector on B777-300ER new clean and comfortable aircraft with 3-3-3 configuration. Shortly after on time departure cabin crew served only non alcoholic drinks and cabin light was turn off. 3 hours before landing 2 choices (western and asian) was served. Food was delicious. Transit at KWI Airport was smooth and quick. KWI-FRA departure at bus gate I told the gate staff that I could not step the stairs well and requested the boarding asistance. They said yes, they would do that but nothings was happend at boarding so I had to caimb 33 steps. On board new A330-800 neo I had a great experience. Cabin Crew were very attentive and helpfll. Seating comfortable the 2-4-2 configuration great legroom and recline. Shorty after departure Lunch (arabic lamb and western chicken) was served with plenty of non alcoholic drinks. Food was adequate. IFE average. During the flights cabin crew offered water and juices several times. 90 minutes before landing at FRA chicken sandwiches and drinks was serve. Great flight with great aircraft with great value for money.

After 14 years of flying almost exclusively with Southwest Airlines, I never expected to be writing a review like this—but my most recent experience was extremely disappointing. For over a decade, I chose Southwest because it was different. The airline built its reputation on simplicity, transparency, and customer service that actually felt genuine. That’s why I left airlines like United and Delta and became loyal to Southwest. Unfortunately, that experience seems to be gone. First, the pricing structure now feels like constant nickel-and-diming. I paid full price for what was essentially the most expensive ticket available on my flight because it advertised extra legroom and a better boarding position. Yet during check-in, I was immediately prompted to upgrade again to “Premier” for another $27. If I’ve already purchased one of the highest-priced tickets, why am I still being asked to pay more just to improve my boarding position? Even with the higher-priced ticket, there was very little real value. Boarding Group 1 still meant standing in line with dozens of other passengers, competing for seats just like everyone else. The “benefits” felt almost nonexistent compared to what other airlines provide at similar or lower prices. To make matters worse, the same carry-on bag I’ve used on Southwest flights for the last 14 years was suddenly considered too large and I was required to check it. That was another unexpected cost added to an already expensive ticket. The service also felt very different from the Southwest culture I used to appreciate. In the past, their staff were known for being friendly and personable. On this trip, interactions felt rushed and indifferent—far from the experience that once set Southwest apart. Finally, every leg of my trip was delayed. I eventually reached my destination, but everything ran late and the overall travel experience felt frustrating rather than reliable. What’s most disappointing is that Southwest used to stand out. Today it feels like they’ve adopted the exact same pricing tactics and service model as the airlines many of us originally left. After 14 years of loyalty, I’ll be using the remaining miles I have and then moving on to another airline. Sadly, the Southwest that earned that loyalty no longer seems to exist

Booked months in advance for a special anniversary trip, we selected and confirmed our Business Class seats during online check-in. Despite this, seats were changed multiple times without notice, and on the Istanbul–Bali flight, the seats we originally booked were occupied by other passengers. Most seriously, my wife and another passenger appeared to hold the same seat. Cabin crew confirmed our assignment, but the other passenger refused to move, leaving my wife standing in tears in a busy Business Class cabin. The airline requested documentation proving our family relationship to investigate, which we provided promptly, yet it appears this was never meaningfully considered. Slap in the face pretty much. This represents a serious operational and procedural failure. Turkish Airlines must improve its seat allocation, boarding processes, and complaint handling, particularly for long-haul premium passengers. We are currently in a longstanding feedback conversation with Customer Relations and just keep getting generic responses. Disgraceful.

Overall pleasantly surprised by my recent flights especially the 15 1/2 hour non stop sector from Sydney to Houston. Staff were friendly and efficient, the aircraft clean and comfortable, and the food (AVML) was excellent.

Overall pleasantly surprised by my recent flights especially the 15 1/2 hour non stop sector from Sydney to Houston. Staff were friendly and efficient, the aircraft clean and comfortable, and the food (AVML) was excellent.

Our flight from Spokane to Lihue, HI was cancelled due to mechanical issues. That part is understandable. What isn’t is how you’re treated afterwards. First we line up at the gate agent along with the rest of the plane. We’re told it might be faster to scan a bar code to start a chat with an Alaska rep to change our flight. While that’s pending, I called Alaska’s 800 number. The recording said my call would be answered in 8 hours. After about 3 hours waiting in line, we get to the gate agent. Still no response on the chat initiated hours earlier. We finally get rebooked for the following day. A more circuitous route with seat assignments either in the absolute last row by the bathroom or non-existent forcing us to pay to upgrade just to get a decent seat on the 6 hour leg of our flight. Another call to Alaska when we got home after 7 hours at the airport, got an agent who helped us get an assigned seat on a leg where we had none at all. That was a speedy 2 hour wait. My main complaint is that Alaska’s customer service is terrible. There is no dedicated number to call when you need to rearrange your life for the next 24 hours. Instead, it’s a completely frustrating experience followed by an exceptionally insulting weak apology letter with an accompanying tiny flight credit to be used with plenty of restrictions. If we didn’t have to depend on Alaska Airlines as it’s the largest carrier in our area, I would never fly this airline!

The communication was absolutely horrific. They cancelled my flight 4 hours before it was set to depart and forced me onto another flight 2 days later, but then refused to offer me any accommodations or compensation.

The communication was absolutely horrific. They cancelled my flight 4 hours before it was set to depart and forced me onto another flight 2 days later, but then refused to offer me any accommodations or compensation.

Our flight from Spokane to Lihue, HI was cancelled due to mechanical issues. That part is understandable. What isn’t is how you’re treated afterwards. First we line up at the gate agent along with the rest of the plane. We’re told it might be faster to scan a bar code to start a chat with an Alaska rep to change our flight. While that’s pending, I called Alaska’s 800 number. The recording said my call would be answered in 8 hours. After about 3 hours waiting in line, we get to the gate agent. Still no response on the chat initiated hours earlier. We finally get rebooked for the following day. A more circuitous route with seat assignments either in the absolute last row by the bathroom or non-existent forcing us to pay to upgrade just to get a decent seat on the 6 hour leg of our flight. Another call to Alaska when we got home after 7 hours at the airport, got an agent who helped us get an assigned seat on a leg where we had none at all. That was a speedy 2 hour wait. My main complaint is that Alaska’s customer service is terrible. There is no dedicated number to call when you need to rearrange your life for the next 24 hours. Instead, it’s a completely frustrating experience followed by an exceptionally insulting weak apology letter with an accompanying tiny flight credit to be used with plenty of restrictions. If we didn’t have to depend on Alaska Airlines as it’s the largest carrier in our area, I would never fly this airline!

The flight itself was smooth, and the flight attendants were professional and doing their best. However, there was virtually nothing offered onboard, only one round of drinks, and coffee or water had to be requested. For a paid service on an expensive flight, offering a small snack like a cheap bar or chips feels inadequate and disappointing. Additionally, the flight was advertised as having Wi-Fi, but there was none. There were no screens or even basic route information available, which made the experience feel very bare. As an Aeroplan member, I was also surprised to be charged for luggage despite traveling with just one piece, which should have been included. This was frustrating and felt unreasonable. For a late evening flight (9:30 PM), when passengers often don’t have access to dinner beforehand, the lack of proper food and beverage service is especially noticeable. Basic offerings like coffee, tea, water, and more substantial snacks should be standard—not something passengers need to ask for. Air Canada needs to invest more in onboard service and ensure that what is advertised is actually delivered. At current prices, the level of service provided is simply not acceptable.

Unexceptional Business Class, with normal airline food. Staff were pleasant enough. Aircraft old and tired. Business Class not worth the price on this short route. I had high hopes for Cathay's revival post covid, but they're not there yet. Check-in at BKK was smooth and efficient.

No fast track for Biz Class security, but maybe that's the new normal. Lounge at Pier Wing very large, but well able to cope with the many who are entitled to use it. Good selection of everything. Uneventful Business Class on board, with normal food. Staff were very pleasant and professional. Aircraft old and tired, like most on this sector. Business Class certainly not worth the price on this short route.

I recently flew on flight LO71 on 20th March and wanted to highlight two exceptional crew members. Mateusz handled a genuinely difficult situation with another passenger with complete professionalism and grace — calm, firm, and kind throughout. It’s not easy to manage that kind of situation mid-flight and he did it brilliantly. Natalia went truly above and beyond. I was suffering from a severe headache during the flight and she checked on me multiple times, helped me get medication, and made sure I was comfortable. Both of them are a credit to LOT Polish Airlines.

I was blown away by the service, particularly on board, but also in the airport. I normally fly BA but had to buy a last minute ticket with Tianjin due to the issues in the Middle East. Of over 50 long haul business class trips, this was amongst the top few, maybe even the best. From opening my slipper bag to making the bed, with mattress, sheet, duvet and extra pillow, high quality Rituals amenity bag, pyjamas to the food (Chinese and Western options), and overall genuine care and attention to detail. Thank you to all the crew, you made a long flight very enjoyable!

Had to wait for check-in to open 3hours before departure. Pre purchased additional bag 22kg, AUD 50. Had purchased bundle seat, meal and additional 5kg baggage. Delayed departure approx 35mins due to late arrival of aircraft. Welcomed on board with a smile, crew proactively helped passengers find seats and assisted with placing bags in overhead lockers. Flight was may be 50% full Service commenced with bottles of water shortly after takeoff. Then prepurchased meals, followed by snack/drink sales. Crew very pleasant, smiling, call bells answered within seconds. Arrived Perth only 20 minutes late Cleared the airport within 20 minutes of landing. TransNusa do not serve alcohol on board. Overall very happy with TransNusa low cost carrier with a high level of service. Definitely recommend.

Purchased Bundle which included choice of seat, meal and additional 5kg baggage. 20 kg included in the fare. Check-in fast and easy Boarding commenced 1hour before departure. Welcomed with a smile. It was a full flight. Departed 15 minutes early Service began with complimentary bottle of water. Pre-purchased meals were next- meal was hot and included bottle of water and a dessert. Food was very good. Arrived Denpasar early new e-gates very easy and fast Bags arrived only a few minutes after clearing immigration Customs very quick through the airport and met our driver within 30 minutes Very happy with TransNusa Will fly them again.

I recently did a safari in the Republic of the Congo with my son, who is based in London. I bought our tickets on my Wells Fargo visa on the second of November. At the end of January, two days before departure, I was notified that my account had been hacked so my credit card was canceled and a new one issued. At the completion of our safari, three hours before departure from Brazzaville, my son received an email from Air France stating that his ticket had been canceled due to fraud on the account. We immediately departed the hotel where we had just paid for a day room, to go to the airport to explain to the agent that although there had indeed been recent fraud on the account, their ticket was paid for on the second of November, which I could demonstrate to them with my credit card statement on my phone. After an hour of arguing with the agent and her speaking with Paris, I was informed that my son could only fly if I bought him another ticket, at the inflated last minute price. Therefore, I was out his original ticket plus a 50% more expensive second ticket. Absurd. I was sure I could sort it out when back to the states. Wrong. I filed the claim as instructed and nothing happened. I have spoken to customer service multiple times which is difficult as you must search diligently to find a phone number, when you call it usually takes over thirty minutes to speak to someone, and when you do get an agent they are in the Phillipines with lots of background noise. You can never actually speak to anyone with authority, the agent you get just sends another message to the refund department and nothing happens. I have been a BA gold and silver member for many years, and their customer service looks impeccable by comparison. It has now been six weeks with no refund and no explanation. Needless to say, my first experience with Air France will be my last.

My experience with American Airlines on this trip was an absolute disaster from the moment we landed in Philadelphia. Our connecting flight to Reagan was cancelled less than an hour after we arrived, and that’s when the real chaos began. We waited in a long line at the customer service desk, only for the agents to close the counter right as we were about to be helped. No explanation, no apology—just a door slammed in the faces of passengers who had already been stranded. We were then forced to trek across the terminal to another service desk, where the situation somehow got worse. When we finally reached an agent, she made zero effort to rebook us. We were told there were no direct flights for two days, not to Reagan, not even back to our original destination in Salt Lake City. Everything was booked, and instead of offering solutions, the agent shrugged and told us that American “isn’t going to do anything” and that we’d be better off renting a car or taking Amtrak to Washington DC. That was the extent of their “assistance.” To make matters worse, I was promised a refund for the unused portion of our flight, which never happened. Not a penny. Not even a follow‑up. Then came baggage claim. When we arrived at the baggage office, the agent literally put up a sign saying he’d be back in 15 minutes. He returned an hour later, casually admitting it was his dinner break. No urgency, no concern for the dozens of passengers waiting on him, just a shrug and a “yeah, I was gone for a while.” This entire experience showed a complete lack of organization, accountability, and basic customer service. American Airlines left us stranded, uninformed, and unsupported at every step. I’ve never encountered an airline so unwilling to help its own passengers during a disruption it caused. I will go out of my way to avoid flying American again. No traveler deserves to be treated like this.

My first experience with Breeze. Flight supposed to leave 8:25pm. Still on the tarmac at 10:40pm. Excuses are maintenance issues, paperwork needs to be done and now waiting on a few passengers. I heard this airline was known for delays and cancellations but they do not do a good job of updating flight delays and you can’t talk to someone. The app wouldn’t work and no one responded to the messages. I will never fly Breeze again. Nothing about this experience has been a Breeze. Almost Midnight and still on the tarmac. Guess those last passengers are in another city.

I recently flew Business Class on BA95 from London to Montreal. Despite paying a premium price for a modern Business Class experience, I was provided with an ancient 2-4-2 "Ying-Yang" cabin layout. This configuration offers zero privacy, requires jumping over other passengers' legs, and is entirely inconsistent with the "Club Suite" product British Airways markets. To make matters worse, there was no WiFi connectivity for the duration of this international flight. When I raised these issues, British Airways  acknowledged the "inconvenience" but offered no compensation.

I strongly advise against booking with Cebu Pacific. My experience has been a complete odyssey. Out of four flights booked, two were cancelled and another one had an aircraft change at the last minute. This caused constant stress and ruined our travel logistics. Their lack of reliability and poor scheduling make them a very risky choice if you have a tight itinerary. Save yourself the trouble and book with a different airline.

What was supposed to be a simple 9-hour flight from Frankfurt to Chicago turned into a 3-day nightmare of incompetence, silence, and disrespect. We reached Chicago airspace… and then spent an hour circling with no explanation, no updates. Then the screens switch to Detroit. That’s how we find out we’re being diverted. When people finally asked, the answer? “Refueling.” Mid-flight diversion, and that’s the best you’ve got? We land in Detroit nearly 2 hours late and still no communication. Then we sit for three hours on the plane. Confusion everywhere, zero answers. Then as we’re deplaning—boom. Notification: flight canceled. Reason? Crew ran out of legal flying hours. So this disaster was predictable and completely mismanaged. We’re pushed through customs and then left waiting 2 hours for luggage because the airport apparently isn’t equipped to handle international arrivals.  Finally reach United customer service to be met with rudeness and indifference. No hotel. No assistance. No accountability. Just “come back in the morning.” So at 4AM, exhausted and stranded, most of us end up sleeping on the airport floor like we’re invisible. Morning comes. New day, same chaos. No gate info. No updates. Staff literally telling us to “walk around and figure it out.” Eventually we’re told to go to gate D9. So we wait. 11:45 passes—nothing. Then: “We’re waiting for pilots.” Hours go by. Pilots arrive. Then suddenly—new excuses. Missing crew. Missing parts.  At 6PM after another full day of this circus we finally board. And the luggage? We were told it was already on the plane. That was a lie too. Mid-flight, we’re informed it’ll arrive on a different aircraft—because they “didn’t have equipment” to load it earlier. We land in Chicago and the luggage plane hasn’t even left yet. Another 5-hour wait at O’Hare. I finally get my bag at 1AM Tuesday. So a “no-brainer” 9-hour flight that should’ve ended Sunday afternoon dragged into Tuesday morning—complete with lost hotel night, wasted car rental, zero compensation, and a complete lack of basic human decency. This wasn’t just bad service. This was systemic failure at every single step. Easily the worst travel experience I’ve ever had.

My wife and I were supposed to fly back to Madrid from Hong Kong directly on 6th March. Three hours before landing in Munich, the captain announced that due to a technical issue the flight’s destination would be changed and we would land in Munich instead. After landing, we expected that Cathay Pacific staff would be present to assist all passengers in rearranging their onward flights so that everyone could reach their respective final destinations smoothly. Unfortunately, after we collected our luggage at Munich Airport, there was no support available. There were no Cathay Pacific staff present to assist passengers. The only answer we received at the airport was that we should each check our email, and Cathay Pacific would send updated flight arrangements to everyone. When we received the email, the arrangement given to us was to fly from Munich to Lisbon eight hours later, and then from Lisbon to our final destination, Barcelona, with less than one hour of transit time in Lisbon. Cathay Pacific customer service did not offer us any direct flight options. We called Cathay Pacific customer service to request a more reasonable flight arrangement. Unfortunately, the customer service agent was unable to rebook us onto any direct flight that would allow us to return to our destination as soon as possible that same day. Instead, the only option available was a direct flight from Munich to Barcelona operated by a Spanish low-cost airline the following day. This means that our arrival time in Barcelona would be approximately twenty-four hours later than originally scheduled. During this period, none of the arrangements were provided by Cathay Pacific. We had to pay for and book a hotel near the airport ourselves to rest, and all meals, beverages, transfers were also paid for and arranged by ourselves at the hotel. We wrote to Cathay Pacific and it has been 3 weeks now we got no answer at all. A top airline is not only about inflight experience, it is about how the airline responds and provides assistance to passengers when problems arise. The arrangements made by Cathay Pacific were extremely disappointing and left us feeling very dissatisfied and frustrated. Very disappointed.

Flight on time, baggage delivered quickly, friendly staff, decent entertainment for a 16 hour flight. The only downside was the food, I took an economy flight with the same airline the day before and I enjoyed a much better meal. The rainbow macrons are awesome though.

Flew in business class from Hong Kong to Bangkok on the 20th March. The lounge at Hong kong airport was nowhere near to Emirates usual standard. The aircraft looked very dated indeed with sockets for the TV not working and neither were the USB sockets for charging our phones. The seats were extremely uncomfortable for a business class flight Food was average at best and service was also very slow. A passenger who spent most of the journey at the on-board bar was drunk when he returned to his seat. Even although the same passenger became rather loud and was also stood up in the aisle just after landing the crew did nothing about the passengers behaviour. This is not acceptable.

Flair Airlines actively tries to make their customers pay more in time and money than any other airline while providing a terrible service. I will never fly Flair again. amongst things like paying over $80 dollars for a carryon bag, and $100 dollars for a checked bag, we waited over 50 minutes just to complete a check in (that we had already done online to avoid paying $34 dollars in person). We made it through security faster than doing the check in.
Super nice. The seats are very comfortable, and the flight attendants are very nice too. The inflight entertainment had lots of movies to choose from

Icelandair is known for their nickel and dime policies to charge you more for each service. What they also do is to ask if you want to upgrade to their Saga Premium and allow you to place an offer that is/is not accepted 48 hours before departure. If you choose to do this, beware! They will send you upgrade solicitations to get you to pay twice as much. Do Not Open these emails! Since customer service for Icelandair is one of the worst in the airline business, do not expect to be able to resolve any issue with them. I literally waited 6 hours on hold before the trip and 3 hours trying to get to a chat (they just dropped the chat when they didn't want to address my issue).
We were impressed with the customer service from cabin crew. Our return tickets were good value and recommend this airline.

For both flights although checking in on-line 24 hours before flight time, my wife and I were unable to get seats beside each other. Bigger issue was WJ Cancun operation. Upon landing in Cancun, it took 40 minutes for the stairs to be rolled out to our plane. When we arrived in the terminal two previous WJ flights were waiting for bags. Passengers started to talk and said WJ baggage handlers were on some kind of work stoppage. There was no communication from on-site WJ staff and we were told it could take 2 - 4 hours for our bags to arrive. After waiting well over an hour, the previous flights bags arrived. Then some passengers noticed bags coming out on the next carousel, yet the TV screens were not updated no any communication. It turns out our flights bags came out on that carousel. Then the Nexus tour line to take a shuttle to our hotel was outlandishly long so we arranged a taxi. The return trip home ,although we got out bags tags from the kiosk, we had to wait in line over an hour to drop off the bags. Then the flight was an hour late leaving and little communication from the gate agents why and when the flight would leave. They did one announcement at he time the flight was scheduled to leave saying we could board in 15 minutes, but it was more like 30 minutes plus. Westjet Cancun operations is horrible.

Unfortunately there was a delay of about 45 minutes and there was also a delay in landing. Otherwise it was an enjoyable flight. Check in was easy and the staff were friendly. Only water, tea and coffee is free. Perhaps they can give customers the chance to pre purchase a meal as some airlines do. his would be particularly worthwhile for lunch or dinner.

Check in was easy and the flight left on time. The staff were very friendly and personable. Only tea, coffee and water are free which is no big deal on such a short flight. Overall a nice way to end my break.
